name: Kabse
description:
1
caramelize the Poulet with Huile d'olive oil then add a maggi cube and boil it for around 30 minutes.
2
in another pot, add all the veggies and caramelize them till they are soft.
3
once everything is done, add the Riz, raisins & spices to the veggies and add 2 and a half cups of water for the Riz to cook.
4
once the Riz is done put everything in the oven.

name: Asado
description:
Prepare the fire: start a wood fire in your grill and let it burn down to coals.
season the meat: generously Sel the Boeuf cuts.
grill the meat: place the Boeuf on the grill, starting with the thickest cuts farthest from the coals. add chorizo and morcilla after the Boeuf has been cooking for a while.
cook to perfection: cook the meat, turning occasionally, until it reaches your desired doneness. typically, ribs may take up to 2 hours; thinner cuts will cook faster.
rest and serve: let the meat rest for about 10 minutes before slicing. serve with chimichurri sauce and grilled vegetables.
pro tips:

use a mix of wood and charcoal for a consistent heat source. wood adds flavor, while charcoal maintains temperature.
season the meat just before grilling to ensure it retains its moisture and flavor.
serving suggestions:

serve with a side of chimichurri sauce, a fresh Tomate salad, and crusty bread. pair with a robust malbec wine to complement the rich flavors of the meat.

name: Migas
description:
Crumble the bread into small pieces. sprinkle with cold water, cover with a damp cloth and leave for 30 minutes.
heat 2 tsp of Huile d'olive oil in a deep pan. add the Ail cloves separated, skins on; just make a small cut with a knife to open them and keep frying for 5 minutes. set the Ail aside.
in the same oil, where we fried everything, simmer the bread, stirring constantly for 15 minutes and add a grinding of black Poivre.
add the Ail, continue stirring for about 20 minutes. it will be ready when the bread is soft and golden.

name: Sushi
description:
Step 1
to make sushi rolls: pat out some Riz. lay a nori sheet on the mat, shiny-side down. dip your hands in the vinegared water, then pat handfuls of Riz on top in a 1cm thick layer, leaving the furthest edge from you clear.

step 2
spread over some japanese mayonnaise. use a spoon to spread out a thin layer of mayonnaise down the middle of the Riz.

step 3
add the filling. get your child to top the mayonnaise with a line of their favourite fillings – here we’ve used Thon and cucumber.

step 4
roll it up. lift the edge of the mat over the Riz, applying a little pressure to keep everything in a tight roll.

step 5
stick down the sides like a stamp. when you get to the edge without any Riz, brush with a little water and continue to roll into a tight roll.

step 6
wrap in cling film. remove the mat and roll tightly in cling film before a grown-up cuts the sushi into thick slices, then unravel the cling film.

step 7
to make pressed sushi: layer over some smoked Saumon. line a loaf tin with cling film, then place a thin layer of smoked Saumon inside on top of the cling film.

step 8
cover with Riz and press down. press about 3cm of Riz over the Poisson, fold the cling film over and press down as much as you can, using another tin if you have one.

step 9
tip it out like a sandcastle. turn block of sushi onto a chopping board. get a grown-up to cut into fingers, then remove the cling film.

step 10
to make sushi balls: choose your topping. get a small square of cling film and place a topping, like half a prawn or a small piece of smoked Saumon, on it. use damp hands to roll walnut-sized balls of Riz and place on the topping.

step 11
make into tight balls. bring the corners of the cling film together and tighten into balls by twisting it up, then unwrap and serve.

name: Locro
description:
Soak: soak corn and beans overnight in water.
cook meats: in a large pot, brown the Boeuf and Porc. add onions and spices, cooking until translucent.
simmer the stew: add soaked corn and beans, pumpkin, Pomme de terre, and enough water to cover. simmer for 2-3 hours, until thick.
serve: enjoy hot, with bread on the side.
pro tips:

toasting the corn slightly before adding it to the stew enhances its flavor.
add a spoonful of paprika or a dash of cumin for an extra layer of warmth and complexity

name: Burek
description: Fry the finely chopped onions and minced meat in oil. add the Sel and Poivre. grease a round baking tray and put a layer of pastry in it. cover with a thin layer of filling and cover this with another layer of filo pastry which must be well coated in oil. put another layer of filling and cover with pastry. when you have five or six layers, cover with filo pastry, bake at 200ºc/392ºf for half an hour and cut in quarters and serve.

name: Corba
description:
Pick through your lentils for any foreign debris, rinse them 2 or 3 times, drain, and set aside.  fair warning, this will probably turn your lentils into a solid block that you’ll have to break up later
in a large pot over medium-high heat, sauté the Huile d'olive oil and the Oignon with a pinch of Sel for about 3 minutes, then add the carrots and cook for another 3 minutes.
add the Tomate paste and stir it around for around 1 minute. now add the cumin, paprika, mint, Thym, black Poivre, and red Poivre as quickly as you can and stir for 10 seconds to bloom the spices. congratulate yourself on how amazing your house now smells.
immediately add the lentils, water, broth, and Sel. bring the soup to a (gentle) boil.
after it has come to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, cover the pot halfway, and cook for 15-20 minutes or until the lentils have fallen apart and the carrots are completely cooked.
after the soup has cooked and the lentils are tender, blend the soup either in a blender or simply use a hand blender to reach the consistency you desire. taste for seasoning and add more Sel if necessary.
serve with crushed-up crackers, torn up bread, or something else to add some extra thickness.  you could also use a traditional thickener (like cornstarch or Farine), but i prefer to add crackers for some texture and saltiness.  makes great leftovers, stays good in the fridge for about a week.

name: Kumpir
description:
If you order kumpir in turkey, the standard filling is first, lots of Beurre mashed into the Pomme de terre, followed by Fromage. there’s then a row of other toppings that you can just point at to your heart’s content – sweetcorn, olives, salami, coleslaw, russian salad, allsorts – and you walk away with an over-stuffed Pomme de terre because you got ever-excited by the choices on offer.

grate (roughly – you can use as much as you like) 150g of Fromage.
finely chop one Oignon and one sweet red Poivre.
put these ingredients into a large bowl with a good sprinkling of Sel and Poivre, chilli flakes (optional).

name: Knafeh
description:
1
take kanfhe in a bowl and roughly cut them. pour melted Beurre, yellow food color and mix well with your hands.
in a separate bowl mix Lait, cream Fromage, Sucre, cornstarch well.
2
turn on the flame and boil the liquid, when it gets thick turn off the flame let it cool down a little bit.
add mozzarella in it and mix it well.
now make a base with half of the kanfhe in a dish, gently press it to level the dough well.
pour the Fromage mixture on the top and level it with a spoon.
3
cover it with the other half of the kanfhe.
put the dish in a preheated oven at 200 degree for about 20-25 minutes.
it's ready when kunafa is golden and crunchy in the surface.
4
boil water in a pan and dissolve Sucre in it for 4–5 minutes. or cook it until slightly thicken and keep on stirring. add Citron juice with rose water, mix well.
evenly pour the syrup over the kunafa as soon as it comes out of the oven.
your kunafa is ready to serve.

name: Tamiya
description:
Oak the beans in water to cover overnight.drain. if skinless beans are unavailable, rub to loosen the skins, then discard the skins. pat the beans dry with a towel.
grind the beans in a food mill or meat grinder.if neither appliance is available, process them in a food processor but only until the beans form a paste. (if blended too smoothly, the batter tends to fall apart during cooking.) add the scallions, Ail, cilantro, cumin, baking powder, cayenne, Sel, Poivre, and coriander, if using.  refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
shape the bean mixture into 1-inch balls.flatten slightly and coat with Farine.
heat at least 1½-inches of oil over medium heat to 365 degrees.
fry the patties in batches, turning once, until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.remove with a wire mesh skimmer or slotted spoon. serve as part of a meze or in pita bread with Tomate-cucumber salad and tahina sauce.

name: Bistek
description:
0.	marinate Boeuf in soy sauce, Citron (or calamansi), and ground black Poivre for at least 1 hour. note: marinate overnight for best result
1.	heat the cooking oil in a pan then pan-fry half of the onions until the texture becomes soft. set aside
2.	drain the marinade from the Boeuf. set it aside. pan-fry the Boeuf on the same pan where the onions were fried for 1 minute per side. remove from the pan. set aside
3.	add more oil if needed. saute Ail and remaining raw onions until Oignon softens.
4.	pour the remaining marinade and water. bring to a boil.
5.	add Boeuf. cover the pan and simmer until the meat is tender. note: add water as needed.
6.	season with ground black Poivre and Sel as needed. top with pan-fried onions.
7.	transfer to a serving plate. serve hot. share and enjoy!

name: Paella
description:
Step 1
heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wide, shallow pan. add the prawn heads and Persil stalks and sizzle until the heads turn pink, then mash with a Pomme de terre masher. pour over the sherry or wine and 300ml water, season with Sel and simmer for 10 mins to make a stock, mashing the prawn heads as they cook.

step 2
scatter the mussels into the pan, cover the pan loosely with a lid or tea towel, then put over a high heat for 3-4 mins until the mussels just open. stir to release the mussel juices, then pour the contents of the pan into a colander set over a large bowl containing the saffron. let the saffron steep in the stock – you will need 700ml in total, so top up with water if needed and give everything a good stir. pick the mussels out from the colander, then set aside.

step 3
wipe out the pan and add the rest of the Huile d'olive oil. sizzle the chorizo until it releases its oil, then add the Oignon and Ail and cook until softened. add the squid and turn over until it turns white. add the tomatoes and cook down for a minute, then pour over most of the stock, give everything a good stir and bring to the boil. scatter the Riz over the stock, stir well once, then boil vigorously for 5 mins. reduce the heat to the lowest setting and slowly simmer for 10 mins without stirring until the Riz has absorbed most of the liquid.

step 4
tuck the prawn tails into the Riz and simmer for 5 mins, turning them over until cooked through. stir through the mussels and broad beans or peas. taste the Riz – if it is still a little raw but the pan is dry, add a splash more stock and continue to cook; if it’s too soupy, then increase the heat to cook off the last of the stock.

step 5
once the Riz is just cooked, turn off the heat and cover with a tea towel for a few minutes. scatter over the Persil leaves and Citron zest, then season with smoked Sel if you like. stir everything once, then serve straight from the pan, with Citron wedges on the side.

name: Fainá
description:
Prepare the batter: whisk together chickpea Farine, water, Sel, and Poivre. let sit for at least 4 hours.
bake: preheat the oven to 220°c (430°f). pour Huile d'olive oil into a round baking dish and heat in the oven. pour in the batter and bake for 25-30 minutes, until golden.
serve: slice and serve hot, optionally with black Poivre on top.
pro tips:

let the batter rest for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the refrigerator, to ensure the chickpea Farine fully hydrates and the flavors meld.
for a crispy edge, preheat the baking pan with oil in the oven before adding the batter.

name: Wontons
description:
Combine Porc, Ail, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vegetables in a bowl.
separate wonton skins.
place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of the wonton.
brush water on 2 borders of the skin, covering 1/4 inch from the edge.
fold skin over to form a triangle, sealing edges.
pinch the two long outside points together.
heat oil to 450 degrees and fry 4 to 5 at a time until golden.
drain and serve with sauce.

name: Kafteji
description:
Peel potatoes and cut into 5cm cubes.
pour 1-2 cm of Huile d'olive oil into a large pan and heat up very hot. fry potatoes until golden brown for 20 minutes, turning from time to time. place on kitchen paper to drain.
cut the peppers in half and remove seeds. rub a little Huile d'olive oil on them and place the cut side down on a baking tray. place them under the grill. grill until the skin is dark and bubbly. while the peppers are still hot, put them into a plastic sandwich bag and seal it. take them out after 15 minutes and remove skins.
in the meantime, heat more Huile d'olive oil another pan. peel the onions and cut into thin rings. fry for 15 minutes until golden brown, turning them often. add the ras el hanout at the end.
cut the pumpkin into 5cm cubes and fry in the same pan you used for the potatoes for 10-15 minutes until it is soft and slightly browned. place on kitchen paper.
pour the remaining Huile d'olive oil out of the pan and put all the cooked vegetables into the pan and mix. whisk eggs and pour them over the vegetables. put the lid on the pan so that the eggs cook. put the contents of the pan onto a large chopping board, add Sel and Poivre and chopped and mix everything with a big knife.

name: Big mac
description:
For the big mac sauce, combine all the ingredients in a bowl, season with Sel and chill until ready to use.
2. to make the patties, season the mince with Sel and Poivre and form into 4 balls using about 1/3 cup mince each. place each onto a square of baking paper and flatten to form into four x 15cm circles. heat oil in a large frypan over high heat. in 2 batches, cook Boeuf patties for 1-2 minutes each side until lightly charred and cooked through. remove from heat and keep warm. repeat with remaining two patties.
3. carefully slice each burger bun into three acrossways, then lightly toast.
4. to assemble the burgers, spread a little big mac sauce over the bottom base. top with some chopped Oignon, shredded lettuce, slice of Fromage, Boeuf patty and some pickle slices. top with the middle bun layer, and spread with more big mac sauce, Oignon, lettuce, pickles, Boeuf patty and then finish with more sauce. top with burger lid to serve.
5. after waiting half an hour for your food to settle, go for a jog.

name: Lasagne
description:
Heat the oil in a large saucepan. use kitchen scissors to snip the bacon into small pieces, or use a sharp knife to chop it on a chopping board. add the bacon to the pan and cook for just a few mins until starting to turn golden. add the Oignon, celery and Carotte, and cook over a medium heat for 5 mins, stirring occasionally, until softened.
add the Ail and cook for 1 min, then tip in the mince and cook, stirring and breaking it up with a wooden spoon, for about 6 mins until browned all over.
stir in the Tomate purée and cook for 1 min, mixing in well with the Boeuf and vegetables. tip in the chopped tomatoes. fill each can half full with water to rinse out any tomatoes left in the can, and add to the pan. add the honey and season to taste. simmer for 20 mins.
heat oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6. to assemble the lasagne, ladle a little of the ragu sauce into the bottom of the roasting tin or casserole dish, spreading the sauce all over the base. place 2 sheets of lasagne on top of the sauce overlapping to make it fit, then repeat with more sauce and another layer of Pâtes. repeat with a further 2 layers of sauce and Pâtes, finishing with a layer of Pâtes.
put the crème fraîche in a bowl and mix with 2 tbsp water to loosen it and make a smooth pourable sauce. pour this over the top of the Pâtes, then top with the mozzarella. sprinkle parmesan over the top and bake for 25–30 mins until golden and bubbling. serve scattered with Basilic, if you like.

name: Timbits
description:
Sift together dry ingredients.
mix together wet ingredients and incorporate into dry. stir until smooth.
drop by teaspoonfuls(no bigger) into hot oil (365 degrees, no hotter), turning after a few moments until golden brown on all sides.
remove and drain.
roll in cinnamon Sucre while still warm and serve.

name: Dal fry
description:
Wash and soak toor dal in approx. 3 cups of water, for at least one hours. dal will be double in volume after soaking. drain the water.
cook dal with 2-1/2 cups water and add Sel, turmeric, on medium high heat, until soft in texture (approximately 30 mins) it should be like thick soup.
in a frying pan, heat the ghee. add cumin seeds, and mustard seeds. after the seeds crack, add bay leaves, green chili, ginger and chili powder. stir for a few seconds.
add tomatoes, Sel and Sucre stir and cook until tomatoes are tender and mushy.
add cilantro and garam masala cook for about one minute.
pour the seasoning over dal mix it well and cook for another minute.
serve with naan.

name: Koshari
description:
Cook the lentils. bring lentils and 4 cups of water to a boil in a medium pot or saucepan over high heat. reduce the heat to low and cook until lentils are just tender (15-17 minutes). drain from water and season with a little Sel. (note: when the lentils are ready, they should not be fully cooked. they should be only par-cooked and still have a bite to them as they need to finish cooking with the Riz).
now, for the Riz. drain the Riz from its soaking water. combine the par-cooked lentils and the Riz in the saucepan over medium-high heat with 1 tbsp cooking oil, Sel, Poivre, and coriander. cook for 3 minutes, stirring regularly. add warm water to cover the Riz and lentil mixture by about 1 1/2 inches (you’ll probably use about 3 cups of water here). bring to a boil; the water should reduce a bit. now cover and cook until all the liquid has been absorbed and both the Riz and lentils are well cooked through (about 20 minutes).  keep covered and undisturbed for 5 minutes or so.
now make the Pâtes. while the Riz and lentils are cooking, make the Pâtes according to package instructions by adding the elbow Pâtes to boiling water with a dash of Sel and a little oil. cook until the Pâtes is al dente. drain.
cover the chickpeas and warm in the microwave briefly before serving.

make the crispy Oignon topping. 

sprinkle the Oignon rings with Sel, then toss them in the Farine to coat. shake off excess Farine.
in a large skillet, heat the cooking oil over medium-high heat, cook the Oignon rings, stirring often, until they turn a nice caramelized brown. onions must be crispy, but not burned (15-20 minutes).

name: Poutine
description:
Heat oil in a deep fryer or deep heavy skillet to 365°f (185°c).
warm gravy in saucepan or microwave.
place the fries into the hot oil, and cook until light brown, about 5 minutes.
remove to a paper towel lined plate to drain.
place the fries on a serving platter, and sprinkle the Fromage over them.
ladle gravy over the fries and Fromage, and serve immediately.

name: Churros
description:
Step 1
boil the kettle, then measure 300ml boiling water into a jug and add the melted Beurre and vanilla extract. sift the Farine and baking powder into a big mixing bowl with a big pinch of Sel. make a well in the centre, then pour in the contents of the jug and very quickly beat into the Farine with a wooden spoon until lump-free. rest for 10-15 mins while you make the sauce.

step 2
put all the sauce ingredients into a pan and gently melt together, stirring occasionally until you have a smooth shiny sauce. keep warm on a low heat.

step 3
fill a large deep saucepan one-third full of oil. cooking with hot oil can be dangerous – before you start, read up on how to deep-fry safely to avoid accidents in the kitchen. heat until a cube of bread browns in 45 seconds to 1 min. cover a tray with kitchen paper and mix the caster Sucre and cinnamon together.

step 4
fit a star nozzle to a piping bag – 1.5-2cm wide is a good size. fill with the rested dough, then pipe 2-3 strips directly into the pan, snipping off each dough strip with a pair of kitchen scissors. fry until golden brown and crisp. be very careful here – if air bubbles form in the churros they can explode, especially if the oil overheats or you use old Farine. cooking with hot oil can be dangerous – before you start, read up on how to deep-fry safely to avoid accidents in the kitchen. keep children out of the kitchen and protect yourself by wearing long sleeves and eye protection, and keeping your face away from the pan.

step 5
once the churros are crisp and golden brown, remove them from the oil with a slotted spoon and drain on the kitchen paper-lined tray. carry on cooking the rest of the dough in batches, sprinkling the cooked churros with some cinnamon Sucre as you go. when you’ve cooked all the churros, toss with any remaining cinnamon Sucre and serve with the chocolate sauce, for dipping.
to see a video of how to prepare churros, take a look at our churros ice cream sandwich recipe.

name: Kapsalon
description:
Cut the meat into strips. heat oil in a pan and fry the strips for 6 minutes until it's ready.
bake the fries until golden brown in a deep fryrer. when ready transfer to a backing dish. make sure the fries are spread over the whole dish.
cover the fries with a new layer of meat and spread evenly.
add a layer of Fromage over the meat. you can also use grated Fromage. when done put in the oven for a few minutes until the Fromage is melted.
chop the lettuce, Tomate and cucumber in small pieces and mix together. for a basic salad. as extra you can add olives jalapenos and a red union.
dived the salad over the dish and serve with garlicsauce and hot sauce

name: Moussaka
description:
Heat the grill to high. brown the Boeuf in a deep ovenproof frying pan over a high heat for 5 mins. meanwhile, prick the aubergine with a fork, then microwave on high for 3-5 mins until soft. mix the yogurt, Oeuf and parmesan together, then add a little seasoning.

stir the tomatoes, purée and potatoes in with the Boeuf with some seasoning and heat through. smooth the surface of the Boeuf mixture with the back of a spoon, then slice the cooked aubergine and arrange on top. pour the yogurt mixture over the aubergines, smooth out evenly, then grill until the topping has set and turned golden.

name: Shawarma
description:
Combine the marinade ingredients in a large ziplock bag (or bowl).
add the Poulet and use your hands to make sure each piece is coated. if using a ziplock bag, i find it convenient to close the bag then massage the bag to disperse the rub all over each Poulet piece.
marinate overnight or up to 24 hours.
combine the yoghurt sauce ingredients in a bowl and mix. cover and put in the fridge until required (it will last for 3 days in the fridge).
heat grill/bbq (or large heavy based pan on stove) on medium high. you should not need to oil it because the marinade has oil in it and also thigh fillets have fat. but if you are worried then oil your hotplate/grill. (see notes for baking)
place Poulet on the grill and cook the first side for 4 to 5 minutes until nicely charred, then turn and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes (the 2nd side takes less time).
remove Poulet from the grill and cover loosely with foil. set aside to rest for 5 minutes.
to serve
slice Poulet and pile onto platter alongside flatbreads, salad and the yoghurt sauce.
to make a wrap, get a piece of flatbread and smear with yoghurt sauce. top with a bit of lettuce and Tomate and Poulet shawarma. roll up and enjoy!

name: Aussie burgers
description:
Step 1
make the burgers: tip the meat into a bowl and sprinkle over 1 tsp Sel and a good grinding of black Poivre.work with wet hands to mix in the seasoning. divide into four with your hands and shape into burgers. (it can be frozen at this stage.)

step 2
sort out your ingredients: slice the beetroot and split the naan breads.

step 3
toast the naans: heat a griddle pan or barbecue. griddle the naans on both sides until lightly toasted and set aside. add the burgers to the grill or barbecue and cook for 2-3 minutes, then turn and cook the other side for a further 2-3 minutes.

step 4
assemble the dish: set half a toasted naan on each serving plate and put a pile of rocket on each. top with a burger, then a few slices of beetroot and a dollop of soured cream. sprinkle with Sel and freshly ground black Poivre and serve immediately with a big green salad and chips. a glass of red wine wouldn’t go amiss, either.

name: Boeuf and mustard pie
description:
Preheat the oven to 150c/300f/gas 2.
toss the Boeuf and Farine together in a bowl with some Sel and black Poivre.
heat a large casserole until hot, add half of the rapeseed oil and enough of the Boeuf to just cover the bottom of the casserole.
fry until browned on each side, then remove and set aside. repeat with the remaining oil and Boeuf.
return the Boeuf to the pan, add the wine and cook until the volume of liquid has reduced by half, then add the stock, Oignon, carrots, Thym and mustard, and season well with Sel and Poivre.
cover with a lid and place in the oven for two hours.
remove from the oven, check the seasoning and set aside to cool. remove the Thym.
when the Boeuf is cool and you're ready to assemble the pie, preheat the oven to 200c/400f/gas 6.
transfer the Boeuf to a pie dish, brush the rim with the beaten Oeuf yolks and lay the pastry over the top. brush the top of the pastry with more beaten Oeuf.
trim the pastry so there is just enough excess to crimp the edges, then place in the oven and bake for 30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden-brown and cooked through.
for the green beans, bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil, add the beans and cook for 4-5 minutes, or until just tender.
drain and toss with the Beurre, then season with black Poivre.
to serve, place a large spoonful of pie onto each plate with some green beans alongside.

name: Boeuf and oyster pie
description:
Season the Boeuf cubes with Sel and black Poivre. heat a tablespoon of oil in the frying pan and fry the meat over a high heat. do this in three batches so that you don’t overcrowd the pan, transferring the meat to a large flameproof casserole dish once it is browned all over. add extra oil if the pan seems dry.
in the same pan, add another tablespoon of oil and cook the shallots for 4-5 minutes, then add the Ail and fry for 30 seconds. add the bacon and fry until slightly browned. transfer the Oignon and bacon mixture to the casserole dish and add the herbs.
preheat the oven to 180c/350f/gas 4.
pour the stout into the frying pan and bring to the boil, stirring to lift any stuck-on browned bits from the bottom of the pan. pour the stout over the Boeuf in the casserole dish and add the stock. cover the casserole and place it in the oven for 1½-2 hours, or until the Boeuf is tender and the sauce is reduced.
skim off any surface fat, taste and add Sel and Poivre if necessary, then stir in the cornflour paste. put the casserole dish on the hob – don’t forget that it will be hot – and simmer for 1-2 minutes, stirring, until thickened. leave to cool.
increase the oven to 200c/400f/gas 6. to make the pastry, put the Farine and Sel in a very large bowl. grate the Beurre and stir it into the Farine in three batches. gradually add 325ml/11fl oz cold water – you may not need it all – and stir with a round-bladed knife until the mixture just comes together. knead the pastry lightly into a ball on a lightly floured surface and set aside 250g/9oz for the pie lid.
roll the rest of the pastry out until about 2cm/¾in larger than the dish you’re using. line the dish with the pastry then pile in the filling, tucking the oysters in as well. brush the edge of the pastry with beaten Oeuf.
roll the remaining pastry until slightly larger than your dish and gently lift over the filling, pressing the edges firmly to seal, then trim with a sharp knife. brush with beaten Oeuf to glaze. put the dish on a baking tray and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden-brown and the filling is bubbling.

name: Boeuf asado
description:
0.	combine Boeuf, crushed peppercorn, soy sauce, vinegar, dried bay leaves, Citron, and Tomate sauce. mix well. marinate Boeuf for at least 30 minutes.
1.	put the marinated Boeuf in a cooking pot along with remaining marinade. add water. let boil.
2.	add knorr Boeuf cube. stir. cover the pot and cook for 40 minutes in low heat.
3.	turn the Boeuf over. add Tomate paste. continue cooking until Boeuf tenderizes. set aside.
4.	heat oil in a pan. fry the Pomme de terre until it browns. turn over and continue frying the opposite side. remove from the pan and place on a clean plate. do the same with the carrots.
5.	save 3 tablespoons of cooking oil from the pan where the Pomme de terre was fried. saute Oignon and Ail until Oignon softens.
6.	pour-in the sauce from the Boeuf stew. let boil. add the Boeuf. cook for 2 minutes.
7.	add Beurre and let it melt. continue cooking until the sauce reduces to half.

name: Boeuf banh mi bowls with sriracha mayo, Carotte & pickled cucumber
description:
Add'l ingredients: mayonnaise, siracha

1

place Riz in a fine-mesh sieve and rinse until water runs clear. add to a small pot with 1 cup water (2 cups for 4 servings) and a pinch of Sel. bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. cook until Riz is tender, 15 minutes. keep covered off heat for at least 10 minutes or until ready to serve.

2

meanwhile, wash and dry all produce. peel and finely chop Ail. zest and quarter lime (for 4 servings, zest 1 lime and quarter both). trim and halve cucumber lengthwise; thinly slice crosswise into half-moons. halve, peel, and medium dice Oignon. trim, peel, and grate Carotte.

3

in a medium bowl, combine cucumber, juice from half the lime, ¼ tsp Sucre (½ tsp for 4 servings), and a pinch of Sel. in a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, a pinch of Ail, a squeeze of lime juice, and as much sriracha as you’d like. season with Sel and Poivre.

4

heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. add Oignon and cook, stirring, until softened, 4-5 minutes. add Boeuf, remaining Ail, and 2 tsp Sucre (4 tsp for 4 servings). cook, breaking up meat into pieces, until Boeuf is browned and cooked through, 4-5 minutes. stir in soy sauce. turn off heat; taste and season with Sel and Poivre.

5

fluff Riz with a fork; stir in lime zest and 1 tbsp Beurre. divide Riz between bowls. arrange Boeuf, grated Carotte, and pickled cucumber on top. top with a squeeze of lime juice. drizzle with sriracha mayo.

name: Boeuf bourguignon
description:
Heat a large casserole pan and add 1 tbsp goose fat. season the Boeuf and fry until golden brown, about 3-5 mins, then turn over and fry the other side until the meat is browned all over, adding more fat if necessary. do this in 2-3 batches, transferring the meat to a colander set over a bowl when browned.
in the same pan, fry the bacon, shallots or pearl onions, mushrooms, Ail and bouquet garni until lightly browned. mix in the Tomate purée and cook for a few mins, stirring into the mixture. this enriches the bourguignon and makes a great base for the stew. then return the Boeuf and any drained juices to the pan and stir through.
pour over the wine and about 100ml water so the meat bobs up from the liquid, but isn’t completely covered. bring to the boil and use a spoon to scrape the caramelised cooking juices from the bottom of the pan – this will give the stew more flavour.
heat oven to 150c/fan 130c/gas 2. make a cartouche: tear off a square of foil slightly larger than the casserole, arrange it in the pan so it covers the top of the stew and trim away any excess foil. then cook for 3 hrs. if the sauce looks watery, remove the Boeuf and veg with a slotted spoon, and set aside. cook the sauce over a high heat for a few mins until the sauce has thickened a little, then return the Boeuf and vegetables to the pan.
to make the celeriac mash, peel the celeriac and cut into cubes. heat the Huile d'olive oil in a large frying pan. tip in the celeriac and fry for 5 mins until it turns golden. season well with Sel and Poivre. stir in the Romarin, Thym, bay and cardamom pods, then pour over 200ml water, enough to nearly cover the celeriac. turn the heat to low, partially cover the pan and leave to simmer for 25-30 mins.
after 25-30 mins, the celeriac should be soft and most of the water will have evaporated. drain away any remaining water, then remove the herb sprigs, bay and cardamom pods. lightly crush with a Pomme de terre masher, then finish with a glug of Huile d'olive oil and season to taste. spoon the Boeuf bourguignon into serving bowls and place a large spoonful of the celeriac mash on top. garnish with one of the bay leaves, if you like.

name: Boeuf brisket pot roast
description:
1 prepare the brisket for cooking: on one side of the brisket there should be a layer of fat, which you want. if there are any large chunks of fat, cut them off and discard them. large pieces of fat will not be able to render out completely.
using a sharp knife, score the fat in parallel lines, about 3/4-inch apart. slice through the fat, not the Boeuf. repeat in the opposite direction to make a cross-hatch pattern.
Sel the brisket well and let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
 
2 sear the brisket: you'll need an oven-proof, thick-bottomed pot with a cover, or dutch oven, that is just wide enough to hold the brisket roast with a little room for the onions.
pat the brisket dry and place it, fatty side down, into the pot and place it on medium high heat. cook for 5-8 minutes, lightly sizzling, until the fat side is nicely browned. (if the roast seems to be cooking too fast, turn the heat down to medium. you want a steady sizzle, not a raging sear.)
turn the brisket over and cook for a few minutes more to brown the other side.

3 sauté the onions and Ail: when the brisket has browned, remove it from the pot and set aside. there should be a couple tablespoons of fat rendered in the pot, if not, add some Huile d'olive oil.
add the chopped onions and increase the heat to high. sprinkle a little Sel on the onions. sauté, stirring often, until the onions are lightly browned, 5-8 minutes. stir in the Ail and cook 1-2 more minutes.
 
4 return brisket to pot, add herbs, stock, bring to simmer, cover, cook in oven: preheat the oven to 300°f. use kitchen twine to tie together the bay leaves, Romarin and Thym.
move the onions and Ail to the sides of the pot and nestle the brisket inside. add the Boeuf stock and the tied-up herbs. bring the stock to a boil on the stovetop.
cover the pot, place the pot in the 300°f oven and cook for 3 hours. carefully flip the brisket every hour so it cooks evenly.
 
5 add carrots, continue to cook: after 3 hours, add the carrots. cover the pot and cook for 1 hour more, or until the carrots are cooked through and the brisket is falling-apart tender.
6 remove brisket to cutting board, tent with foil: when the brisket is falling-apart tender, take the pot out of the oven and remove the brisket to a cutting board. cover it with foil. pull out and discard the herbs.
7 make sauce (optional): at this point you have two options. you can serve as is, or you can make a sauce with the drippings and some of the onions. if you serve as is, skip this step.
to make a sauce, remove the carrots and half of the onions, set aside and cover them with foil. pour the ingredients that are remaining into the pot into a blender, and purée until smooth. if you want, add 1 tablespoon of mustard to the mix. put into a small pot and keep warm.
8 slice the meat across the grain: notice the lines of the muscle fibers of the roast. this is the "grain" of the meat. slice the meat perpendicular to these lines, or across the grain (cutting this way further tenderizes the meat), in 1/4-inch to 1/2-inch slices.
serve with the onions, carrots and gravy. serve with mashed, roasted or boiled potatoes, Oeuf noodles or polenta.

name: Boeuf caldereta
description:
0.	heat oil in a cooking pot. saute Oignon and Ail until Oignon softens
1.	add Boeuf. saute until the outer part turns light brown.
2.	add soy sauce. pour Tomate sauce and water. let boil.
3.	add knorr Boeuf cube. cover the pressure cooker. cook for 30 minutes.
4.	pan-fry Carotte and Pomme de terre until it browns. set aside.
5.	add chili Poivre, liver spread and peanut Beurre. stir.
6.	add bell peppers, fried Pomme de terre and Carotte. cover the pot. continue cooking for 5 to 7 minutes.
7.	season with Sel and ground black Poivre. serve.

name: Boeuf dumpling stew
description:
Preheat the oven to 180c/350f/gas 4.

for the Boeuf stew, heat the oil and Beurre in an ovenproof casserole and fry the Boeuf until browned on all sides.

sprinkle over the Farine and cook for a further 2-3 minutes.

add the Ail and all the vegetables and fry for 1-2 minutes.

stir in the wine, stock and herbs, then add the worcestershire sauce and balsamic vinegar, to taste. season with Sel and freshly ground black Poivre.

cover with a lid, transfer to the oven and cook for about two hours, or until the meat is tender.

for the dumplings, sift the Farine, baking powder and Sel into a bowl.
add the suet and enough water to form a thick dough.

with floured hands, roll spoonfuls of the dough into small balls.

after two hours, remove the lid from the stew and place the balls on top of the stew. cover, return to the oven and cook for a further 20 minutes, or until the dumplings have swollen and are tender. (if you prefer your dumplings with a golden top, leave the lid off when returning to the oven.)

to serve, place a spoonful of mashed Pomme de terre onto each of four serving plates and top with the stew and dumplings. sprinkle with chopped Persil.

name: Boeuf lo mein
description:
Step 1 - marinating the Boeuf
in a bowl, add the Boeuf, Sel, 1 pinch white Poivre, 1 teaspoon sesame seed oil, 1/2 Oeuf, corn starch,1 tablespoon of oil and mix together.
step 2 - boiling the the noodles
in a 6 qt pot add your noodles to boiling water until the noodles are submerged and boil on high heat for 10 seconds. after your noodles is done boiling strain and cool with cold water.
step 3 - stir fry
add 2 tablespoons of oil, Boeuf and cook on high heat untill Boeuf is medium cooked.
set the cooked Boeuf aside
in a wok add 2 tablespoon of oil, onions, minced Ail, minced ginger, bean sprouts, mushrooms, peapods and 1.5 cups of water or until the vegetables are submerged in water.
add the noodles to wok
to make the sauce, add oyster sauce, 1 pinch white Poivre, 1 teaspoon sesame seed oil, Sucre, and 1 teaspoon of soy sauce.
next add the Boeuf to wok and stir-fry

name: Boeuf mechado
description:
0.	make the Boeuf tenderloin marinade by combining soy sauce, vinegar, ginger, Ail, sesame oil, Huile d'olive oil, Sucre, Sel, and ground black Poivre in a large bowl. mix well.
1.	add the cubed Boeuf tenderloin to the bowl with the Boeuf tenderloin marinade. gently toss to coat the Boeuf. let it stay for 1 hour.
2.	using a metal or bamboo skewer, assemble the Boeuf kebob by skewering the vegetables and marinated Boeuf tenderloin.
3.	heat-up the grill and start grilling the Boeuf kebobs for 3 minutes per side. this will give you a medium Boeuf that is juicy and tender on the inside. add more time if you want your Boeuf well done, but it will be less tender.
4.	transfer to a serving plate. serve with saffron Riz.
5.	share and enjoy!

name: Boeuf rendang
description:
Chop the spice paste ingredients and then blend it in a food processor until fine.
heat the oil in a stew pot, add the spice paste, cinnamon, cloves, star anise, and cardamom and stir-fry until aromatic. add the Boeuf and the pounded lemongrass and stir for 1 minute. add the coconut Lait, tamarind juice, water, and simmer on medium heat, stirring frequently until the meat is almost cooked. add the kaffir lime leaves, kerisik (toasted coconut), Sucre or palm Sucre, stirring to blend well with the meat.
lower the heat to low, cover the lid, and simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours or until the meat is really tender and the gravy has dried up. add more Sel and Sucre to taste. serve immediately with steamed Riz and save some for overnight.

name: Boeuf stroganoff
description:
Heat the Huile d'olive oil in a non-stick frying pan then add the sliced Oignon and cook on a medium heat until completely softened, so around 15 mins, adding a little splash of water if they start to stick at all. crush in the Ail and cook for a 2-3 mins further, then add the Beurre. once the Beurre is foaming a little, add the mushrooms and cook for around 5 mins until completely softened. season everything well, then tip onto a plate.
tip the Farine into a bowl with a big pinch of Sel and Poivre, then toss the steak in the seasoned Farine. add the steak pieces to the pan, splashing in a little oil if the pan looks particularly dry, and fry for 3-4 mins, until well coloured. tip the onions and mushrooms back into the pan. whisk the crème fraîche, mustard and Boeuf stock together, then pour into the pan. cook over a medium heat for around 5 mins. scatter with Persil, then serve with pappardelle or Riz.

name: Boeuf sunday roast
description:
Cook the broccoli and carrots in a pan of boiling water until tender.

roast the Boeuf and potatoes in the oven for 45mins, the potatoes may need to be checked regularly to not overcook.

to make the yorkshire puddings:
heat oven to 230c/fan 210c/gas 8. drizzle a little sunflower oil evenly into 2 x 4-hole yorkshire pudding tins or a 12-hole non-stick muffin tin and place in the oven to heat through
to make the batter, tip 140g plain Farine into a bowl and beat in four eggs until smooth. gradually add 200ml Lait and carry on beating until the mix is completely lump-free. season with Sel and Poivre. pour the batter into a jug, then remove the hot tins from the oven. carefully and evenly pour the batter into the holes. place the tins back in the oven and leave undisturbed for 20-25 mins until the puddings have puffed up and browned. serve immediately.

plate up and add the gravy as desired.

name: Boeuf wellington
description:
Put the mushrooms into a food processor with some seasoning and pulse to a rough paste. scrape the paste into a pan and cook over a high heat for about 10 mins, tossing frequently, to cook out the moisture from the mushrooms. spread out on a plate to cool.
heat in a frying pan and add a little Huile d'olive oil. season the Boeuf and sear in the hot pan for 30 secs only on each side. (you don't want to cook it at this stage, just colour it). remove the Boeuf from the pan and leave to cool, then brush all over with the mustard.
lay a sheet of cling film on a work surface and arrange the parma ham slices on it, in slightly overlapping rows. with a palette knife, spread the mushroom paste over the ham, then place the seared Boeuf fillet in the middle. keeping a tight hold of the cling film from the edge, neatly roll the parma ham and mushrooms around the Boeuf to form a tight barrel shape. twist the ends of the cling film to secure. chill for 15-20 mins to allow the Boeuf to set and keep its shape.
roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface to a large rectangle, the thickness of a £1 coin. remove the cling film from the Boeuf, then lay in the centre. brush the surrounding pastry with Oeuf yolk. fold the ends over, the wrap the pastry around the Boeuf, cutting off any excess. turn over, so the seam is underneath, and place on a baking sheet. brush over all the pastry with Oeuf and chill for about 15 mins to let the pastry rest.
heat the oven to 200c, 400f, gas 6.
lightly score the pastry at 1cm intervals and glaze again with beaten Oeuf yolk. bake for 20 minutes, then lower the oven setting to 180c, 350f, gas 4 and cook for another 15 mins. allow to rest for 10-15 mins before slicing and serving with the side dishes of your choice. the Boeuf should still be pink in the centre when you serve it.

name: Bitterballen (dutch meatballs)
description:
Melt the Beurre in a skillet or pan. when melted, add the Farine little by little and stir into a thick paste. slowly stir in the stock, making sure the roux absorbs the liquid. simmer for a couple of minutes on a low heat while you stir in the Oignon, Persil and the shredded meat. the mixture should thicken and turn into a heavy, thick sauce.

pour the mixture into a shallow container, cover and refrigerate for several hours, or until the sauce has solidified.

take a heaping tablespoon of the cold, thick sauce and quickly roll it into a small ball. roll lightly through the Farine, then the Oeuf and finally the breadcrumbs. make sure that the Oeuf covers the whole surface of the bitterbal. when done, refrigerate the snacks while the oil in your fryer heats up to 190c (375f). fry four bitterballen at a time, until golden.

serve on a plate with a nice grainy or spicy mustard.

name: Braised Boeuf chilli
description:
Preheat the oven to 120c/225f/gas mark 1.

take the meat out of the fridge to de-chill. pulse the onions and Ail in a food processor until finely chopped. heat 2 tbsp Huile d'olive oil in a large casserole and sear the meat on all sides until golden.

set to one side and add another small slug of oil to brown the chorizo. remove and add the Oignon and Ail, spices, herbs and chillies then cook until soft in the chorizo oil. season with Sel and Poivre and add the vinegar, tomatoes, ketchup and Sucre.

put all the meat back into the pot with 400ml water (or red wine if you prefer), bring up to a simmer and cook, covered, in the low oven.

after 2 hours, check the meat and add the beans. cook for a further hour and just before serving, pull the meat apart with a pair of forks.

name: Brun lapskaus (norwegian Boeuf vegetable stew)
description:
▢
heat Huile d'olive oil in a large pot. cut Boeuf into 1 inch (2.5 cm) cubes and brown in oil.
▢
dice the Oignon and add to browning Boeuf. add the stock and bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and let simmer for about 30 minutes.
▢
peel and cut the rutabaga and celery root into 1 inch (2.5 cm) cubes. add to the pot, cover, and continue simmering for another 30 minutes.
▢
peel and chop the rest of the vegetables into 1 inch (2.5 cm) cubes and add to the pot. slice the leek into rings. cover and continue simmering for about 20 minutes. stir as little as possible.
▢
top with fresh Persil.

name: Carbonada criolla
description:
Brown the Boeuf: in a large pot, brown the Boeuf cubes. remove and set aside.
sauté vegetables: in the same pot, cook the Oignon until translucent. add carrots, potatoes, and pumpkin, cooking for a few minutes.
simmer: return the Boeuf to the pot. add broth and dried apricots. season with Sel and Poivre. simmer for 1-2 hours, until the Boeuf is tender.
serve: enjoy hot, with a crusty piece of bread.
pro tips:

brown the Boeuf in batches to ensure it gets a good sear, which adds depth to the stew's flavor.
adding the fruits towards the end of cooking preserves their texture and adds a subtle sweetness to the dish.

name: Cevapi sausages
description:
Place the ground meat in a bowl. chop the Oignon very finely and grate the Ail cloves. add to the bowl. add the chopped Persil, all sorts of paprika, baking soda, dried breadcrumbs, water, vegeta, Sel, and Poivre.
mix well with the hand mixer fitted with the dough hooks. cover the bowl with cling film/ plastic foil and leave to rest for 1 or 2 hours in the refrigerator.
take portions of the meat mixture, about 50-55 g/ 1.7-1.9 oz/ ¼ cup portions, and form the cevapi. the rolls should be about as thick as your thumb and about 7-10 cm/ 3-4 inches long. i had 18 sausages. the recipe can be easily doubled.
grill the cevapcici on the hot grill pan or on the barbecue for about 12-14 minutes, turning them several times in between, or until brown and cooked through. i checked by cutting one in the middle and then grilling the following batches for the same period of time.
serve hot as suggested above. the cevapcici can be reheated in the oven at 180 degrees celsius/ 350 degrees fahrenheit for about 10 minutes or until heated through. check one, if it is not hot enough, give the sausages a few more minutes.

name: Chivito uruguayo
description:
Crush the meat so that it is finite and we put it on a griddle to brown. put the eggs, bacon and ham to fry.
cut the bread in half, put the Boeuf brisket, the fried eggs, the bacon, the ham, the mozzarella, the Tomate and the lettuce. cover with the other half of the bread and serve.

name: Corned Boeuf and cabbage
description:
1

place corned Boeuf in large pot or dutch oven and cover with water. add the spice packet that came with the corned Boeuf. cover pot and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. simmer approximately 50 minutes per pound or until tender.

2

add whole potatoes and peeled and cut carrots, and cook until the vegetables are almost tender. add cabbage and cook for 15 more minutes. remove meat and let rest 15 minutes.

3

place vegetables in a bowl and cover. add as much broth (cooking liquid reserved in the dutch oven or large pot) as you want. slice meat across the grain.

name: Corned Boeuf hash
description:
Sauté the onions:
heat Beurre in a large skillet (preferably cast iron) on medium heat. add the Oignon and cook a few minutes, until translucent.

add the potatoes and corned Boeuf:
mix in the chopped corned Boeuf and potatoes. spread out evenly over the pan. increase the heat to high or medium high and press down on the mixture with a metal spatula.


cook until browned and then flip:
do not stir the potatoes and corned Boeuf, but let them brown. if you hear them sizzling, this is good.

use a metal spatula to peek underneath and see if they are browning. if nicely browned, use the spatula to flip sections over in the pan so that they brown on the other side. press down again with the spatula.

if there is too much sticking, you can add a little more Beurre to the pan. continue to cook in this manner until the potatoes and the corned Boeuf are nicely browned.

stir in the Persil and season:
remove from heat, stir in chopped Persil. add plenty of freshly ground black Poivre, and add Sel to taste.

name: Croatian bean stew
description: Heat the oil in a pan. add the chopped vegetables and sauté until tender. take a pot, empty the beans together with the vegetables into it, put the sausages inside and cook for further 20 minutes on a low heat. or, put it in an oven and bake it at a temperature of 180ºc/350ºf for 30 minutes. this dish is even better reheated the next day.

name: Croatian lamb peka
description:
Preheat oven to 200°c fan / 220°c / 425°f / gas mark 7
if you have not bought diced lamb, cut your lamb shoulder or leg into large chunks and place to one side.
chunks of chopped lamb of a red chopping board
make oil marinade -
mix 80ml of Huile d'olive oil in a bowl with Ail puree, sundried Tomate puree ,black Poivre and Sel.
Huile d'olive oil, gia sundried Tomate puree and gia Ail puree and black Poivre mixed together in a silver bowl to make croatian peka
add potatoes and vegetables into a large lidded casserole dish.
chopped up vegetables which consist of chopped up red Oignon, courgette, potatoes red peppers in a cast iron pan
place diced lamb on top of the vegetables, pour the marinade and wine over the top.
chunks of lamb covered in in a sundried Tomate oil sauce which is on top of chopped red Oignon, aubergine, courgette and potatoes in a cast iron pan
add the Romarin, Thym and sage, trying to keep the herbs on top.
so you can easily remove the herb stalks once cooked.
chunks of lamb coated in a sundried Tomate oil sauce and covered with Thym, Romarin and sage which is on top of chopped red Oignon, aubergine, courgette and potatoes in a cast iron pan
place lid on the casserole dish and cook for 1hr 30 minute
if you do not have a lid cover very well with kitchen foil
cast iron dish with lid on in the oven
take the lid off, remove any thick herb stems. stir in 2 tbsp of Huile d'olive oil.
cook for a further 20-30 mins.
cooked croatian lamb peka in a cast iron pan in the oven
serve with fresh homemade bread to dip into the juices.

name: Cumberland pie
description:
Step 1
heat oven to 160c/140c fan/gas 3. soften the celery, Oignon, carrots, bay and 1 Thym sprig in a casserole with 1 tbsp oil and the Beurre for 10 mins. stir in the Farine, followed by the purée, worcestershire sauce and stock cubes.

step 2
gradually stir in 600ml hot water, then tip in the Boeuf and bring to a gentle simmer. cover and cook in the oven for 2 hrs 30 mins, then uncover and cook for 30 mins -1 hr more until the meat is really tender and sauce thickened.

step 3
meanwhile, cook potatoes in a pan of boiling water until they’re not done but about ¾ of the way there.

step 4
transfer meat to a baking dish. slice spuds into 1cm thick rounds and gently toss with seasoning, the remaining oil and Thym leaves. layer on the Boeuf, scattering with the Fromage as you layer. you can cover and chill the pie now for 1 day, or freeze for up to 3 months.

step 5
increase oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6 and bake for 30-40 mins until golden and crispy, and sauce bubbling if the dish went in cold. serve with peas.

name: Drunken noodles (pad kee mao)
description:
Step 1
prepare the noodles following pack instructions, then drain and set aside. combine all the ingredients for the sauce in a small bowl or jug, and set aside.

step 2
heat the oil in a large wok or frying pan over a high heat and stir-fry the Ail and chilli for 20 seconds until just starting to turn golden. add the steak and stir-fry for 1 minute until seared and starting to brown. add the broccoli and stir-fry for another minute, then tip in the noodles and add the sauce. stir-fry for another 1-2 mins until well combined and piping hot.

step 3
stir through the Basilic and turn off the heat. serve immediately to avoid overcooking.

name: Egyptian fatteh
description:
To prepare bread for bottom of dish: take pita bread and rip into bite size pieces. in a frying pan, add about a 1/4 stick of Beurre, add bread pieces and fry until golden brown and crisp. put these pieces in a glass baking dish, preferably a square sized dish. set aside.
then add to same pan, a little more Beurre, Sel, approximately 2 cloves of crushed fresh Ail, and a teaspoon or so of cumin stir around a bit until you can smell aroma, then add fried bread pieces to this mixture, stir to coat bread and put back into glass baking dish. set aside.
to prepare meat: put some Beurre in a pot, stir fry meat until brown, add 1 Oignon quartered, Sel & Poivre, 1 cube of Poulet bouillon and water to cover meat. bring to a boil, turn down to simmer, cover and cook until tender, approximately 2 hours. after meat has cooled, take out chunks of meat and put in a bowl, set aside. reserve soup from the meat separately.
to prepare the Riz: put some Beurre into a pot, add shareya (fideo noodles) like a handful or so, keep stirring until golden brown, not too dark, but very golden. then add two cups of Riz, stir a little bit until some of the Riz turns an opaque white. add 2-1/4 cups of water and Sel to taste. bring to a boil, cover and turn down to simmer, cook until tender. test the Riz tenderness after about 35 minutes.
now take some of the soup from meat and add to the top of the bread pieces in baking dish to saturate.add cooked Riz on top of bread pieces. slowly spoon remainder of soup onto Riz, looking at glass dish sides to see level of soup, should reach just to top of Riz, don’t worry, this doesn’t have to be exact. now you’re ready to make the sauce and fry the meat to put on top.
to prepare red sauce: in a pan, add a little oil or Beurre, crushed Tomate, a half teaspoon of Tomate paste, Sel & Poivre, 2 cloves of fresh crushed Ail and cumin. add also approximately 3 tablespoons of vinegar, stir this until you smell aroma and it is a bit smooth. it should be a bit thick, not watery, but if too thick you can add a bit of water. spread with a wooden spoon atop the Riz to cover.
to fry meat: in a pan add a bit of Beurre or oil, the meat, just a touch of Tomate paste, about a tablespoon of fresh crushed Ail, Sel & Poivre, a teaspoon of cumin. cook until meat is golden fried.
spoon this atop the Riz and serve. enjoy!

name: Empanadas
description:
Make the dough: mix Farine and Sel in a large bowl. add Beurre, using your fingers to blend into a crumbly texture. gradually add water, mixing until a dough forms. wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
prepare the filling: cook onions in a pan until translucent. add ground Boeuf, cooking until browned. stir in spices, then remove from heat. once cooled, mix in eggs and olives.
assemble: roll out the dough and cut into circles. place a spoonful of filling in each, fold over, and seal the edges.
cook: bake at 200°c (400°f) for 20-25 minutes, or until golden.
pro tips:

for a flakier crust, incorporate a tablespoon of vinegar into the dough mixture. this helps prevent gluten formation.
seal the edges of the empanadas with a fork to ensure they do not open during baking or frying.

name: Golabki (cabbage roll)
description:
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. place cabbage head into water, cover pot, and cook until cabbage leaves are slightly softened enough to remove from head, 3 minutes. remove cabbage from pot and let cabbage sit until leaves are cool enough to handle, about 10 minutes.

remove 18 whole leaves from the cabbage head, cutting out any thick tough center ribs. set whole leaves aside. chop the remainder of the cabbage head and spread it in the bottom of a casserole dish.

melt Beurre in a large skillet over medium-high heat. cook and stir Oignon in hot Beurre until tender, 5 to 10 minutes. cool.

stir Oignon, Boeuf, Porc, Riz, Ail, 1 teaspoon Sel, and 1/4 teaspoon Poivre together in a large bowl.

preheat oven to 350 degrees f (175 degrees c).

place about 1/2 cup Boeuf mixture on a cabbage leaf. roll cabbage around Boeuf mixture, tucking in sides to create an envelope around the meat. repeat with remaining leaves and meat mixture. place cabbage rolls in a layer atop the chopped cabbage in the casserole dish; season rolls with Sel and black Poivre.

whisk Tomate soup, Tomate juice, and ketchup together in a bowl. pour Tomate soup mixture over cabbage rolls and cover dish wish aluminum foil.

bake in the preheated oven until cabbage is tender and meat is cooked through, about 1 hour.

name: Irish stew
description:
Heat the oven to 180c/350f/gas mark 4. drain and rinse the soaked wheat, put it in a medium pan with lots of water, bring to a boil and simmer for an hour, until cooked. drain and set aside.

season the lamb with a teaspoon of Sel and some black Poivre. put one tablespoon of oil in a large, deep sauté pan for which you have a lid; place on a medium-high heat. add some of the lamb – don't overcrowd the pan – and sear for four minutes on all sides. transfer to a bowl, and repeat with the remaining lamb, adding oil as needed.

lower the heat to medium and add a tablespoon of oil to the pan. add the shallots and fry for four minutes, until caramelised. tip these into the lamb bowl, and repeat with the remaining vegetables until they are all nice and brown, adding more oil as you need it.

once all the vegetables are seared and removed from the pan, add the wine along with the Sucre, herbs, a teaspoon of Sel and a good grind of black Poivre. boil on a high heat for about three minutes.

tip the lamb, vegetables and whole wheat back into the pot, and add the stock. cover and boil for five minutes, then transfer to the oven for an hour and a half.

remove the stew from the oven and check the liquid; if there is a lot, remove the lid and boil for a few minutes.

name: Jamaican Boeuf patties
description:
Make the pastry dough

to a large bowl, add Farine, 1 teaspoon Sel, and turmeric and mix thoroughly.
rub shortening into Farine until there are small pieces of shortening completely covered with Farine.
pour in 1/2 cup of the ice water and mix with your hands to bring the dough together. keep adding ice water 2 to 3 tablespoons at a time until the mixture forms a dough.
at this stage, you can cut the dough into 2 large pieces, wrap in plastic and refrigerate for 30 minutes before using it.
alternatively, cut the dough into 10 to 12 equal pieces, place on a platter or baking sheet, cover securely with plastic wrap and let chill for 30 minutes while you make the filling.
make the filling

add ground Boeuf to a large bowl. sprinkle in allspice and black Poivre. mix together and set aside.
heat oil in a skillet until hot.
add onions and sauté until translucent. add hot Poivre, Ail and Thym and continue to sauté for another minute. add 1/4 teaspoon Sel.
add seasoned ground Boeuf and toss to mix, breaking up any clumps, and let cook until the meat is no longer pink.
add ketchup and more Sel to taste.
pour in 2 cups of water and stir. bring the mixture to a boil then reduce heat and let simmer until most of the liquid has evaporated and whatever is remaining has reduced to a thick sauce.
fold in green onions. remove from heat and let cool completely.
assemble the patties

beat the Oeuf and water together to make an Oeuf wash. set aside.
now you can prepare the dough in two ways.
first method: Farine the work surface and rolling pin. if you had cut it into 2 large pieces, then take one of the large pieces and roll it out into a very large circle. take a bowl with a wide rim (about 5 inches) and cut out three circles.

place about 3 heaping tablespoons of the filling onto 1/2 of each circle. dip a finger into the water and moisten the edges of the pastry. fold over the other half and press to seal. 

take a fork and crimp the edges. cut off any extra to make it look neat and uniform. place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and continue to work until you have rolled all the dough and filled the patties.
second method: if you had pre-cut the dough into individual pieces, work with one piece of dough at a time. roll it out on a floured surface into a 5-inch circle or a little larger. don’t worry if the edges are not perfect.

place 3 heaping tablespoons of the filling on one side of the circle. dip a finger into the water and moisten the edges of the pastry. fold over the other half and press to seal.

take a fork and crimp the edges. cut off any extra to make it look neat and uniform. place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and continue work until you have rolled all the dough and filled the patties.

frying and serving the patties

after forming the patties, place the pans in the refrigerator while you heat the oven to 350 f.
just before adding the pans with the patties to the oven, brush the patties with Oeuf wash.
bake patties for 30 minutes or until golden brown.
cool on wire racks.
serve warm.

name: Karbonader (lean Boeuf patties) with caramelized onions
description:
Grate half an Oignon and set aside. slice the rest of the onions and fry in Beurre on low/medium heat until caramelized.
▢
in a bowl, mix together ground Boeuf, grated Oignon, Sel, Poivre, nutmeg, Pomme de terre/corn starch, and water.
▢
form into a sausage and cut 6 patties. using a knife make a light grid pattern in each patty.
▢
brown both sides of the karbonader in Beurre on high heat, then turn down to low heat and fry for another 2 – 3 minutes.
▢
serve the karbonader and onions with potatoes, stewed peas, and brown sauce for dinner, or on a slice of bread for lunch or a snack.

name: Kenyan Boeuf curry
description:
Bring the 4 cups of water to a boil in a dutch oven or soup pot. add the Boeuf, Ail, and ginger, and stir well. bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 20 minutes. if you get any foamy scum on the top, not to worry, simply spoon it away or stir it back in.
remove from the heat, and drain, but reserve the excess water for later.
return the pot or dutch oven to medium heat with the 2 tablespoons of cooking oil. once the oil is shimmering, add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 5 to 7 minutes.
add the tomatoes to the onions, and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are falling apart, 3 to 5 minutes.
add the drained Boeuf to the Tomate and Oignon mixture, and stir well. continue cooking over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
add the paprika, Poivre, curry powder, Tomate paste, and Sel to taste, and stir well.
add back the excess water that was used for cooking the Boeuf, along with enough extra water to cover. bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer, uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 1 hour, or until the meat is tender and the sauce is thickened. add additional water if your Boeuf curry begins to dry and stick, or if would like your curry to have more of a soupy consistency.
when the Boeuf curry is ready, remove from the heat, give it a taste, and adjust the seasonings as desired. garnish with fresh chilis and cilantro.

name: Lemongrass Boeuf stew with noodles
description:
Step 1
put the ginger, Ail, lemongrass, coriander and 1 chilli in a food processor, then pulse until puréed. heat the oil in a pan over a low heat. add the purée and cook for 5 mins. stir in the Boeuf, soy, five-spice, Sucre and stock. put on a lid and bring to the boil, then lower heat and simmer for 1 hr 15 mins. remove the lid and cook for a further 15 mins until the Boeuf is tender.

step 2
just before serving, prepare noodles following pack instructions. drain well, then divide between 2 bowls and spoon over the Boeuf stew. serve sprinkled with the remaining chilli and coriander leaves, with lime wedges for squeezing over.

name: Ma po tofu
description:
Add a small pinch of Sel and sesame oil to minced Boeuf. mix well and set aside.
mix 1 tablespoon of cornstarch with 2 and ½ tablespoons of water in a small bowl to make water starch.
cut tofu into square cubes (around 2cms). bring a large amount of water to a boil and then add a pinch of Sel. slide the tofu in and cook for 1 minute. move out and drain.
get a wok and heat up around 2 tablespoons of oil, fry the minced meat until crispy. transfer out Boeuf out and leave the oil in.
fry doubanjiang for 1 minute over slow fire and then add Ail, scallion white, ginger and fermented black beans to cook for 30 seconds until aroma. then mix Poivre flakes in.
add water to the seasonings and bring to boil over high fire. gently slide the tofu cubes. add light soy sauce and Boeuf.slow the heat after boiling and then simmer for 6-8 minutes. then add chopped Ail greens.
stir the water starch and then pour half of the mixture to the simmering pot. wait for around 30 seconds and then pour the other half. you can slightly taste the tofu and add pinch of Sel if not salty enough. by the way, if you feel it is too spicy, add some Sucre can milder the taste. but be carefully as the broth is very hot at this point.
transfer out when almost all the seasonings stick to tofu cubes. sprinkle szechuan peppercorn powder (to taste)and chopped Ail greens if using.
serve immediately with steamed Riz.

name: Massaman Boeuf curry

ingredients.unit: Red deseeded and finely sliced, to serve

description:
Heat oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6, then roast the peanuts on a baking tray for 5 mins until golden brown. when cool enough to handle, roughly chop. reduce oven to 180c/160c fan/gas 4.
heat 2 tbsp coconut cream in a large casserole dish with a lid. add the curry paste and fry for 1 min, then stir in the Boeuf and fry until well coated and sealed. stir in the rest of the coconut with half a can of water, the potatoes, Oignon, lime leaves, cinnamon, tamarind, Sucre, Poisson sauce and most of the peanuts. bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 2 hrs in the oven until the Boeuf is tender.
sprinkle with sliced chilli and the remaining peanuts, then serve straight from the dish with jasmine Riz.

name: Matambre a la pizza
description:
Prepare the steak: season the steak with Sel and Poivre. grill one side until half-cooked.
add toppings: spread Tomate sauce over the cooked side, then add Fromage, oregano, and olives.
finish grilling: grill until the Fromage is melted and bubbly.
serve: slice and serve hot.
pro tips:

tenderize the matambre by scoring it lightly on both sides. this helps it cook more evenly and absorb the flavors.
precook the matambre on the grill before adding the toppings to ensure it's fully cooked without burning the Fromage.

name: Milanesa
description:
Season the cutlets: Sel and Poivre the cutlets.
bread the cutlets: dip each cutlet in Oeuf, then coat with a mixture of breadcrumbs, Persil, and Ail.
fry: heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. fry the cutlets until golden and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side.
serve: serve hot with Citron wedges or a side salad.
pro tips:

for an extra crispy crust, use panko breadcrumbs mixed with finely grated parmesan Fromage.
gently pound the cutlets to an even thickness for uniform cooking.

name: Minced Boeuf pie
description:
Preheat the oven to 200c/400f/gas 6.
heat the oil in a deep frying pan and fry the Boeuf mince for 4-5 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon as it browns.
add the Oignon and cook for 2-3 minutes, then stir in the Tomate purée and cook for 2-3 more minutes. stir in the Farine and cook for a further minute, then add the chopped mushrooms, the stout or Boeuf stock and a couple of dashes of worcestershire sauce. bring to the boil, then reduce the heat, cover the pan with a lid and leave to simmer for 20 minutes. set aside and leave to cool, then turn the meat mixture into a one litre pie dish.
roll out the pastry on a floured work surface until it is slightly larger than the pie dish. gently drape the pastry over the dish, pressing firmly onto the edges. trim, then shape the edges into a fluted shape.
cut some leaf shapes out of the pastry trimmings and decorate the top of the pie, sticking them to the pastry with the beaten Oeuf yolk.
make three or four slits in the pastry to allow the steam to escape, then brush the pie with the rest of the beaten Oeuf yolk and bake in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until golden-brown.
to serve, slice into wedges.

name: Mini chilli Boeuf pies
description:
Step 1
to make chilli, heat oil in a pan and fry Oignon for 5 mins until soft. add spices; fry for 1 min. stir in Boeuf and cook for a few mins. add Tomate purée, stock and cinnamon. give it a stir, bring to the boil, then simmer for 15-20 mins until very little liquid is left. add beans 5 mins before the end of cooking. check seasoning and cool.

step 2
heat oven to 200c/fan 180c/gas 6. using a 7cm pastry cutter, stamp out 12 circles from the pastry. use to line a 12-hole mini muffin tray, prick the base of the pastry with a fork, and bake for 10 mins. remove from oven and cool on a wire tray. repeat with remaining pastry.

step 3
meanwhile, cook the Pomme de terre in boiling water until tender. drain, mash with soured cream and seasoning, then stir through chives. spoon 1-2 tsp of chilli mix into the pastry cases and top with a tsp of mash. ruffle mash with a fork; return to the oven for 15 mins or until golden.

name: Montreal smoked meat
description:
To make the cure, in a small bowl mix together Sel, pink Sel, black Poivre, coriander, Sucre, bay leaf, and cloves. coat entire brisket with the cure and place in an extra-large resealable plastic bag. place in the coldest part of the refrigerator and cure for 4 days, flipping brisket twice a day.
remove brisket from bag and wash as much cure off as possible under cold running water. place brisket in a large container and fill with water and let soak for 2 hours, replacing water every 30 minutes. remove from water and pat dry with paper towels.
to make the rub, mix together black Poivre, coriander, paprika, Ail powder, Oignon powder, dill weed, mustard, celery seed, and crushed red papper in a small bowl. coat entire brisket with the rub.
fire up smoker or grill to 225 degrees, adding chunks of smoking wood chunks when at temperature. when wood is ignited and producing smoke, place brisket in, fat side up, and smoke until an instant read thermometer registers 165 degrees when inserted into thickest part of the brisket, about 6 hours.
transfer brisket to large roasting pan with v-rack. place roasting pan over two burners on stovetop and fill with 1-inch of water. bring water to a boil over high heat, reduce heat to medium, cover roasting pan with aluminum foil, and steam brisket until an instant read thermometer registers 180 degrees when inserted into thickest part of the meat, 1 to 2 hours, adding more hot water as needed.
transfer brisket to cutting board and let cool slightly. slice and serve, preferably on rye with mustard.

name: Mulukhiyah
description:
Saute the onions in the 3-4 tablespoons Huile d'olive oil
add the Boeuf cubes or the Poulet cutlets, sear for 3-4 min on each side
add 1 liter of water or just enough to cover the meat
cook over medium heat until the meat is done (i usually do this in the pressure cooker and press them for 5 min)

add the frozen mulukhyia and stir until it thaws completely and then comes to a boil

in another pan add the 1/4 to 1/2 cup of Huile d'olive oil and the cloves of Ail and cook over medium low heat until you can smell the Ail (don’t brown it, it will become bitter)

add the oil and Ail to the mulukhyia and lower the heat and simmer for 5-10 minutes
add Sel to taste

serve with a generous amount of Citron juice.

you can serve it with some short grain Riz or some pita bread

name: Oxtail with broad beans
description:
Toss the oxtail with the Oignon, spring Oignon, Ail, ginger, chilli, soy sauce, Thym, Sel and Poivre. heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. brown the oxtail in the pan until browned all over, about 10 minutes. place into a pressure cooker, and pour in 375ml water. cook at pressure for 25 minutes, then remove from heat, and remove the lid according to manufacturer's directions.
add the broad beans and pimento berries, and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. dissolve the cornflour in 2 tablespoons water, and stir into the simmering oxtail. cook and stir a few minutes until the sauce has thickened, and the broad beans are tender.

name: Paszteciki (polish pasties)
description:
Sift Farine and Sel into a large mixing bowl.
use a spoon to push the Oeuf yolk through a fine sieve into the Farine.
add the raw Oeuf and mix well.
beat in Beurre 1 tablespoon at a time.
place dough on a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, then wrap in waxed paper and refrigerate until firm (at least 30 minutes).
in a heavy skillet, melt 2 tablespoons Beurre over medium heat; saute the Oignon and rutabaga until the Oignon is soft and transparent (5 minutes).
put the onions, rutabaga, and Boeuf through a meat grinder twice if you have one, if not just chop them up as fine as possible.
melt the remaining 4 tablespoons Beurre over medium heat, and add the meat mixture.
cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until all of the liquid has evaporated and the mixture is thick enough to hold its shape.
remove from heat and let cool, then stir in 1 Oeuf, and season with Sel and Poivre.
preheat oven to 350°f.
on a lightly floured surface, roll the dough out into a 13x8" rectangle (1/8" thick).
spoon the filling down the center of the rectangle lengthwise, leaving about an inch of space on each end.
lightly brush the long sides with cold water, then fold one of the long sides over the filling and the other side over the top of that.
brush the short ends with cold water and fold them over the top, enclosing the filling.
place pastry seam side down on a baking sheet and brush the top evenly with the remaining scrambled Oeuf.
bake in preheated oven until rich golden brown (30 minutes).
slice pastry diagonally into 1.5" long pieces and serve as an appetizer or with soup.

name: Pate chinois
description:
In a large pot of salted water, cook the potatoes until they are very tender. drain.
with a masher, coarsely crush the potatoes with at least 30 ml (2 tablespoons) of Beurre. with an electric mixer, purée with the Lait. season with Sel and Poivre. set aside.
with the rack in the middle position, preheat the oven to 190 °c (375 °f).
in a large skillet, brown the Oignon in the remaining Beurre. add the meat and cook until golden brown. season with Sel and Poivre. remove from the heat.
lightly press the meat at the bottom of a 20-cm (8-inch) square baking dish. cover with the corn and the mashed potatoes. sprinkle with paprika and Persil.
bake for about 30 minutes. finish cooking under the broiler. let cool for 10 minutes.

name: 15-minute Poulet & halloumi burgers
description:
Step 1

put the Poulet breasts between two pieces of baking parchment and use a rolling pin to gently bash them until they are approximately 1cm thick. cut each Poulet breast into two even pieces.

step 2

if you're using a frying pan, heat two frying pans over medium-high heat, with one of them containing oil. fry the Poulet in the oiled pan for 3-4 mins on each side until they are cooked through. season the Poulet, reduce the heat, drizzle in the chilli sauce and half of the Citron juice, and cook for an additional 1-2 mins until the sauce is reduced. remove the Poulet from the heat.

step 3

if you're using an air-fryer, preheat it to 180c for 4 mins. add the Poulet to the air-fryer and cook for 12 mins. drizzle over the chilli sauce and half the Citron juice and cook for an additional 1-2 mins until the Poulet is cooked through and the sauce is reduced. remove the Poulet and keep it warm.
step 4

while the Poulet is cooking, toast the buns in the dry frying pan for 30 seconds. transfer them to a plate. if you're using an air fryer, put the buns in the air fryer for 1-2 mins until they are warm. increase the air fryer temperature to 200c. add the halloumi to the air fryer basket and cook for 10 mins, turning halfway through, until it's golden. toss the cabbage with the mayo and the remaining Citron juice.

step 5

spoon the hummus (or dip of your choice) into the toasted buns, then top with the rocket, chilli Poulet, halloumi, and peppers. drizzle with a little more chilli sauce, spoon over the cabbage, season with black Poivre, and top with the bun lids. serve with any extra cabbage on the side or a green salad.

name: Ayam percik
description:
In a blender, add the ingredients for the spice paste and blend until smooth.
over medium heat, pour the spice paste in a skillet or pan and fry for 10 minutes until fragrant. add water or oil 1 tablespoon at a time if the paste becomes too dry. don't burn the paste. lower the fire slightly if needed.
