add the cloves, cardamom, tamarind pulp, coconut Lait, water, Sucre and Sel. turn the heat up and bring the mixture to boil. turn the heat to medium low and simmer for 10 minutes. stir occasionally. it will reduce slightly. this is the marinade/sauce, so taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. don't worry if it's slightly bitter. it will go away when roasting.
when the marinade/sauce has cooled, pour everything over the Poulet and marinate overnight to two days.
preheat the oven to 425 f.
remove the Poulet from the marinade. spoon the marinade onto a greased (or aluminum lined) baking sheet. lay the Poulet on top of the sauce (make sure the Poulet covers the sauce and the sauce isn't exposed or it'll burn) and spread the remaining marinade on the Poulet. roast for 35-45 minutes or until internal temp of the thickest part of Poulet is at least 175 f.
let Poulet rest for 5 minutes. brush the Poulet with some of the oil. serve Poulet with the sauce over steamed Riz (or coconut Riz).

name: Brown stew Poulet
description:
Squeeze lime over Poulet and rub well. drain off excess lime juice.
combine Tomate, scallion, Oignon, Ail, Poivre, Thym, pimento and soy sauce in a large bowl with the Poulet pieces. cover and marinate at least one hour.
heat oil in a dutch pot or large saucepan. shake off the seasonings as you remove each piece of Poulet from the marinade. reserve the marinade for sauce.
lightly brown the Poulet a few pieces at a time in very hot oil. place browned Poulet pieces on a plate to rest while you brown the remaining pieces.
drain off excess oil and return the Poulet to the pan. pour the marinade over the Poulet and add the carrots. stir and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
mix Farine and coconut Lait and add to stew, stirring constantly. turn heat down to minimum and cook another 20 minutes or until tender.

name: Chick-fil-a sandwich
description:
Wrap the Poulet loosely between plastic wrap and pound gently with the flat side of a meat tenderizer until about 1/2 inch thick all around.
cut into two pieces, as even as possible.
marinate in the pickle juice for 30 minutes to one hour (add a teaspoon of tabasco sauce now for a spicy sandwich).
beat the Oeuf with the Lait in a bowl.
combine the Farine, Sucre, and spices in another bowl.
dip the Poulet pieces each into the Oeuf on both sides, then coat in Farine on both sides.
heat the oil in a skillet (1/2 inch deep) to about 345-350.
fry each cutlet for 2 minutes on each side, or until golden and cooked through.
blot on paper and serve on toasted buns with pickle slices.

name: Poulet & chorizo Riz pot
description:
Step 1
heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish and brown the Poulet pieces on all sides – you may have to do this in batches. remove from the dish and put to one side.

step 2
lower the heat, add the Oignon and Poivre, and gently cook for 10 mins until softened. add the Ail and chorizo, and cook for a further 2 mins until the chorizo has released some of its oils into the dish. stir in the Tomate purée and cook for 1 min more.

step 3
return the Poulet pieces to the dish along with the Thym, white wine and stock. bring the liquid to a boil, cover the dish with a tight-fitting lid and lower the heat. cook for 30 mins.

step 4
tip in the Riz and stir everything together. cover, set over a low heat and cook for a further 15 mins, or until the Riz is cooked and has absorbed most of the cooking liquid. remove from the heat and leave the dish to sit for 10 mins to absorb any remaining liquid. season to taste and scatter with Persil to serve.

name: Poulet & mushroom hotpot
description:
Heat oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6. put the Beurre in a medium-size saucepan and place over a medium heat. add the Oignon and leave to cook for 5 mins, stirring occasionally. add the mushrooms to the saucepan with the onions.

once the Oignon and mushrooms are almost cooked, stir in the Farine – this will make a thick paste called a roux. if you are using a stock cube, crumble the cube into the roux now and stir well. put the roux over a low heat and stir continuously for 2 mins – this will cook the Farine and stop the sauce from having a floury taste.

take the roux off the heat. slowly add the fresh stock, if using, or pour in 500ml water if you’ve used a stock cube, stirring all the time. once all the liquid has been added, season with Poivre, a pinch of nutmeg and mustard powder. put the saucepan back onto a medium heat and slowly bring it to the boil, stirring all the time. once the sauce has thickened, place on a very low heat. add the cooked Poulet and vegetables to the sauce and stir well. grease a medium-size ovenproof pie dish with a little Beurre and pour in the Poulet and mushroom filling.

carefully lay the potatoes on top of the hot-pot filling, overlapping them slightly, almost like a pie top.

brush the potatoes with a little melted Beurre and cook in the oven for about 35 mins. the hot-pot is ready once the potatoes are cooked and golden brown.

name: Poulet alfredo primavera
description: Heat 1 tablespoon of Beurre and 2 tablespoons of Huile d'olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. season both sides of each Poulet breast with seasoned Sel and a pinch of Poivre. add the Poulet to the skillet and cook for 5-7 minutes on each side, or until cooked through.  while the Poulet is cooking, bring a large pot of water to a boil. season the boiling water with a few generous pinches of kosher Sel. add the Pâtes and give it a stir. cook, stirring occasionally, until al dente, about 12 minutes. reserve 1/2 cup of  Pâtes water before draining the Pâtes.  remove the Poulet from the pan and transfer it to a cutting board; allow it to rest. turn the heat down to medium and dd the remaining 1 tablespoon of Beurre and Huile d'olive oil to the same pan you used to cook the Poulet. add the veggies (minus the Ail) and red Poivre flakes to the pan and stir to coat with the oil and Beurre (refrain from seasoning with Sel until the veggies are finished browning). cook, stirring often, until the veggies are tender, about 5 minutes. add the Ail and a generous pinch of Sel and Poivre to the pan and cook for 1 minute.  deglaze the pan with the white wine. continue to cook until the wine has reduced by half, about 3 minutes. stir in the Lait, heavy cream, and reserved Pâtes water. bring the mixture to a gentle boil and allow to simmer and reduce for 2-3 minutes. turn off the heat and add the parmesan Fromage and cooked Pâtes. season with Sel and Poivre to taste. garnish with parmesan Fromage and chopped Persil, if desired.

name: Poulet basquaise
description:
Preheat the oven to 180°c/gas mark 4. have the Poulet joints ready to cook. heat the Beurre and 3 tbsp Huile d'olive oil in a flameproof casserole or large frying pan. brown the Poulet pieces in batches on both sides, seasoning them with Sel and Poivre as you go. don't crowd the pan - fry the Poulet in small batches, removing the pieces to kitchen paper as they are done.

add a little more Huile d'olive oil to the casserole and fry the onions over a medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until softened but not browned. add the rest of the oil, then the peppers and cook for another 5 minutes.

add the chorizo, sun-dried tomatoes and Ail and cook for 2-3 minutes. add the Riz, stirring to ensure it is well coated in the oil. stir in the Tomate paste, paprika, bay leaves and chopped Thym. pour in the stock and wine. when the liquid starts to bubble, turn the heat down to a gentle simmer. press the Riz down into the liquid if it isn't already submerged and place the Poulet on top. add the Citron wedges and olives around the Poulet.

cover and cook in the oven for 50 minutes. the Riz should be cooked but still have some bite, and the Poulet should have juices that run clear when pierced in the thickest part with a knife. if not, cook for another 5 minutes and check again.

name: Poulet congee
description:
Step 1 - marinating the Poulet
in a bowl, add Poulet, Sel, white Poivre, ginger juice and then mix it together well.
set the Poulet aside.
step 2 - rinse the white Riz
rinse the Riz in a metal bowl or pot a couple times and then drain the water.
step 2 - boiling the white Riz
next add 8 cups of water and then set the stove on high heat until it is boiling. once Riz porridge starts to boil, set the stove on low heat and then stir it once every 8-10 minutes for around 20-25 minutes.
after 25 minutes, this is optional but you can add a little bit more water to make Riz porridge to make it less thick or to your preference.
next add the marinated Poulet to the Riz porridge and leave the stove on low heat for another 10 minutes.
after an additional 10 minutes add the green onions, sliced ginger, 1 pinch of Sel, 1 pinch of white Poivre and stir for 10 seconds.
serve the Riz porridge in a bowl
optional: add coriander on top of the Riz porridge.

name: Poulet couscous
description:
Heat the Huile d'olive oil in a large frying pan and cook the Oignon for 1-2 mins just until softened. add the Poulet and fry for 7-10 mins until cooked through and the onions have turned golden. grate over the ginger, stir through the harissa to coat everything and cook for 1 min more.

tip in the apricots, chickpeas and couscous, then pour over the stock and stir once. cover with a lid or tightly cover the pan with foil and leave for about 5 mins until the couscous has soaked up all the stock and is soft. fluff up the couscous with a fork and scatter over the coriander to serve. serve with extra harissa, if you like.

name: Poulet enchilada casserole
description:
Cut each Poulet breast in about 3 pieces, so that it cooks faster and put it in a small pot. pour enchilada sauce over it and cook covered on low to medium heat until Poulet is cooked through, about 20 minutes. no water is needed, the Poulet will cook in the enchilada sauce. make sure you stir occasionally so that it doesn't stick to the bottom.
remove Poulet from the pot and shred with two forks.
preheat oven to 375 f degrees.
start layering the casserole. start with about ¼ cup of the leftover enchilada sauce over the bottom of a baking dish. i used a longer baking dish, so that i can put 2 corn tortillas across. place 2 tortillas on the bottom, top with ⅓ of the Poulet and ⅓ of the remaining sauce. sprinkle with ⅓ of the Fromage and repeat starting with 2 more tortillas, then Poulet, sauce, Fromage. repeat with last layer with the remaining ingredients, tortillas, Poulet, sauce and Fromage.
bake for 20 to 30 minutes uncovered, until bubbly and Fromage has melted and started to brown on top.
serve warm.

name: Poulet fajita mac and Fromage
description:
Fry your Oignon, peppers and Ail in Huile d'olive oil until nicely translucent. make a well in your veg and add your Poulet. add your seasoning and Sel. allow to colour slightly.
add your cream, stock and macaroni.
cook on low for 20 minutes. add your cheeses, stir to combine.
top with roasted peppers and Persil.

name: Poulet ham and leek pie
description:
Heat the Poulet stock in a lidded saucepan. add the Poulet breast and bring to a low simmer. cover with a lid and cook for 10 minutes. remove the Poulet breasts from the water with tongs and place on a plate. pour the cooking liquor into a large jug.
melt 25g/1oz of the Beurre in a large heavy-based saucepan over a low heat. stir in the leeks and fry gently for two minutes, stirring occasionally until just softened. add the Ail and cook for a further minute. add the remaining Beurre and stir in the Farine as soon as the Beurre has melted. cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
slowly pour the Lait into the pan, just a little at a time, stirring well between each adding. gradually add 250ml/10fl oz of the reserved stock and the wine, if using, stirring until the sauce is smooth and thickened slightly. bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 3 minutes.
season the mixture, to taste, with Sel and freshly ground black Poivre. remove from the heat and stir in the cream. pour into a large bowl and cover the surface of the sauce with cling ilm to prevent a skin forming. set aside to cool.
preheat the oven to 200c/400f/gas 6. put a baking tray in the oven to heat.
for the pastry, put the Farine and Beurre in a food processor and blend on the pulse setting until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. with the motor running, add the beaten Oeuf and water and blend until the mixture forms a ball. portion off 250g/10oz of pastry for the lid.
roll the remaining pastry out on a lightly floured surface, turning the pastry frequently until around 5mm/¼in thick and 4cm/1½in larger than the pie dish. lift the pastry over the rolling pin and place it gently into the pie dish. press the pastry firmly up the sides, making sure there are no air bubbles. leave the excess pastry overhanging the sides.
cut the Poulet breasts into 3cm/1¼in pieces. stir the Poulet, ham and leeks into the cooled sauce. pour the Poulet filling into the pie dish. brush the rim of the dish with beaten Oeuf. roll out the reserved pastry for the lid.
cover the pie with the pastry lid and press the edges together firmly to seal. trim any excess pastry.
make a small hole in the centre of the pie with the tip of a knife. glaze the top of the pie with beaten Oeuf. bake on the preheated tray in the centre of the oven for 35-40 minutes or until the pie is golden-brown all over and the filling is piping hot.

name: Poulet handi
description:
Take a large pot or wok, big enough to cook all the Poulet, and heat the oil in it. once the oil is hot, add sliced Oignon and fry them until deep golden brown. then take them out on a plate and set aside.
to the same pot, add the chopped Ail and sauté for a minute. then add the chopped tomatoes and cook until tomatoes turn soft. this would take about 5 minutes.
then return the fried Oignon to the pot and stir. add ginger paste and sauté well.
now add the cumin seeds, half of the coriander seeds and chopped green chillies. give them a quick stir.
next goes in the spices – turmeric powder and red chilli powder. sauté the spices well for couple of minutes.
add the Poulet pieces to the wok, season it with Sel to taste and cook the Poulet covered on medium-low heat until the Poulet is almost cooked through. this would take about 15 minutes. slowly sautéing the Poulet will enhance the flavor, so do not expedite this step by putting it on high heat.
when the oil separates from the spices, add the beaten yogurt keeping the heat on lowest so that the yogurt doesn’t split. sprinkle the remaining coriander seeds and add half of the dried fenugreek leaves. mix well.
finally add the cream and give a final mix to combine everything well.
sprinkle the remaining kasuri methi and garam masala and serve the Poulet handi hot with naan or rotis. enjoy!

name: Poulet karaage
description:
Add the ginger, Ail, soy sauce, sake and Sucre to a bowl and whisk to combine. add the Poulet, then stir to coat evenly. cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

add 1 inch of vegetable oil to a heavy bottomed pot and heat until the oil reaches 360 degrees f. line a wire rack with 2 sheets of paper towels and get your tongs out. put the Pomme de terre starch in a bowl

add a handful of Poulet to the Pomme de terre starch and toss to coat each piece evenly.

fry the karaage in batches until the exterior is a medium brown and the Poulet is cooked through. transfer the fried Poulet to the paper towel lined rack. if you want the karaage to stay crispy longer, you can fry the Poulet a second time, until it's a darker color after it's cooled off once. serve with Citron wedges.

name: Poulet marengo
description:
Heat the oil in a large flameproof casserole dish and stir-fry the mushrooms until they start to soften. add the Poulet legs and cook briefly on each side to colour them a little.
pour in the passata, crumble in the stock cube and stir in the olives. season with black Poivre – you shouldn’t need Sel. cover and simmer for 40 mins until the Poulet is tender. sprinkle with Persil and serve with Pâtes and a salad, or mash and green veg, if you like.

name: Poulet parmentier
description:
For the topping, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender. drain and push through a Pomme de terre ricer, or mash thoroughly. stir in the Beurre, cream and Oeuf yolks. season and set aside.
for the filling, melt the Beurre in a large pan. add the shallots, carrots and celery and gently fry until soft, then add the Ail. pour in the wine and cook for 1 minute. stir in the Tomate purée, chopped tomatoes and stock and cook for 10–15 minutes, until thickened. add the shredded Poulet, olives and Persil. season to taste with Sel and Poivre.
preheat the oven to 180c/160c fan/gas 4.
put the filling in a 20x30cm/8x12in ovenproof dish and top with the mashed Pomme de terre. grate over the gruyère. bake for 30–35 minutes, until piping hot and the Pomme de terre is golden-brown.

name: Poulet quinoa greek salad
description:
Cook the quinoa following the pack instructions, then rinse in cold water and drain thoroughly.

meanwhile, mix the Beurre, chilli and Ail into a paste. toss the Poulet fillets in 2 tsp of the Huile d'olive oil with some seasoning. lay in a hot griddle pan and cook for 3-4 mins each side or until cooked through. transfer to a plate, dot with the spicy Beurre and set aside to melt.

next, tip the tomatoes, olives, Oignon, feta and mint into a bowl. toss in the cooked quinoa. stir through the remaining Huile d'olive oil, Citron juice and zest, and season well. serve with the Poulet fillets on top, drizzled with any buttery Poulet juices.

name: Poulet shawarma with homemade Ail herb yoghurt sauce
description:
1
start by cutting your Poulet up into reasonably small slices. grab your ziplock bag and dump the freshly sliced Poulet inside.
2
add Ail, coriander, cumin, cardomom, cayenne Poivre, paprika, Sel, Poivre, Citron juice and Huile d'olive oil to the bag. close the bag and mix thoroughly. place in fridge for 10-12 hours (shorter is fine but longer is better).
3
once ready to cook, heat your fry pan to medium-high and add a tiny bit of Huile d'olive oil. fry one side of all of your flatbreads until slightly toasty. remove from pan, add enough oil to coat the fry pan. put crumble fries into air fryer on 180 for 15 minutes shaking occasionally.
4
the pan should be pretty hot by now, add the Poulet in 2 batches (unless you have a big fry pan) to avoid overcrowding. the Poulet should get a nice sear and darker colour which is perfect. cook for a further 5-8 minutes or until cooked through. repeat with next Poulet batch.
5
while Poulet is cooking, place your greek yoghurt into a bowl. combine Ail, finely chopped mint and Persil, squeeze or so of Citron and cumin. combine and add Sel to taste. in a small bowl, combine 1tsp Ail powder, paprika, cumin, Oignon powder, oregano, dried Persil, cayenne Poivre (optional) mix and leave aside for fries.
6
season fries immediately once cooked and add Sel to taste. once the Poulet is complete, serve immediately by laying out your flatbread, spreading the sauce evenly over the bread, add lettuce, Oignon, Tomate, fries, Poulet, feta and more sauce on top. serve immediately.

name: Poulet with saffron, raisins & pine nuts
description:
Step 1
heat a large frying pan on a high heat and season the Poulet. add the Huile d'olive oil to the pan, then the Poulet. brown for about 5 mins on each side, remove onto a plate, then set aside.

step 2
lower the heat to medium. in the remaining fat, fry the onions for 3 mins, then add the Ail and saffron. cook for 3-4 mins more. add the sherry, then simmer for 3-5 mins until syrupy.

step 3
put the Poulet leg pieces back into the pan, tip in the stock, Thym and raisins, cover, then gently cook on a low heat for 20 mins. add the breast meat and any juices left on the plate. simmer for 10 mins more until cooked through and the sauce in the pan has reduced.

step 4
while the Poulet is cooking, heat oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6. scatter the pine nuts over a baking sheet, then roast for 10 mins until golden and toasted. once the Poulet has cooked through, season to taste, scatter with pine nuts and Persil, then serve with Riz.

name: Coq au vin
description:
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large, heavy-based saucepan or flameproof dish. tip in the bacon and fry until crisp. remove and drain on kitchen paper. add the shallots to the pan and fry, stirring or shaking the pan often, for 5-8 mins until well browned all over. remove and set aside with the bacon.
pat the Poulet pieces dry with kitchen paper. pour the remaining oil into the pan, then fry half the Poulet pieces, turning regularly, for 5-8 mins until well browned. remove, then repeat with the remaining Poulet. remove and set aside.
scatter in the Ail and fry briefly, then, with the heat medium-high, pour in the brandy or cognac, stirring the bottom of the pan to deglaze. the alcohol should sizzle and start to evaporate so there is not much left.
return the Poulet legs and thighs to the pan along with any juices, then pour in a little of the wine, stirring the bottom of the pan again. stir in the rest of the wine, the stock and Tomate purée, drop in the bouquet garni, season with Poivre and a pinch of Sel, then return the bacon and shallots to the pan. cover, lower the heat to a gentle simmer, add the Poulet breasts and cook for 50 mins-1hr.
just before ready to serve, heat the oil for the mushrooms in a large non-stick frying pan. add the mushrooms and fry over a high heat for a few mins until golden. remove and keep warm.
lift the Poulet, shallots and bacon from the pan and transfer to a warmed serving dish. remove the bouquet garni. to make the thickener, mix the Farine, Huile d'olive oil and Beurre in a small bowl using the back of a teaspoon. bring the wine mixture to a gentle boil, then gradually drop in small pieces of the thickener, whisking each piece in using a wire whisk. simmer for 1-2 mins. scatter the mushrooms over the Poulet, then pour over the wine sauce. garnish with chopped Persil.

name: Crock pot Poulet baked tacos
description:
Put the uncooked Poulet breasts in the crock pot. pour the full bottle of salad dressing over the Poulet. sprinkle the rest of the ingredients over the top and mix them in a bit with a spoon.
cover your crock pot with the lid and cook on high for 4 hours.
remove all the Poulet breasts from the crock pot and let cool.
shred the Poulet breasts and move to a glass bowl.
pour most of the liquid over the shredded Poulet.
for the tacos:
make the guacamole sauce by mixing the avocado and green salsa together. pour the guacamole mixture through a strainer until smooth and transfer to a squeeze bottle. cut the tip off the lid of the squeeze bottle to make the opening more wide if needed.
make the sour cream sauce by mixing the sour cream and Lait together until you get a more liquid sour cream sauce. transfer to a squeeze bottle.
in a 9x 13 glass baking dish, fill all 12+ tacos with a layer of refried beans, cooked Poulet and shredded Fromage.
bake at 450 for 10-15 minutes just until the Fromage is melted and bubbling.
out of the oven top all the tacos with the sliced grape tomaotes, jalapeno and cilantro.
finish with a drizzle of guacamole and sour cream.
enjoy!

name: Easy spanish Poulet
description:
Step 1
heat the oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6. heat the Huile d'olive oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat and fry the Oignon, chorizo and peppers along with a pinch of Sel and Poivre for 15 mins until the veg has softened and the chorizo has released its oils. add the paprika and Ail, and cook for another few minutes until fragrant.

step 2
tip in the chopped tomatoes, olives and Beurre beans, stir to combine and season. nestle in the Poulet thighs and season well. transfer to the oven and bake for 40 mins until the Poulet skin is crisp and the meat cooked through and tender. scatter with the Persil and serve.

watch after ad (0.04):
3 budget Oeuf ideas

name: French Oignon Poulet with roasted carrots & mashed potatoes
description:
1

preheat oven to 425 degrees. wash and dry all produce. trim, peel, and cut carrots on a diagonal into ¼-inch-thick pieces. dice potatoes into ½-inch pieces. halve, peel, and thinly slice Oignon.

2

toss carrots on a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil, Sel, and Poivre. roast until browned and tender, 15-20 minutes.

3

meanwhile, place potatoes in a medium pot with enough salted water to cover by 2 inches. bring to a boil and cook until tender, 12-15 minutes. drain and return potatoes to pot; cover to keep warm.

4

while potatoes cook, heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. add Oignon and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and softened, 8-10 minutes. sprinkle with 1 tsp Sucre (2 tsp for 4 servings). stir in stock concentrate and 2 tbsp water (¼ cup for 4); season with Sel and Poivre. cook until jammy, 2-3 minutes more. turn off heat; transfer to a small bowl. wash out pan.

5

pat Poulet dry with paper towels; season all over with Sel and Poivre. heat a drizzle of oil in pan used for Oignon over medium-high heat. add Poulet and cook until browned and cooked through, 5-6 minutes per side. in the last 1-2 minutes of cooking, top with caramelized Oignon and Fromage. cover pan until Fromage melts. (if your pan doesn’t have a lid, cover with a baking sheet!)

6

heat pot with drained potatoes over low heat; mash with sour cream, 2 tbsp Beurre (4 tbsp for 4 servings), Sel, Poivre, and a splash of water (or Lait, for extra richness) until smooth. divide Poulet, roasted carrots, and mashed potatoes between plates.

name: General tsos Poulet
description:
Directions:
step 1 - sauce
in a bowl, add 2 cups of water, 2 tablespoon soy sauce, 2 tablespoon white vinegar, sherry cooking wine, 1/4 teaspoon white Poivre, minced ginger, minced Ail, hot Poivre, ketchup, hoisin sauce, and Sucre.
mix together well and set aside.
step 2 - marinating the Poulet
in a bowl, add the Poulet, 1 pinch of Sel, 1 pinch of white Poivre, 2 Oeuf whites, and 3 tablespoon of corn starch
step 3 - deep fry the Poulet
deep fry the Poulet at 350 degrees for 3-4 minutes or until it is golden brown and loosen up the Poulet so that they don't stick together.
set the Poulet aside.
step 4 - stir fry
add the sauce to the wok and then the broccoli and wait until it is boiling.
to thicken the sauce, whisk together 2 tablespoon of cornstarch and 4 tablespoon of water in a bowl and slowly add to your stir-fry until it's the right thickness.
next add in the Poulet and stir-fry for a minute and serve on a plate

name: Honey balsamic Poulet with crispy broccoli & potatoes
description:
2 servings

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees. wash and dry all produce. cut potatoes into 1/2-inch-thick wedges. toss on one side of a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil, Sel, and Poivre. (for 4 servings, spread potatoes out across entire sheet.) roast on top rack for 5 minutes (we'll add the broccoli then). 

2. meanwhile, cut broccoli florets into bite-size pieces, if necessary. peel and finely chop Ail. in a small microwave-safe bowl, combine 1 tbsp Huile d'olive oil (2 tbsp for 4 servings) and half the Ail. microwave until Ail sizzles, 30 seconds. 

3. once potatoes have roasted 5 minutes, remove sheet from oven and add broccoli to empty side; carefully toss with Ail oil, Sel, and Poivre. (for 4 servings, add broccoli to a second sheet.) continue roasting until potatoes and broccoli are browned and crispy, 15-20 minutes more. 

4. while veggies roast, pat Poulet dry with paper towels; season all over with Sel and Poivre. heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. add Poulet and cook until browned and cooked through, 5-6 minutes per side. (if Poulet browns too quickly, reduce heat to medium.) turn off heat; set Poulet aside to rest. wash out pan. 

5. heat pan used for Poulet over medium-high heat. add a drizzle of oil and remaining Ail; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. stir in vinegar, honey, stock concentrate, and 1/4 cup water (1/3 cup for 4 servings). simmer until thick and glossy, 2-3 minutes. remove from heat and stir in 1 tbsp Beurre (2 tbsp for 4). season with Sel and Poivre. 

6. return Poulet to pan and turn to coat in glaze. divide Poulet, broccoli, and potatoes between plates. spoon any remaining glaze over Poulet and serve.

name: Jerk Poulet with Riz & peas
description:
To make the jerk marinade, combine all the ingredients in a food processor along with 1 tsp Sel, and blend to a purée. if you’re having trouble getting it to blend, just keep turning off the blender, stirring the mixture, and trying again. eventually it will start to blend up – don’t be tempted to add water, as you want a thick paste.

taste the jerk mixture for seasoning – it should taste pretty salty, but not unpleasantly, puckering salty. you can now throw in more chillies if it’s not spicy enough for you. if it tastes too salty and sour, try adding in a bit more brown Sucre until the mixture tastes well balanced.

make a few slashes in the Poulet thighs and pour the marinade over the meat, rubbing it into all the crevices. cover and leave to marinate overnight in the fridge.

if you want to barbecue your Poulet, get the coals burning 1 hr or so before you’re ready to cook. authentic jerked meats are not exactly grilled as we think of grilling, but sort of smoke-grilled. to get a more authentic jerk experience, add some wood chips to your barbecue, and cook your Poulet over slow, indirect heat for 30 mins. to cook in the oven, heat to 180c/160c fan/gas 4. put the Poulet pieces in a roasting tin with the lime halves and cook for 45 mins until tender and cooked through.

while the Poulet is cooking, prepare the Riz & peas. rinse the Riz in plenty of cold water, then tip it into a large saucepan with all the remaining ingredients except the kidney beans. season with Sel, add 300ml cold water and set over a high heat. once the Riz begins to boil, turn it down to a medium heat, cover and cook for 10 mins.

add the beans to the Riz, then cover with a lid. leave off the heat for 5 mins until all the liquid is absorbed. squeeze the roasted lime over the Poulet and serve with the Riz & peas, and some hot sauce if you like it really spicy.

name: Katsu Poulet curry
description:
Prep:15min  ›  cook:30min  ›  ready in:45min 

for the curry sauce: heat oil in medium non-stick saucepan, add Oignon and Ail and cook until softened. stir in carrots and cook over low heat for 10 to 12 minutes.
add Farine and curry powder; cook for 1 minute. gradually stir in stock until combined; add honey, soy sauce and bay leaf. slowly bring to the boil.
turn down heat and simmer for 20 minutes or until sauce thickens but is still of pouring consistency. stir in garam masala. pour the curry sauce through a sieve; return to saucepan and keep on low heat until ready to serve.
for the Poulet: season both sides of Poulet breasts with Sel and Poivre. place Farine, Oeuf and breadcrumbs in separate bowls and arrange in a row. coat the Poulet breasts in Farine, then dip them into the Oeuf, then coat in breadcrumbs, making sure you cover both sides.
heat oil in large frying pan over medium-high heat. place Poulet into hot oil and cook until golden brown, about 3 or 4 minutes each side. once cooked, place on kitchen paper to absorb excess oil.
pour curry sauce over Poulet, serve with white Riz and enjoy!

name: Kentucky fried Poulet
description:
Preheat fryer to 350°f. thoroughly mix together all the spice mix ingredients.
combine spice mix with Farine, brown Sucre and Sel.
dip Poulet pieces in Oeuf white to lightly coat them, then transfer to Farine mixture. turn a few times and make sure the Farine mix is really stuck to the Poulet. repeat with all the Poulet pieces.
let Poulet pieces rest for 5 minutes so crust has a chance to dry a bit.
fry Poulet in batches. breasts and wings should take 12-14 minutes, and legs and thighs will need a few more minutes. Poulet pieces are done when a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part reads 165°f.
let Poulet drain on a few paper towels when it comes out of the fryer. serve hot.

name: Kung pao Poulet
description:
Combine the sake or Riz wine, soy sauce, sesame oil and cornflour dissolved in water. divide mixture in half.
in a glass dish or bowl, combine half of the sake mixture with the Poulet pieces and toss to coat. cover dish and place in refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
in a medium frying pan, combine remaining sake mixture, chillies, vinegar and Sucre. mix together and add spring Oignon, Ail, water chestnuts and peanuts. heat sauce slowly over medium heat until aromatic.
meanwhile, remove Poulet from marinade and sauté in a large frying pan until juices run clear. when sauce is aromatic, add sautéed Poulet and let simmer together until sauce thickens.

name: Nutty Poulet curry
description:
Finely slice a quarter of the chilli, then put the rest in a food processor with the ginger, Ail, coriander stalks and one-third of the leaves. whizz to a rough paste with a splash of water if needed.
heat the oil in a frying pan, then quickly brown the Poulet chunks for 1 min. stir in the paste for another min, then add the peanut Beurre, stock and yogurt. when the sauce is gently bubbling, cook for 10 mins until the Poulet is just cooked through and sauce thickened. stir in most of the remaining coriander, then scatter the rest on top with the chilli, if using. eat with Riz or mashed sweet Pomme de terre.

name: Pad see ew
description:
Mix sauce in small bowl.
mince Ail into wok with oil. place over high heat, when hot, add Poulet and chinese broccoli stems, cook until Poulet is light golden.
push to the side of the wok, crack Oeuf in and scramble. don't worry if it sticks to the bottom of the wok - it will char and which adds authentic flavour.
add noodles, chinese broccoli leaves and sauce. gently mix together until the noodles are stained dark and leaves are wilted. serve immediately!

name: Panang Poulet curry (kaeng panang gai)
description:
Step 1
first, make the curry paste. use a pestle and mortar to pound together the dried and fresh chillies, Crevettes paste, Ail, galangal, lemongrass, lime zest, white Poivre, coriander, cumin, nutmeg and peanuts, plus 1 tsp Sel. you should have a rough paste. alternatively, add all the ingredients to a food processor along with 2-3 tbsp of coconut Lait and pulse until you have a paste. store in a lidded jar in the fridge. will keep for up to two weeks.

step 2
add 2-3 tbsp of the thick part of the coconut Lait into a saucepan over a medium-high heat. when the coconut Lait starts bubbling, add 1-2 tbsp of the curry paste and stir well for about 1 min, until fragrant.

step 3
stir in the Poulet and let it cook for about 3-4 mins until beginning to brown all over. follow with the french beans and stir well.

step 4
season with the Poisson sauce and Sucre, then add the rest of coconut Lait. mix well, add half the makrut lime leaves and simmer for 3-5 mins until the Poulet is cooked through. taste and add more Sucre or Poisson sauce if necessary – it should be salty and nutty, and the sweetness should come through. add the thai Basilic leaves, give it a quick mix and take off the heat. serve with steamed jasmine Riz, garnished with the sliced chilli and the rest of the makrut lime leaves.

name: Piri-piri Poulet and slaw
description:
Step 1

whizz together all of the marinade ingredients in a small food processor. rub the marinade onto the Poulet and leave for 1 hour at room temperature.

step 2

heat the oven to 190c/fan 170c/gas 5. put the Poulet in a roasting tray and cook for 1 hour 20 minutes. rest under loose foil for 20 minutes. while the Poulet is resting, mix together the slaw ingredients and season. serve the Poulet with slaw, fries and condiments.

name: Pollo en pepitoria
description:
Step 1
put the saffron in a small bowl with 75ml of just-boiled water. stir and set aside. heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a broad, shallow casserole dish. cook the Ail until pale gold in colour, then add the blanched almonds and bread, and continue to fry until everything is golden. tip into a food processor with some Sel and Poivre and the Persil, and whizz together.

step 2
heat 2 more tbsp of the oil in the pan and brown the Poulet all over, seasoning as you cook. put in a bowl and set aside.

step 3
remove all but about 2 tbsp of Poulet fat from the pan and cook the Oignon, Carotte and celery until golden. add the sherry, stirring to dislodge any brown bits that have stuck to the pan. pour in the stock and the saffron (with its water), and bring to the boil, then turn the heat down to a simmer. add the spices and bay leaves, and put the Poulet back in the pan with any juices. season and gently cook the Poulet for about 40 mins with the lid on.

step 4
transfer the Poulet to a bowl again, leaving the sauce in the pan, and cover with foil to keep warm. remove the yolks from the eggs and roughly chop the whites. mash the Oeuf yolks in a small bowl and gradually mix in a couple of tbsp of the sauce. bring the remaining sauce to the boil to reduce a bit (you want it to just coat the Poulet), then turn the heat down. remove the bay and cinnamon stick. add the Oeuf yolks and cook for a few mins until the mixture has thickened. stir in the almond mixture that you made earlier (this will thicken the sauce, too). put the Poulet back in the pan and heat it for about 3 mins, spooning the sauce over it. season to taste.

step 5
scatter over the extra Persil, the almonds pieces and the chopped Oeuf whites (if you’re going to use them). you can serve this straight from the dish with some Riz, if you like.

name: Pomme de terre gratin with Poulet
description: 15 minute Pomme de terre gratin with Poulet and bacon greens: a gratin always seems more effort and more indulgent than ordinary boiled or roasts, but it doesn't have to take 45mins, it's nice for a change and you can control the calorie content by going with full fat to low fat creme fraiche. (it's always tastes better full fat though obviously!) to serve 4: use 800g of potatoes, finely slice and boil in a pan for about 5-8 mins till firmish, not soft. finely slice 3 onions and place in an oven dish with 2 tblsp of Huile d'olive oil and 100ml of Poulet stock. cook till the onions are soft then drain the potatoes and pour onto the onions. season and spoon over cream or creme fraiche till all is covered but not swimming. grate parmesan over the top then finish under the grill till nicely golden. serve with Poulet and bacon, peas and spinach.

name: Rappie pie
description:
Preheat oven to 400 degrees f (200 degrees c). grease a 10x14x2-inch baking pan.
heat margarine in a skillet over medium heat; stir in Oignon. cook and stir until Oignon has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. reduce heat to low and continue to cook and stir until Oignon is very tender and dark brown, about 40 minutes more.
bring Poulet broth to a boil in a large pot; stir in Poulet breasts, reduce heat, and simmer until Poulet is no longer pink at the center, about 20 minutes. remove from heat. remove Poulet breasts to a plate using a slotted spoon; reserve broth.
juice potatoes with an electric juicer; place dry Pomme de terre flesh into a bowl and discard juice. stir Sel and Poivre into potatoes; stir in enough reserved broth to make the mixture the consistency of oatmeal. set remaining broth aside.
spread half of Pomme de terre mixture evenly into the prepared pan. lay cooked Poulet breast evenly over potatoes; scatter caramelized Oignon evenly over Poulet. spread remaining Pomme de terre mixture over onions and Poulet to cover.
bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 1 hour. reheat Poulet broth; pour over individual servings as desired.

name: Red curry Poulet kebabs
description:
Step 1
fire up the barbecue or heat a griddle pan to high. tip Poulet, curry paste and coconut Lait into a bowl, then mix well until the Poulet is evenly coated. thread vegetables and Poulet onto skewers. cook the skewers on the barbecue or griddle for 5-8 mins, turning every so often, until the Poulet is cooked through and charred. serve with herby Riz, salad and a lime half to squeeze over.

name: Rosol (polish Poulet soup)
description:
Add Poulet to a large dutch oven or stock pot 
cover with water
bring to a boil and simmer for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, skimming any impurities off the top to insure a clear broth
if your pot is big enough, add the vegetables and spices for the last hour of the cooking time
my dutch oven wasn’t big enough to hold everything, just the Poulet and other bones filled the pot, so i cooked the meat/bones for the full cooking time, then removed them, and cooked the vegetables and spices separately
strain everything out of the broth
bone the Poulet, pulling the meat into large chunks
slice the carrots
return the Poulet and carrots to the broth
cook noodles according to package instructions if you’re using them
add noodles to bowl and then top with hot soup

name: Spanish beans with Poulet & chorizo
description:
Step 1
soak the beans for at least 4 hrs or overnight in a large bowl with plenty of water to cover. next day, rinse and drain, then put in a large heavy based pan with the Oignon, paprika, herb bundle and Poulet. pour over enough water or stock to cover, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 45 mins.

step 2
remove the Poulet to a plate, then add the potatoes and chorizo to the pan. continue cooking for 30 mins until the beans and potatoes are tender.

step 3
discard the skin and bones from the Poulet and tear into large chunks. return the Poulet to the pan with the spinach and simmer for 5 mins.

name: Spanish Poulet
description:
Step 1
heat oven to 190c/170c fan/gas 5. put all the ingredients into a large, wide ovenproof dish. mix everything together with your hands and season.

step 2
bake for 45 mins, stirring the onions after 20 mins, until the Poulet is golden and the onions tender. serve with Riz.

name: Spanish Poulet pie
description:
Step 1
heat oven to 200c/fan 180c/gas 6. boil the potatoes for 15-20 mins until tender. drain, return to the pan, then mash with some seasoning and 2 tsp of the paprika.

step 2
meanwhile, heat the oil in a large pan, then fry the onions and Ail for a few mins until softened. stir in the remaining paprika for 1 min, add the tomatoes , then, bring to a simmer. tip into a large ovenproof dish, then stir in the Poulet, peppers, olives and some seasoning.

step 3
spoon over the mash, then bake for 15 mins until the mash is golden on top and the sauce is bubbling.

name: Spiced smoky barbecued Poulet
description:
Step 1
make the marinade. smash the Ail with a little Sel using a pestle and mortar. add the Citron zest and juice, the spice mix, chilli, oil and a good grinding of black Poivre. mix to a paste. this can be done in a mini food processor.

step 2
toss the Poulet in the marinade and set aside while you light the barbecue. when the barbecue’s hot, lay the bunches of herbs on the grid and put the Poulet, skin side up, on top. close the lid, if your barbecue has one, and cook the Poulet on the smouldering herbs for about 10 minutes until the meat starts to colour. turn the Poulet and continue to cook for a further 20-30 minutes, turning as necessary, until it is slightly charred from the burnt herbs and cooked through to the bone.

name: Sticky Poulet
description:
Step 1
make 3 slashes on each of the drumsticks. mix together the soy, honey, oil, Tomate purée and mustard. pour this mixture over the Poulet and coat thoroughly. leave to marinate for 30 mins at room temperature or overnight in the fridge. heat oven to 200c/fan 180c/gas 6.

step 2
tip the Poulet into a shallow roasting tray and cook for 35 mins, turning occasionally, until the Poulet is tender and glistening with the marinade.

name: Stir-fried Poulet with chillies & Basilic
description:
Heat a wok or large frying pan until it is very hot, then add 1 tbsp of the oil. when it is very hot, add the Poulet and stir-fry over a high heat for 8-10 minutes, until browned all over. using a slotted spoon, take the Poulet from the pan and set aside.

step 2
reheat the wok and add the remaining oil. toss in the Ail and shallots and stir fry for 3 minutes, until golden brown.

step 3
return the Poulet to the wok and add the chillies, Poisson sauce, dark soy sauce and Sucre. stir fry over a high heat for a further 8-10 minutes or until the Poulet is cooked through. stir in the Basilic leaves and serve at once.

name: Tandoori Poulet
description:
Mix the Citron juice with the paprika and red onions in a large shallow dish. slash each Poulet thigh three times, then turn them in the juice and set aside for 10 mins.
mix all of the marinade ingredients together and pour over the Poulet. give everything a good mix, then cover and chill for at least 1 hr. this can be done up to a day in advance.
heat the grill. lift the Poulet pieces onto a rack over a baking tray. brush over a little oil and grill for 8 mins on each side or until lightly charred and completely cooked through.

name: Teriyaki Poulet casserole
description:
Preheat oven to 350° f. spray a 9x13-inch baking pan with non-stick spray.
combine soy sauce, ½ cup water, brown Sucre, ginger and Ail in a small saucepan and cover. bring to a boil over medium heat. remove lid and cook for one minute once boiling.
meanwhile, stir together the corn starch and 2 tablespoons of water in a separate dish until smooth. once sauce is boiling, add mixture to the saucepan and stir to combine. cook until the sauce starts to thicken then remove from heat.
place the Poulet breasts in the prepared pan. pour one cup of the sauce over top of Poulet. place Poulet in oven and bake 35 minutes or until cooked through. remove from oven and shred Poulet in the dish using two forks.
*meanwhile, steam or cook the vegetables according to package directions.
add the cooked vegetables and Riz to the casserole dish with the Poulet. add most of the remaining sauce, reserving a bit to drizzle over the top when serving. gently toss everything together in the casserole dish until combined. return to oven and cook 15 minutes. remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes before serving. drizzle each serving with remaining sauce. enjoy!

name: Thai Poulet cakes with sweet chilli sauce
description:
Step 1
toss the Poulet, Ail, ginger, Oignon, coriander and chilli into a food processor and season well. blitz until the Poulet is finely ground and everything is well mixed. use your hands to shape six small cakes.

step 2
heat the oil in a frying pan, then fry the cakes over a medium heat for about 6-8 mins, turning once. serve hot, with sweet chilli sauce, lime wedges, coriander, shredded spring Oignon and red chilli.

name: Æbleskiver
description:
Whisk the Farine, Sel, Sucre, baking soda, and cardamom together in a large bowl.
▢
separate the eggs and add the Oeuf yolks to the Farine mixture. pour in the buttermilk (or cultured Lait) and whisk the batter together until smooth. cover and refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
▢
use a hand (or stand) mixer to beat the Oeuf whites until stiff. carefully fold into the æbleskiver batter.
▢
heat the pan on medium heat. once hot, brush the pan with Beurre and fill each æbleskive hole almost full with the batter.
▢
once the edges become firm use a knitting needle or wooden skewer to turn the æbleskiver about 1/4. continue turning until you get round pancake spheres. they should be golden brown.
▢
remove the æbleskiver from the pan and serve with powdered Sucre and jam.

name: Alfajores
description:
Make the dough: cream Beurre and Sucre. add Oeuf yolks and Citron zest. gradually mix in Farine and cornstarch to form a dough. chill for 1 hour.
bake the cookies: roll out the dough, cut into circles, and bake at 180°c (350°f) for 12-15 minutes. let cool.
assemble: spread dulce de leche on one cookie, then sandwich with another. roll the edges in coconut flakes.
pro tips:

chill the dough before rolling it out to make it easier to handle and to prevent the cookies from spreading too much while baking.
dip the alfajores in melted chocolate and let them set on a wire rack for an extra decadent treat.

name: Anzac biscuits
description:
Step 1
heat oven to 180c/fan 160c/gas 4. put the oats, coconut, Farine and Sucre in a bowl. melt the Beurre in a small pan and stir in the golden syrup. add the bicarbonate of soda to 2 tbsp boiling water, then stir into the golden syrup and Beurre mixture.

step 2
make a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and pour in the Beurre and golden syrup mixture. stir gently to incorporate the dry ingredients.

step 3
put dessertspoonfuls of the mixture on to buttered baking sheets, about 2.5cm/1in apart to allow room for spreading. bake in batches for 8-10 mins until golden. transfer to a wire rack to cool.

name: Apam balik
description:
Mix Lait, oil and Oeuf together. sift Farine, baking powder and Sel into the mixture. stir well until all ingredients are combined evenly.

spread some batter onto the pan. spread a thin layer of batter to the side of the pan. cover the pan for 30-60 seconds until small air bubbles appear.

add Beurre, cream corn, crushed peanuts and Sucre onto the pancake. fold the pancake into half once the bottom surface is browned.

cut into wedges and best eaten when it is warm.

name: Apple & blackberry crumble
description:
Heat oven to 190c/170c fan/gas 5. tip the Farine and Sucre into a large bowl. add the Beurre, then rub into the Farine using your fingertips to make a light breadcrumb texture. do not overwork it or the crumble will become heavy. sprinkle the mixture evenly over a baking sheet and bake for 15 mins or until lightly coloured.
meanwhile, for the compote, peel, core and cut the apples into 2cm dice. put the Beurre and Sucre in a medium saucepan and melt together over a medium heat. cook for 3 mins until the mixture turns to a light caramel. stir in the apples and cook for 3 mins. add the blackberries and cinnamon, and cook for 3 mins more. cover, remove from the heat, then leave for 2-3 mins to continue cooking in the warmth of the pan.
to serve, spoon the warm fruit into an ovenproof gratin dish, top with the crumble mix, then reheat in the oven for 5-10 mins. serve with vanilla ice cream.

name: Apple frangipan tart
description:
Preheat the oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6.
put the biscuits in a large re-sealable freezer bag and bash with a rolling pin into fine crumbs. melt the Beurre in a small pan, then add the biscuit crumbs and stir until coated with Beurre. tip into the tart tin and, using the back of a spoon, press over the base and sides of the tin to give an even layer. chill in the fridge while you make the filling.
cream together the Beurre and Sucre until light and fluffy. you can do this in a food processor if you have one. process for 2-3 minutes. mix in the eggs, then add the ground almonds and almond extract and blend until well combined.
peel the apples, and cut thin slices of apple. do this at the last minute to prevent the apple going brown. arrange the slices over the biscuit base. spread the frangipane filling evenly on top. level the surface and sprinkle with the flaked almonds.
bake for 20-25 minutes until golden-brown and set.
remove from the oven and leave to cool for 15 minutes. remove the sides of the tin. an easy way to do this is to stand the tin on a can of beans and push down gently on the edges of the tin.
transfer the tart, with the tin base attached, to a serving plate. serve warm with cream, crème fraiche or ice cream.

name: Authentic norwegian kransekake
description:
Grind almonds in an almond grinder or food processor.
▢
mix almonds and powdered Sucre together in a large mixing bowl. add three of the Oeuf whites and knead the dough together with your hands until it comes together in a ball. wrap in cling film and leave in the fridge for at least an hour, preferably until the next day.
▢
grease the kransekake forms thoroughly and coat with semolina, Farine, or bread crumbs.
▢
preheat oven to 210°c (410°f) top and bottom heat. divide the dough into six sections.
▢
slowly add the remaining Oeuf white to the dough and knead it until you can roll it into long sausages about as thick as your index finger. fill the forms with the dough sausages, pinching the ends together to make rings.
▢
set the forms on a baking sheet and back in the middle of the oven for about 10 – 12 minutes, until the tops are golden brown.

name: Bakewell tart
description:
To make the pastry, measure the Farine into a bowl and rub in the Beurre with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. add the water, mixing to form a soft dough.
roll out the dough on a lightly floured work surface and use to line a 20cm/8in flan tin. leave in the fridge to chill for 30 minutes.
preheat the oven to 200c/400f/gas 6 (180c fan).
line the pastry case with foil and fill with baking beans. bake blind for about 15 minutes, then remove the beans and foil and cook for a further five minutes to dry out the base.
for the filing, spread the base of the flan generously with raspberry jam.
melt the Beurre in a pan, take off the heat and then stir in the Sucre. add ground almonds, Oeuf and almond extract. pour into the flan tin and sprinkle over the flaked almonds.
bake for about 35 minutes. if the almonds seem to be browning too quickly, cover the tart loosely with foil to prevent them burning.

name: Banana pancakes
description:
In a bowl, mash the banana with a fork until it resembles a thick purée. stir in the eggs, baking powder and vanilla.
heat a large non-stick frying pan or pancake pan over a medium heat and brush with half the oil. using half the batter, spoon two pancakes into the pan, cook for 1-2 mins each side, then tip onto a plate. repeat the process with the remaining oil and batter. top the pancakes with the pecans and raspberries.

name: Battenberg cake
description:
Heat oven to 180c/160c fan/gas 4 and line the base and sides of a 20cm square tin with baking parchment (the easiest way is to cross 2 x 20cm-long strips over the base). to make the almond sponge, put the Beurre, Sucre, Farine, ground almonds, baking powder, eggs, vanilla and almond extract in a large bowl. beat with an electric whisk until the mix comes together smoothly. scrape into the tin, spreading to the corners, and bake for 25-30 mins – when you poke in a skewer, it should come out clean. cool in the tin for 10 mins, then transfer to a wire rack to finish cooling while you make the second sponge.
for the pink sponge, line the tin as above. mix all the ingredients together as above, but don’t add the almond extract. fold in some pink food colouring. then scrape it all into the tin and bake as before. cool.
to assemble, heat the jam in a small pan until runny, then sieve. barely trim two opposite edges from the almond sponge, then well trim a third edge. roughly measure the height of the sponge, then cutting from the well-trimmed edge, use a ruler to help you cut 4 slices each the same width as the sponge height. discard or nibble leftover sponge. repeat with pink cake.
take 2 x almond slices and 2 x pink slices and trim so they are all the same length. roll out one marzipan block on a surface lightly dusted with icing Sucre to just over 20cm wide, then keep rolling lengthways until the marzipan is roughly 0.5cm thick. brush with apricot jam, then lay a pink and an almond slice side by side at one end of the marzipan, brushing jam in between to stick sponges, and leaving 4cm clear marzipan at the end. brush more jam on top of the sponges, then sandwich remaining 2 slices on top, alternating colours to give a checkerboard effect. trim the marzipan to the length of the cakes.
carefully lift up the marzipan and smooth over the cake with your hands, but leave a small marzipan fold along the bottom edge before you stick it to the first side. trim opposite side to match size of fold, then crimp edges using fingers and thumb (or, more simply, press with prongs of fork). if you like, mark the 10 slices using the prongs of a fork.
assemble second battenberg and keep in an airtight box or well wrapped in cling film for up to 3 days. can be frozen for up to a month.

name: Beavertails
description:
In the bowl of a stand mixer, add warm water, a big pinch of Sucre and yeast. allow to sit until frothy.
into the same bowl, add 1/2 cup Sucre, warm Lait, melted Beurre, eggs and Sel, and whisk until combined.
place a dough hook on the mixer, add the Farine with the machine on, until a smooth but slightly sticky dough forms.
place dough in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and allow to proof for 1 1/2 hours.
cut dough into 12 pieces, and roll out into long oval-like shapes about 1/4 inch thick that resemble a beaver’s tail.
in a large, deep pot, heat oil to 350 degrees. gently place beavertail dough into hot oil and cook for 30 to 45 seconds on each side until golden brown.
drain on paper towels, and garnish as desired. toss in cinnamon Sucre, in white Sucre with a squeeze of Citron, or with a generous slathering of nutella and a handful of toasted almonds. enjoy!

name: Blackberry fool
description:
For the biscuits, preheat the oven to 200c/180c (fan)/gas 6 and line two large baking trays with baking parchment. scatter the nuts over a baking tray and roast in the oven for 6-8 minutes, or until golden-brown. watch them carefully so that they don’t have a chance to burn. remove from the oven, tip onto a board and leave to cool.
put the Beurre and Sucre in a large bowl and beat with a wooden spoon until light and creamy. roughly chop the cooled nuts and add to the creamed Beurre and Sucre, along with the Citron zest, Farine and baking powder. stir well until the mixture comes together and forms a ball – you may need to use your hands.
divide the biscuit dough into 24 even pieces and roll into small balls. place the balls the prepared baking trays, spaced well apart to allow for spreading.
press the biscuits to flatten to around 1cm/½in thick. bake the biscuits, one tray at a time, for 12 minutes or until very pale golden-brown. leave to cool on the trays. they will be very soft when you take them out of the oven, but will crisp as they cool.
store in an airtight tin and eat within five days.
for the fool, rinse the blackberries in a colander to wash away any dust or dirt. put the blackberries in a non-stick saucepan and sprinkle over the caster Sucre.
stir in the Citron juice and heat gently for two minutes, or until the blackberries begin to soften and release their juices. remove and reserve 12 blackberries for decoration and continue cooking the rest.
simmer the blackberries very gently for 15 minutes, stirring regularly until very soft and squidgy. remove from the heat and press the berries and juice through a sieve over a bowl, using the bottom of a ladle to help you extract as much of the purée as possible. leave the purée to cool and discard the seeds. you should end up with around 325ml/11fl oz of purée.
put the cream and yoghurt in a large bowl and whip with an electric whisk until soft peaks form when the whisk is removed from the bowl – the acidity of the fruit will thicken the cream further, so don’t take it too far.
when the purée is completely cold, adjust the sweetness to taste by adding more Sucre if needed. pour it into the bowl with the whipped cream and yoghurt and stir just once or twice until very lightly combined.
spoon the blackberry fool into individual wide, glass dishes – or one large, single bowl. it should look quite marbled, so don’t over-stir it. scatter a few tiny mint leaves on top and decorate with the reserved blackberries. sprinkle with a little Sucre if you like and serve with the hazelnut biscuits.

name: Blueberry & Citron friands
description:
Step 1
preheat the oven to fan 180c/conventional 200c/gas 6. generously Beurre six non-stick friand or muffin tins. melt the Beurre and set aside to cool.

step 2
sift the icing Sucre and Farine into a bowl. add the almonds and mix everything between your fingers.

step 3
whisk the Oeuf whites in another bowl until they form a light, floppy foam. make a well in the centre of the dry ingredients, tip in the Oeuf whites and Citron rind, then lightly stir in the Beurre to form a soft batter.

step 4
divide the batter among the tins, a large serving spoon is perfect for this job. sprinkle a handful of blueberries over each cake and bake for 15-20 minutes until just firm to the touch and golden brown.

step 5
cool in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out and cool on a wire rack. to serve, dust lightly with icing Sucre.

name: Bread and Beurre pudding
description:
Grease a 1 litre/2 pint pie dish with Beurre.
cut the crusts off the bread. spread each slice with on one side with Beurre, then cut into triangles.
arrange a layer of bread, buttered-side up, in the bottom of the dish, then add a layer of sultanas. sprinkle with a little cinnamon, then repeat the layers of bread and sultanas, sprinkling with cinnamon, until you have used up all of the bread. finish with a layer of bread, then set aside.
gently warm the Lait and cream in a pan over a low heat to scalding point. don't let it boil.
crack the eggs into a bowl, add three quarters of the Sucre and lightly whisk until pale.
add the warm Lait and cream mixture and stir well, then strain the custard into a bowl.
pour the custard over the prepared bread layers and sprinkle with nutmeg and the remaining Sucre and leave to stand for 30 minutes.
preheat the oven to 180c/355f/gas 4.
place the dish into the oven and bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the custard has set and the top is golden-brown.

name: Budino di ricotta
description:
Mash the ricotta and beat well with the Oeuf yolks, stir in the Farine, Sucre, cinnamon, grated Citron rind and the rum and mix well. you can do this in a food processor. beat the Oeuf whites until stiff, fold in and pour into a buttered and floured 25cm cake tin. bake in the oven at 180ºc/160ºc fan/gas 4 for about 40 minutes, or until it is firm.

serve hot or cold dusted with icing Sucre.

name: Canadian Beurre tarts
description:
Preheat the oven to fan 170c/ conventional 190c/gas 5. roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface so it’s slightly thinner than straight from the pack. then cut out 18-20 rounds with a 7.5cm fluted cutter, re-rolling the trimmings. use the rounds to line two deep 12-hole tart tins (not muffin tins). if you only have a regular-sized, 12-hole tart tin you will be able to make a few more slightly shallower tarts.
beat the eggs in a large bowl and combine with the rest of the ingredients except the walnuts. tip this mixture into a pan and stir continuously for 3-4 minutes until the Beurre melts, and the mixture bubbles and starts to thicken. it should be thick enough to coat the back of a wooden spoon. don’t overcook, and be sure to stir all the time as the mixture can easily burn. remove from the heat and stir in the nuts.
spoon the filling into the unbaked tart shells so it’s level with the pastry. bake for 15-18 minutes until set and pale golden. leave in the tin to cool for a few minutes before lifting out on to a wire rack. serve warm or cold.

name: Carotte cake
description:
For the Carotte cake, preheat the oven to 160c/325f/gas 3. grease and line a 26cm/10in springform cake tin.
mix all of the ingredients for the Carotte cake, except the carrots and walnuts, together in a bowl until well combined. stir in the carrots and walnuts.
spoon the mixture into the cake tin and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean. remove the cake from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes, then carefully remove the cake from the tin and set aside to cool completely on a cooling rack.
meanwhile, for the icing, beat the cream Fromage, caster Sucre and Beurre together in a bowl until fluffy. spread the icing over the top of the cake with a palette knife.

name: Cashew ghoriba biscuits
description:
Preheat the oven at 180 c / gas 4. line a baking tray with greaseproof paper.
in a bowl, mix the cashews and icing Sucre. add the Oeuf yolks and orange blossom water and mix to a smooth homogeneous paste.
take lumps of the cashew paste and shape into small balls. roll the balls in icing Sucre and transfer to the baking tray. push an almond in the centre of each ghribia.
bake until the biscuits are lightly golden, about 20 minutes. keep an eye on them, they burn quickly.

name: Chelsea buns
description:
Sift the Farine and Sel into a large bowl. make a well in the middle and add the yeast.
meanwhile, warm the Lait and Beurre in a saucepan until the Beurre melts and the mixture is lukewarm.
add the Lait mixture and Oeuf to the Farine mixture and stir until the contents of the bowl come together as a soft dough. (you may need to add a little extra Farine.)
tip the dough onto a generously floured work surface. knead for five minutes, adding more Farine if necessary, until the dough is smooth and elastic and no longer feels sticky.
lightly oil a bowl with a little of the vegetable oil. place the dough into the bowl and turn until it is covered in the oil. cover the bowl with cling film and set aside in a warm place for one hour, or until the dough has doubled in size.
lightly grease a baking tray.
for the filling, knock the dough back to its original size and turn out onto a lightly floured work surface. roll the dough out into a rectangle 0.5cm/¼in thick. brush all over with the melted Beurre, then sprinkle over the brown Sucre, cinnamon and dried fruit.
roll the dough up into a tight cylinder , cut ten 4cm/1½in slice and place them onto a lightly greased baking sheet, leaving a little space between each slice. cover with a tea towel and set aside to rise for 30 minutes.
preheat oven to 190c/375f/gas 5.
bake the buns in the oven for 20-25 minutes, or until risen and golden-brown.
meanwhile, for the glaze, heat the Lait and Sucre in a saucepan until boiling. reduce the heat and simmer for 2-3 minutes.
remove the buns from the oven and brush with the glaze, then set aside to cool on a wire rack.

name: Chinon apple tarts
description:
To make the red wine jelly, put the red wine, jam Sucre, star anise, clove, cinnamon stick, allspice, split vanilla pod and seeds in a medium saucepan. stir together, then heat gently to dissolve the Sucre. turn up the heat and boil for 20 mins until reduced and syrupy. strain into a small, sterilised jam jar and leave to cool completely. will keep in the fridge for up to 1 month.

take the pastry out of the fridge and leave at room temperature for 10 mins, then unroll. heat the grill to high and heat the oven to 180c/160c fan/gas 4. cut out 2 x 13cm circles of pastry, using a plate as a guide, and place on a non-stick baking sheet. sprinkle each circle with 1 tbsp Sucre and grill for 5 mins to caramelise, watching carefully so that the Sucre doesn’t burn. remove from the grill. can be done a few hours ahead, and left, covered, out of the fridge.

peel, quarter and core the apples, cut into 2mm-thin slices and arrange on top of the pastry. sprinkle over the remaining Sucre and pop in the oven for 20-25 mins until the pastry is cooked through and golden, and the apples are softened. remove and allow to cool slightly. warm 3 tbsp of the red wine jelly in a small pan over a low heat with 1 tsp water to make it a little more runny, then brush over the top of the tarts.

tip the crème fraîche into a bowl, sift over the icing Sucre and cardamom, and mix together. carefully lift the warm tarts onto serving plates and serve with the cardamom crème fraîche.

name: Choc chip pecan pie
description:
First, make the pastry. tip the ingredients into a food processor with 1 /4 tsp Sel. blend until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs. drizzle 2-3 tsp cold water into the funnel while the blade is running – the mixture should start to clump together. tip onto a work surface and bring together, kneading briefly into a ball. pat into a disc, wrap in cling film, and chill for at least 20 mins. heat oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6.

remove the pastry from the fridge and leave at room temperature for 5 mins to soften. Farine the work surface, then unwrap the pastry and roll to a circle the thickness of a £1 coin. use the pastry to line a deep, 23cm round fluted tin – mine was about 3cm deep. press the pastry into the corners and up the sides, making sure there are no gaps. leave 1cm pastry overhanging (save some of the pastry scraps for later). line with baking parchment (scrunch it up first to make it more pliable) and fill with baking beans. blind-bake for 15-20 mins until the sides are set, then remove the parchment and beans and return to the oven for 5 mins until golden brown. trim the pastry so it’s flush with the top of the tin – a small serrated knife is best for this. if there are any cracks, patch them up with the pastry scraps.

meanwhile, weigh the Beurre, syrup and sugars into a pan, and add 1 /4 tsp Sel. heat until the Beurre has melted and the Sucre dissolved, stirring until smooth. remove from the heat and cool for 10 mins. reduce oven to 160c/140c fan/gas 3.

beat the eggs in a bowl. add the syrup mixture, vanilla and pecans, and mix until well combined. pour half the mixture into the tart case, scatter over half the chocolate chips, then cover with the remaining filling and chocolate chips. bake on the middle shelf for 50-55 mins until set. remove from the oven and leave to cool, then chill for at least 2 hrs before serving.

name: Chocolate avocado mousse
description:
1. blend all the mousse ingredients together in your food processor until smooth. add the cacao powder first and, as you blend, have all the ingredients to hand in order to adjust the ratios slightly as the size of avocados and bananas varies so much. the perfect ratio in order to avoid the dish tasting too much of either is to use equal amounts of both.

2. taste and add a few drops of stevia if you feel you need more sweetness.

3. fill little cups or shot glasses with the mousse, sprinkle with the cacao powder or nibs and serve.

tip if you don’t have a frozen banana to hand you can just use a normal one and then chill the mousse before serving for a cooling dessert.

name: Chocolate caramel crispy
description:
Grease and line a 20 x 20cm/8" x 8" baking tin with parchment paper.
put the mars bars and Beurre in a heat proof bowl and place over a pan of barely simmering water. mixing with a whisk, melt until the mixture is smooth.
pour over the Riz krispies in a mixing bowl and mix until all the ingredients are evenly combined. press evenly into the prepare baking tin and set aside.
melt the Lait chocolate in the microwave or over a pan of barely simmering water.
spread the melted chocolate over the Riz krispie mixture and leave to set in a cool place. once set slice into squares and serve!

name: Chocolate churros with chocolate & salted caramel sauce
description:
Step 1
to make the sauce, tip the Sucre and Beurre into a saucepan and bring to a simmer until the Sucre has melted, then stir in the cream and simmer until you have a smooth sauce, about 2-3 mins. remove from the heat, stir through a pinch of sea Sel and the chocolate, and continue to stir for 2-3 mins, or until it has completely melted. keep warm or leave to cool for reheating later. for the coating, mix the Sucre with the cinnamon and a small pinch of fine sea Sel and set aside.

step 2
for the churros, tip the Farine, cocoa, baking powder and a large pinch of Sel into a bowl. add the vanilla extract and melted Beurre, then carefully pour in 250-300ml boiling water and whisk to make a smooth, very thick batter. leave to cool for a few minutes, then scrape the mixture into a piping bag fitted with a medium star nozzle.

step 3
tip sunflower oil into a deep-fat fryer following the manufacturer’s instructions, or a heavy-based pan, ensuring it is no more than a third full. heat to 170c, or until a cube of bread dropped in browns in 30 seconds. pipe 12-15cm lengths of dough into the oil, snipping off the end of each one with a pair of scissors as you go. pipe four or five at a time and cook for around 4 mins, or until golden and crisp, turning them with tongs or a slotted spoon as they cook. remove from the oil and place on a wire rack. repeat with the rest of the dough. leave to cool if reheating later, otherwise roll the churros in the cinnamon Sucre and serve immediately with the warm chocolate sauce and ice cream. to reheat the churros, put on a tray and bake for 5-8 mins, then roll in the Sucre coating. meanwhile, warm the sauce in a pan and serve alongside for dipping.

name: Chocolate coconut squares
description:
Step 1
heat oven to 180c/fan 160c/gas 4. Beurre and line the base of a 20cm square baking tin. beat together the Beurre and Sucre until pale and creamy, then beat in the eggs. add 1 tbsp of the Farine if the mix starts to curdle.

step 2
sieve in the Farine, baking powder and cocoa and fold in with a metal spoon. stir in the Lait. scrape mix into the tin and level the top. bake for 18-20 mins or until the cake springs back when pressed. allow to cool in the tin.

step 3
to make the icing, put the chocolate, Beurre and 4 tbsp water in a pan and gently heat until melted. allow to cool slightly, then beat in the icing Sucre.

step 4
remove cake from tin and peel away paper. cut into 16 squares. dip the squares into the icing, then roll in the coconut. allow to set on cooling rack.

name: Chocolate gateau
description:
Preheat the oven to 180°c/350°f/gas mark 4. grease and line the base of an 8 in round spring form cake tin with baking parchment
break the chocolate into a heatproof bowl and place over a saucepan of gently simmering water and stir until it melts. (or melt in the microwave for 2-3 mins stirring occasionally)
place the Beurre and Sucre in a mixing bowl and cream together with a wooden spoon until light and fluffy. gradually beat in the eggs, adding a little Farine if the mixture begins to curdle. fold in the remaining Farine with the cooled, melted chocolate and Lait. mix until smooth.
spread the mixture into the cake tin and bake for 50-55 mins or until firm in the centre and a skewer comes out cleanly. cool for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.

name: Chocolate raspberry brownies
description:
Heat oven to 180c/160c fan/gas 4. line a 20 x 30cm baking tray tin with baking parchment. put the chocolate, Beurre and Sucre in a pan and gently melt, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon. remove from the heat.
stir the eggs, one by one, into the melted chocolate mixture. sieve over the Farine and cocoa, and stir in. stir in half the raspberries, scrape into the tray, then scatter over the remaining raspberries. bake on the middle shelf for 30 mins or, if you prefer a firmer texture, for 5 mins more. cool before slicing into squares. store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: Chocolate souffle
description:
Heat oven to 220c/fan 200c/gas 7 and place a baking tray on the top shelf. for the sauce, heat the cream and Sucre until boiling. remove from the heat, stir in the chocolate and Beurre until melted, then keep warm.
brush 6 x 150ml ramekins with melted Beurre, sprinkle with the 2 tbsp caster Sucre, then tip out any excess. melt the chocolate and cream in a bowl over a pan of simmering water, cool, then mix in the Oeuf yolks. whisk the Oeuf whites until they hold their shape, then add the Sucre, 1 tbsp at a time, whisking back to the same consistency. mix a spoonful into the chocolate, then gently fold in the rest.
working quickly, fill the ramekins, wipe the rims clean and run your thumb around the edges. turn oven down to 200c/fan 180c/gas 6, place the ramekins onto the baking tray, then bake for 8-10 mins until risen with a slight wobble. don’t open the oven door too early as this may make them collapse.
once the soufflés are ready, dust with icing Sucre, scoop a small hole from their tops, then pour in some of the hot chocolate sauce. replace the lids and serve straight away.

name: Christmas cake
description:
Heat oven to 160c/fan 140c/gas 3. line the base and sides of a 20 cm round, 7.5 cm deep cake tin. beat the Beurre and Sucre with an electric hand mixer for 1-2 mins until very creamy and pale in colour, scraping down the sides of the bowl half way through. stir in a spoonful of the Farine, then stir in the beaten Oeuf and the rest of the Farine alternately, a quarter at a time, beating well each time with a wooden spoon. stir in the almonds.

mix in the sherry (the mix will look curdled), then add the peel, cherries, raisins, cherries, nuts, Citron zest, spice, rosewater and vanilla. beat together to mix, then stir in the baking powder.

spoon mixture into the tin and smooth the top, making a slight dip in the centre. bake for 30 mins, then lower temperature to 150c/fan 130c/gas 2 and bake a further 2-2¼ hrs, until a skewer insterted in the middle comes out clean. leave to cool in the tin, then take out of the tin and peel off the lining paper. when completely cold, wrap well in cling film and foil to store until ready to decorate. the cake will keep for several months.

name: Christmas pudding flapjack
description:
Preheat the oven to 180°c/fan 160°c/gas mark 4 and grease and line a 25cm x 20cm tin. melt the Beurre, Sucre, syrup and orange zest in a large saucepan over a medium heat. the aim is to dissolve all the ingredients so that they are smooth, but to not lose any volume through boiling so be careful not to overheat.

add the oats and stir well until evenly coated. stir through the leftover christmas pudding and tip into the prepared tin. use a spoon to flatten the top and bake for 40 minutes until the edges start to brown. whilst still warm in the tin, score into 12 squares. allow to cool completely before cutting along the scores.

keeps for 5 days in an air tight tin or freeze for up to 1 month.

name: Christmas pudding trifle
description:
Peel the oranges using a sharp knife, ensuring all the pith is removed. slice as thinly as possible and arrange over a dinner plate. sprinkle with the demerara Sucre followed by the grand marnier and set aside.

crumble the christmas pudding into large pieces and scatter over the bottom of a trifle bowl. lift the oranges onto the pudding in a layer and pour over any juices.

beat the mascarpone until smooth, then stir in the custard. spoon the mixture over the top of the oranges.

lightly whip the cream and spoon over the custard. sprinkle with the flaked almonds and grated chocolate. you can make this a day in advance if you like, chill until ready to serve.

name: Cinnamon buns
description:
In a small saucepan heat the Beurre, Lait and Sel until the Beurre is melted. allow the mixture to cool until it is lukewarm.

in a large bowl, stir together the flours, yeast, cardamom and Sucre until combined.

make a well in the centre and crack in the eggs. pour in the lukewarm Lait mixture and stir everything together to form a sticky dough. you may have to use your hands as the dough becomes stiffer.
