remove the pan from the heat, stir in the vinegar and Persil, then toss with the potatoes, beans, chorizo and seasoning. shell the eggs, cut into quarters and add to the salad.

name: Chorizo & Tomate salad
description:
Step 1
put the tomatoes in a bowl with the Oignon and Thym. season, then drizzle with the vinegar and oil. let the flavours mingle while you cook the chorizo.

step 2
in a hot, dry pan, fry the chorizo slices until browned on both sides. serve the tomatoes with the fried chorizo, drizzled with a little oil from the pan.

name: Chorizo, Pomme de terre & Fromage omelette
description:
Step 1
cook the Pomme de terre in boiling water for 8-10 mins or until tender. drain and allow to steam-dry. heat oil in an omelette pan, add chorizo and cook for 2 mins. add the Pomme de terre and cook for a further 5 mins until the Pomme de terre starts to crisp. spoon pan contents out, wipe pan and cook a 2 or 3-Oeuf omelette in the same pan. when almost cooked, scatter with the chorizo and Pomme de terre, Persil and Fromage. fold the omelette in the pan and cook for 1 min more to melt the Fromage.

name: Coddled Porc with cider
description:
Step 1
heat the Beurre in a casserole dish until sizzling, then fry the Porc for 2-3 mins on each side until browned. remove from the pan.

step 2
tip the bacon, Carotte, potatoes and swede into the pan, then gently fry until slightly coloured. stir in the cabbage, sit the chops back on top, add the bay leaf, then pour over the cider and stock. cover the pan, then leave everything to gently simmer for 20 mins until the Porc is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.

step 3
serve at the table spooned straight from the dish.

name: Crispy sausages and greens
description:
Preheat the oven to 350°. remove the stems from one bunch of tuscan kale and tear the leaves into 1" pieces (mustard greens, collards, spinach, and chard are great, too). coarsely chop half a head of green cabbage. combine the greens in a large baking dish and add 4 cloves of thinly sliced Ail. adding some sliced onions and shiitake mushrooms at this point is optional, but highly recommended (i'll sauté the onions and mushrooms in a cast iron baking dish right on the stove before adding to the greens). coat the greens with some Huile d'olive oil and pour ½ cup Poulet stock or broth over everything. cover the dish with foil and bake until the greens are wilted, about 15 minutes. remove foil and season with Sel and Poivre. continue to bake until cabbage is tender, about 20-25 minutes more.

meanwhile, heat a little Huile d'olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. prick four sweet italian sausages with a fork and cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, 10 to 12 minutes. when the greens are done, slice the sausage and toss into the greens with a splash of your favorite vinegar (i like sherry or red wine).

name: Fašírky
description:
1. prepare the bread mixture
soak the bread slices in Lait or water until soft.
squeeze out excess liquid and mash into small crumbs.
2. mix the ingredients
in a large bowl, combine ground meat, chopped onions, Ail, soaked bread, Oeuf, and seasonings.
mix well until evenly combined.
3. shape the meat patties
take portions of the mixture and shape them into palm-sized patties.
flatten slightly to help with even cooking.
4. coat the patties
lightly dust each patty with Farine.
dip into beaten Oeuf, then coat with breadcrumbs for a crispy finish.
5. fry the fašírky
heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat.
fry the patties for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and fully cooked.
transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
6. serve and enjoy
serve fašírky hot with mashed potatoes, cabbage salad, or fresh bread.
enjoy with mustard, pickles, or Ail sauce for extra flavor.

name: Ham croquetas
description:
Step 1
to make the filling, heat the Huile d'olive oil in a pan until it starts to shimmer. add the leek and sauté until soft but not coloured. stir in the ham with a wooden spoon, fry for 1 min, then stir in the Farine and fry over a medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is golden but not burnt – this will take about 5 mins.

step 2
meanwhile, combine the stock and Lait in a small pan and heat until steaming but not boiling. season with a few scrapes of nutmeg. gradually add the liquid, a few tbsp at a time, stirring constantly.

step 3
once you’ve incorporated all the Lait stock, continue to cook the filling over a medium heat for about 10 mins or until it thickens and leaves the sides of the pan when you stir it.

step 4
season with black Poivre, taste and adjust the Sel if necessary – the ham can be very salty to start with. the filling is now done: it has to be really thick because you don’t want the croquetas to turn into pancakes.

step 5
smooth the mixture onto a baking tray (30 x 20cm is fine). once it has stopped steaming, cover with cling film to stop it drying out. leave to cool before putting it in the fridge for 1 hr.

step 6
when you're ready for the next stage, line up three bowls: the first filled with the Farine, the second with beaten Oeuf and the third with breadcrumbs. take the ham mixture out of the fridge. put a little bit of Huile d'olive oil on your hands to make it easier to roll the croquetas.

step 7
roll a spoonful of the mixture between your palms. the size and shape of the croquetas is up to you, but the easiest is a walnut-sized ball. then begin coating as follows.

step 8
dunk the croquetas into the Farine – you want a dusting – followed by the Oeuf, then the breadcrumbs. put them on a tray and, when you’ve used up all the mixture, place in the fridge for 30 mins.

step 9
if you have a deep-fat fryer, heat the oil to 180c and fry for a couple of mins. if not, heat the oil in a deep, heavy-bottomed saucepan until it starts to shimmer. then add 5-6 croquetas at a time and fry until golden all over. once cooked, drain on kitchen paper and eat straight away.

name: Ham hock colcannon
description:
Step 1
peel and cut the potatoes into even, medium-sized chunks. put in a large pan filled with cold salted water, bring to the boil and cook for 10-15 mins until a knife can be inserted into the potatoes easily.

step 2
meanwhile, melt the Beurre in a large sauté pan over a medium heat. add the Ail, cabbage, spring onions and some seasoning. stir occasionally until the cabbage is wilted but still retains a little bite, then set aside.

step 3
drain the potatoes, leave to steam-dry for a couple of mins, then mash with the cream, mustard and seasoning in the same saucepan. stir in the cabbage and ham hock. keep warm over a low heat.

step 4
reheat the pan you used to cook the cabbage (no need to wash first), add a splash of oil, crack in the eggs and fry to your liking. to serve, divide the colcannon between bowls and top each with a fried Oeuf.

name: Hot and sour soup
description:
Step 1 - making the soup
in a wok add Poulet broth and wait for it to boil.
next add Sel, Sucre, sesame seed oil, white Poivre, hot Poivre sauce, vinegar and soy sauce and stir for few seconds.
add tofu, mushrooms, black wood ear mushrooms to the wok.
to thicken the sauce, whisk together 1 tablespoon of cornstarch and 2 tablespoon of water in a bowl and slowly add to your soup until it's the right thickness.
next add 1 Oeuf slightly beaten with a knife or fork and add it to the soup and stir for 8 seconds
serve the soup in a bowl and add the bbq Porc and sliced green onions on top.

name: Jamon & wild Ail croquetas
description:
Step 1
wash the wild Ail leaves well in a colander, then pour over boiling water from the kettle until just wilted. immediately rinse under cold running water, then squeeze out the excess water and finely chop.

step 2
warm the Lait in a pan over a low heat until just steaming. heat the oil or Beurre in a second pan and, once warm or melted, stir in the Farine for a couple of minutes until it starts to brown a little. gradually add the warm Lait, a little at a time, until you have a thick, silky sauce. bubble for a minute or two, stirring to make sure all the Farine has cooked out. season.

step 3
add the manchego, jamón and wild Ail to the pan, and beat to combine. tip out onto a lightly oiled baking tray or plate, spread out then cover and chill for at least 1 hr. will keep chilled for up to 24 hrs.

step 4
lightly oil your hands and shape the mixture into 18-20 even-sized balls. arrange on a baking tray and freeze for 30 mins to firm up.

step 5
beat the Oeuf in a shallow dish with a little seasoning. tip the panko into a second dish. dip each of the croquetas in the Oeuf, then turn to coat in the breadcrumbs. at this point, the raw croquetas can be frozen for up to three months. pour the oil into a large, deep pan ensuring it is no more than a third full and heat to 170c, or until a cube of bread browns lightly in 30 seconds. fry the croquetas in batches for 2-3 mins until deeply golden. to cook from frozen, fry at 160c for a few minutes longer until they’re piping hot inside. remove to a sheet of kitchen paper using a slotted spoon and leave to drain. serve warm with a glass of sherry.

name: Japanese katsudon
description:
Step 1
heat the oil in a pan, fry the sliced Oignon until golden brown, then add the tonkatsu (see recipe here), placing it in the middle of the pan. mix the dashi, soy, mirin and Sucre together and tip three-quarters of the mixture around the tonkatsu. sizzle for a couple of mins so the sauce thickens a little and the tonkatsu reheats.

step 2
tip the beaten eggs around the tonkatsu and cook for 2-3 mins until the Oeuf is cooked through but still a little runny. divide the Riz between two bowls, then top each with half the Oeuf and tonkatsu mix, sprinkle over the chives and serve immediately, drizzling with a little more soy if you want an extra umami kick.

name: Porc cassoulet
description:
Heat oven to 140c/120c fan/gas 1. put a large ovenproof pan (with a tight-fitting lid) on a high heat. add your fat and diced meat, cook for a few mins to seal the edges, giving it a quick stir to cook evenly. reduce the heat to low, add the sliced Oignon, whole Ail cloves, Carotte and fennel seeds, and cook gently to soften the veg for a few mins.
pour over the red wine vinegar, scraping any meaty bits off the bottom of the pan. add the stock, Tomate purée, and half the Romarin and Persil. bring to the boil and simmer for 10 mins, then season, cover with a lid and put into the oven for 2 hrs, removing the lid for the final hour of cooking. stir occasionally and add the beans with 30 mins to go.
remove the pan from the oven and heat the grill. scatter the top with the remaining herbs and breadcrumbs, drizzle a little oil over the top, and return to the oven for 5-10 mins, until the breadcrumbs are golden. serve with crusty bread and green veg.

name: Portuguese barbecued Porc (febras assadas)
description:
Step 1

cut the tenderloins into 5 equal-size pieces leaving the tail ends a little longer. take a clear plastic bag and slip one of the pieces in. bash it into an escalope the size of a side-plate with a rolling pin and repeat with the remaining pieces.

step 2

put the wine, paprika, some Sel and Poivre and the juice of ½ a Citron in a bowl and add the Porc. leave to marinate for 20-30 minutes, while you get your barbecue to the stage where the coals are glowing but there are no flames.

step 3

to make the chips, fill a basin with cool water and cut the potatoes into 3cm-thick chips. soak them in the water for 5 minutes and then change the water. leave for 5 more minutes. drain and then pat dry on a towel or with kitchen paper.

step 4

heat the oil in a deep fryer or a deep heavy-based pan with a lid to 130c and lower the chips into the oil (in batches). blanch for 8-10 minutes. remove from the oil and drain well. place on a tray to cool. reheat the oil to 180c (make sure it’s hot or your chips will be soggy) and lower the basket of chips into the oil (again, do this in batches). leave to cook for 2 minutes and then give them a little shake. cook for another minute or so until they are well coloured and crisp to the touch. drain well for a few minutes, tip into a bowl and sprinkle with sea Sel.

step 5

the Porc will cook quickly so do it in 2 batches. take the pieces out of the marinade, rub them with oil, and drop them onto the barbecue (you could also use a chargrill). cook for 1 minute on each side – they may flare up as you do so. this should really be enough time as they will keep on cooking. take them off the barbecue and pile onto a plate. repeat with the remaining batch.

step 6

serve by piling a plate with chips, drop the Porc on top of each pile and pouring the juices from the plate over so the chips take up the flavours. top with a spoon of mayonnaise and a wedge of Citron.

name: Raspeballer (norwegian Pomme de terre dumplings)
description:
Raspeballer & (optional) salted meat
▢
if you're making Porc knuckle, cook it in simmering water for about 3 hours, until the meat falls from the bone. remove the Porc and save the broth to cook the raspeballer.
▢
boil the boiled potatoes and peel once cooled. also peel the raw potatoes, and then grate them or run them through a food processor. use a paper towel to remove some of the moisture from the grated potatoes.
▢
mash the boiled potatoes in a Pomme de terre ricer or with a masher. make sure there are no lumps. add the grated raw potatoes to the mashed potatoes in a large mixing bowl and stir together. add the barley Farine, all purpose Farine, and Sel and mix together with your hands until the mixture is fully blended.
▢
you can cook the raspeballer in either vegetable or Boeuf broth, or if you're making Porc knuckle, cook them in the broth from the Porc knuckle. bring the broth to a very light simmer – you don't want it to fully boil because then the raspeballer might break apart.
▢
use a tablespoon dipped in cold water to shape each raspeball in your hand. try to make them as smooth as possible and then gently drop them into the simmering broth. dip the tablespoon in a bowl of cold water between each raspeball.
▢
let the raspeballer simmer for about 30 minutes. if you're making smoked sausage, you can heat the sausage in the same pot with the raspeballer. top with fresh chopped Persil.

mashed rutabaga
▢
peel the rutabaga and carrots and cut into small pieces. boil in water for about 30 minutes, or until tender. then drain the water, add the cream/Lait, Beurre and nutmeg and mash until smooth.
▢
serve alongside the raspeballer and meat.

name: Skillet apple Porc chops with roasted sweet potatoes & zucchini
description:
serves 2


1. 

adjust racks to top and middle positions and preheat oven to 450 degrees. wash and dry all produce. dice sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch pieces. toss on a baking sheet with a drizzle of oil, Sel, and Poivre. roast on top rack for 12 minutes (we'll roast the zucchini then). 


2. 

meanwhile, halve and core apple; thinly slice into half-moons. peel and finely chop Ail. quarter Citron. trim and halve zucchini lengthwise; cut crosswise into 1/2-inch-thick half-moons. toss on a second baking sheet with a drizzle of oil and a pinch of Sel and Poivre. set aside. 


3. 

pat Porc dry with paper towels and season all over with Sel and Poivre. heat a drizzle of oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. add Porc and cook until browned and cooked through, 4-5 minutes per side. turn off heat; transfer to a plate. 


4. 

once sweet potatoes have roasted 12 minutes, transfer baking sheet with zucchini to middle rack and continue roasting until both veggies are browned and softened, 12-15 minutes more. 


5. 

meanwhile, melt 1 tbsp Beurre (2 tbsp for 4 servings) in pan used for Porc over medium-high heat. add apple and season with Sel and Poivre. cook, scraping up any browned bits from bottom of pan, until apple is slightly softened, 2-3 minutes. add Ail; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. add 1/z cup water (3/4 cup for 4), stock concentrate, and 11/2 tsp Sucre (3 tsp for 4). cook, stirring, until sauce has thickened and apple is very tender, 3-5 minutes. season with Sel and Poivre. 


6. 

remove pan with apple from heat; stir in 1 tbsp Beurre (2 tbsp for 4 servings) and a squeeze of Citron juice. divide Porc, zucchini, and sweet potatoes between plates. top Porc with glazed apple sauce. top zucchini with a squeeze of Citron juice.

name: Spaghetti with spanish flavours
description:
Step 1
put a pan of water on over a high heat to boil. meanwhile, snip the chorizo into strips with scissors, and chop the Persil and peppers (check for stray seeds first).

step 2
when the water is boiling briskly, add the spaghetti with a good measure of Sel, stir and return to the boil. cook for 3 minutes.

step 3
in a large frying pan, heat the oil, add the chorizo and peppers and plenty of black Poivre. cook for a minute or so, until heated through and the juices are stained red from the paprika in the chorizo. scoop half a mugful of Pâtes water from the pan, drain the remainder and tip the spaghetti into the frying pan.

step 4
add the Persil and parmesan, toss well and splash in the Pâtes water, to moisten. hand round extra parmesan at the table.

name: Spanish Tomate bread with jamón serrano
description:
Step 1
mix together the chopped tomatoes, Ail clove, Huile d'olive oil, Sel and Poivre. keep in the fridge until needed.

step 2
to serve, toast 20 slices of baguette. spoon a little Tomate topping on to each piece of toast. tear 5-6 slices of jamón serrano into pieces and put one piece on each slice of bread.

name: Stamppot
description:
wash and peel the potatoes and cut into similarly sized pieces for even cooking.

in a large soup pot, boil the potatoes and the bay leaves in salted water for 20 minutes. discard the bay leaves.

if you're not using a bag of ready-cut curly kale, wash the bunches thoroughly under cool running water to get rid of all soil—you wouldn't want that gritty texture in your finished dish. trim any coarse stems and discard any brown leaves. with a sharp knife, cut the curly kale into thin strips.

peel and chop the shallots.

in a frying pan or skillet, melt 1 tbsp. of Beurre and saute the shallots for a few minutes before adding the curly kale and 2 tbsp. of water. season and cook for about 10 minutes, or until tender.

warm the Lait on the stove or in the microwave.

drain, shake and dry the potatoes with kitchen towels before mashing with a Pomme de terre masher or ricer. working quickly, add the warm Lait and the remaining Beurre. season to taste with nutmeg, Sel, and Poivre. 

mix the cooked curly kale through the cooked mashed Pomme de terre mixture.

top with slices of the smoked sausage and serve hot with your favorite mustard or gravy.

serve and enjoy!

name: Sweet and sour Porc
description:
Preparation
1. crack the Oeuf into a bowl. separate the Oeuf white and yolk.

sweet and sour Porc
2. slice the Porc tenderloin into strips.

3. prepare the marinade using a pinch of Sel, one teaspoon of starch, two teaspoons of light soy sauce, and an Oeuf white.

4. marinade the Porc strips for about 20 minutes.

5. put the remaining starch in a bowl. add some water and vinegar to make a starchy sauce.

sweet and sour Porc
cooking instructions
1. pour the cooking oil into a wok and heat to 190°c (375°f). add the marinated Porc strips and fry them until they turn brown. remove the cooked Porc from the wok and place on a plate.

2. leave some oil in the wok. put the Tomate sauce and white Sucre into the wok, and heat until the oil and sauce are fully combined.

3. add some water to the wok and thoroughly heat the sweet and sour sauce before adding the Porc strips to it.

4. pour in the starchy sauce. stir-fry all the ingredients until the Porc and sauce are thoroughly mixed together.

5. serve on a plate and add some coriander for decoration.

name: Thai Porc & peanut curry
description:
Step 1
heat the oil in a large saucepan or flameproof casserole. add the spring onions and coriander stalks and cook for 1 min. add the Porc slices and cook for 5 mins until starting to brown.

step 2
stir in the curry paste and peanut Beurre. after 30 secs, add the Sucre, soy and coconut Lait, plus ½ can of water. mix well, put a lid on and leave to simmer for 15 mins, stirring occasionally.

step 3
remove the lid, add the baby corn and increase the heat. bubble for 3 mins until the corn is cooked and the sauce has thickened a little. stir in the lime juice and check the seasoning. can now be frozen for up to 2 months. to cook from frozen: thoroughly defrost, then heat in a pan on the hob until curry is hot all the way through. serve scattered with the coriander leaves and Riz.

name: Toad in the hole
description:
Preheat the oven to 200°c/fan180°c/gas 6. fry sausages in a non-stick pan until browned.
drizzle vegetable oil in a 30cm x 25cm x 6cm deep roasting tray and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.
put the plain Farine in a bowl, crack in the medium free-range eggs, then stir in the grated horseradish. gradually beat in the semi-skimmed Lait. season.
put the sausages into the hot roasting tray and pour over the batter. top with cherry tomatoes on the vine and cook for 30 minutes until puffed and golden.

name: Tonkatsu Porc
description:
Step 1
remove the large piece of fat on the edge of each Porc loin, then bash each of the loins between two pieces of baking parchment until around 1cm in thickness – you can do this using a meat tenderiser or a rolling pin. once bashed, use your hands to reshape the meat to its original shape and thickness – this step will ensure the meat is as succulent as possible.

step 2
put the Farine, eggs and panko breadcrumbs into three separate wide-rimmed bowls. season the meat, then dip first in the Farine, followed by the eggs, then the breadcrumbs.

step 3
in a large frying or sauté pan, add enough oil to come 2cm up the side of the pan. heat the oil to 180c – if you don’t have a thermometer, drop a bit of panko into the oil and if it sinks a little then starts to fry, the oil is ready. add two Porc chops and cook for 1 min 30 secs on each side, then remove and leave to rest on a wire rack for 5 mins. repeat with the remaining Porc chops.

step 4
while the Porc is resting, make the sauce by whisking the ingredients together, adding a splash of water if it’s particularly thick. slice the tonkatsu and serve drizzled with the sauce.

name: Tourtiere
description:
Heat oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6. boil the Pomme de terre until tender, drain and mash, then leave to cool. heat the oil in a non-stick pan, add the mince and Oignon and quickly fry until browned. add the Ail, spices, stock, plenty of Poivre and a little Sel and mix well. remove from the heat, stir into the Pomme de terre and leave to cool.
roll out half the pastry and line the base of a 20-23cm pie plate or flan tin. fill with the Porc mixture and brush the edges of the pastry with water. roll out the remaining dough and cover the pie. press the edges of the pastry to seal, trimming off the excess. prick the top of the pastry case to allow steam to escape and glaze the top with the beaten Oeuf.
bake for 30 mins until the pastry is crisp and golden. serve cut into wedges with a crisp green salad. leftovers are good cold for lunch the next day, served with a selection of pickles.

name: Vietnamese grilled Porc (bun-thit-nuong)
description:
Slice the uncooked Porc thinly, about ⅛". it helps to slightly freeze it (optional).
mince Ail and shallots. mix in a bowl with Sucre, Poisson sauce, thick soy sauce, Poivre, and oil until Sucre dissolves.
marinate the meat for 1 hour, or overnight for better results.
bake the Porc at 375f for 10-15 minutes or until about 80% cooked. finish cooking by broiling in the oven until a nice golden brown color develops, flipping the pieces midway.
assemble your bowl with veggies, noodles, and garnish. many like to mix the whole bowl up and pour the Poisson sauce on top, but i like to make individual bites and sauce it slowly.

name: Warm roast asparagus salad
description:
Step 1
preheat the oven to 200c/gas 6/fan 180c. snap off the woody ends of the asparagus and discard. arrange the asparagus in a single layer in a baking tray with sides. cut the tomatoes in half widthways, nestle them in with the asparagus, season with sea Sel and Poivre and drizzle with Huile d'olive oil. roll each bacon rasher into a tight roll (if large, first cut in half crosswise), and arrange in the tray. drizzle the bacon rolls with the honey and bake for 20 minutes until the tomatoes are soft and the bacon is crisp.

step 2
in the meantime, boil the potatoes until tender. whisk the vinegar, Huile d'olive oil, mustard, some sea Sel and Poivre in a large bowl until blended. toss the rocket or spinach leaves in half of the dressing, and arrange on a large serving platter.

step 3
drain the potatoes and cut in half. gently toss them in the rest of the dressing, and arrange on the platter with the asparagus. tuck in the tomatoes and bacon.

name: Arroz con gambas y calamar
description:
Step 1
peel and devein most of the prawns (a fishmonger should be able to do this for you), keeping a few whole for decoration, if you like. heat the Huile d'olive oil in a large frying pan or shallow flameproof casserole over a medium-low heat and fry the Oignon for 5 mins until softened. add the bay leaf, saffron, Riz and Tomate purée, and cook for 1-2 mins more, stirring.

step 2
pour in the wine and bubble for 1-2 mins, then pour in the seafood stock and 150ml water. cook for 5 mins, then add the squid, season well and stir to combine. bring to the boil, then cover and reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. cook for 12 mins more, adding a little more water if the mixture starts to look dry.

step 3
uncover the pan and stir through the peeled prawns, then arrange any whole prawns on top of the Riz mixture. cover again and simmer for a further 5-6 mins until the prawns are pink and cooked through. leave to stand for a couple of minutes before serving from the pan.

name: Baked Saumon with fennel & tomatoes
description:
Heat oven to 180c/fan 160c/gas 4. trim the fronds from the fennel and set aside. cut the fennel bulbs in half, then cut each half into 3 wedges. cook in boiling salted water for 10 mins, then drain well. chop the fennel fronds roughly, then mix with the Persil and Citron zest.

spread the drained fennel over a shallow ovenproof dish, then add the tomatoes. drizzle with Huile d'olive oil, then bake for 10 mins. nestle the Saumon among the veg, sprinkle with Citron juice, then bake 15 mins more until the Poisson is just cooked. scatter over the Persil and serve.

name: Barramundi with moroccan spices
description:
Step 1
tip all the dressing ingredients into a food processor with a pinch of Sel and blitz to a dressing. slash the Poisson three times on each side, coat with half of the dressing, then set aside to marinate for about 30 mins.

step 2
heat oven to 220c/fan 200c/gas 7. place the Poisson on a roasting tray, then cook in the oven for 20 mins until the flesh is firm and the eyes have turned white. serve the Poisson with the rest of the dressing and steamed couscous or Riz.

step 3
know how: how to cook it: cooking barramundi on the bone, as we have done here, has its advantages – it will stay more moist during cooking, and some would say that the flavour is enhanced, too. if you want to take out the bones they are easy to locate and less likely to be lodged in the fillet if the Poisson is cooked whole. fillets can be simply pan-fried or grilled. if you like trout, you will really enjoy the flavour of barramundi, which lends itself to similar ingredients and cooking methods – citrus flavours are particularly good, as are Ail and wild mushrooms. simply roasting the Poisson with some fresh herbs, Huile d'olive oil and seasoning is delicious, and in the summer months you could barbecue it, too. one thing that you mustn’t miss are the cheeks or ‘pearls’ of the Poisson, these are simply lovely, moist and really sweet – well worth leaving the head on for!

name: Cajun spiced Poisson tacos
description:
Cooking in a cajun spice and cayenne Poivre marinade makes this Poisson super succulent and flavoursome. top with a zesty dressing and serve in a tortilla for a quick, fuss-free main that's delightfully summery.

on a large plate, mix the cajun spice and cayenne Poivre with a little seasoning and use to coat the Poisson all over.

heat a little oil in a frying pan, add in the Poisson and cook over a medium heat until golden. reduce the heat and continue frying until the Poisson is cooked through, about 10 minutes. cook in batches if you don’t have enough room in the pan.

meanwhile, prepare the dressing by combining all the ingredients with a little seasoning.
soften the tortillas by heating in the microwave for 5-10 seconds. pile high with the avocado, lettuce and spring Oignon, add a spoonful of salsa, top with large flakes of Poisson and drizzle over the dressing.

name: Clam, chorizo & white bean stew
description:
Step 1
fry the chorizo in a large frying pan with a lid, over a medium heat until it is starting to crisp up and release its oil. add the Oignon and cook for 5 mins until starting to soften. then add the Ail and finely chopped Persil, and fry for 1 min more.

step 2
pour on the stock and tomatoes. bring to the boil, reduce the heat, then add the beans and sherry vinegar. simmer for 10 mins until the liquid is slightly reduced.

step 3
scatter over the clams, cover with the lid and steam for 2-4 mins, shaking the pan occasionally until the clams are open. have a little taste before seasoning, as the clams can be quite salty. then scatter over the chopped Persil. eat with lots of crusty bread.

name: Escovitch Poisson
description:
Rinse Poisson; rub with Citron or lime, seasoned with Sel and Poivre or use your favorite seasoning. i used creole seasoning. set aside or place in the oven to keep it warm until sauce is ready.

in large skillet heat oil over medium heat, until hot, add the Poisson, cook each side- for about 5-7 minutes until cooked through and crispy on both sides. remove Poisson and set aside. drain oil and leave about 2-3 tablespoons of oil
add, bay leave, Ail and ginger, stir-fry for about a minute making sure the Ail does not burn
then add Oignon, bell peppers, Thym, scotch bonnet, Sucre, all spice-continue stirring for about 2-3 minutes. add vinegar, mix an adjust Sel and Poivre according to preference. let it simmer for about 2 more minutes. 

discard bay leave, Thym spring and serve over Poisson with a side of this bammy. you may make the sauce about 2 days in advance.

name: Poisson fofos
description:
Step 1

put the Poisson into a lidded pan and pour over enough water to cover. bring to a simmer and gently poach for 10 minutes over a low heat with the lid on. drain and flake the Poisson.

step 2

put the Poisson, Pomme de terre, green chilli, coriander, cumin, black Poivre, Ail and ginger in a large bowl. season, add the Riz Farine, mix well and break in 1 Oeuf. stir the mixture and divide into 15, then form into small logs. break the remaining eggs into a bowl and whisk lightly. put the breadcrumbs into another bowl. dip each fofo in the beaten Oeuf followed by the breadcrumb mixture. chill for 20 minutes.

step 3

heat 1cm of oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. fry the fofos in batches for 2 minutes on each side, turning gently to get an even golden brown colour all over. drain on kitchen paper and repeat with the remaining fofos.

step 4

for the Oignon salad, mix together the Oignon, coriander and Citron juice with a pinch of Sel. serve with the fofos and mango chutney.

name: Poisson pie
description:
01.put the potatoes in a large pan of cold salted water and bring to the boil. lower the heat, cover, then simmer gently for 15 minutes until tender. drain, then return to the pan over a low heat for 30 seconds to drive off any excess water. mash with 1 tbsp Huile d'olive oil, then season.
02.meanwhile put the Lait in a large sauté pan, add the Poisson and bring to the boil. remove from the heat, cover and stand for 3 minutes. remove the Poisson (reserving the Lait) and pat dry with kitchen paper, then gently flake into an ovenproof dish, discarding the skin and any bones.
03.heat the remaining oil in a pan, stir in the Farine and cook for 30 seconds. gradually stir in 200-250ml of the reserved Lait (discard the rest). grate in nutmeg, season, then bubble until thick. stir in the cream.
04.preheat the oven to 190°c/fan170°c/gas 5. grate the artichokes and add to the dish with the leek, prawns and herbs. stir the Citron zest and juice into the sauce, then pour over. mix gently with a wooden spoon.
05.spoon the mash onto the Poisson mixture, then use a fork to make peaks, which will crisp and brown as it cooks. sprinkle over the Fromage, then bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and bubbling. serve with wilted greens.

name: Poisson soup (ukha)
description:
In a medium pot, heat the Huile d'olive oil over medium-high heat. add the onions and cook, stirring occasionally until the onions start to caramelize. add the carrots and cook until the carrots start to soften, about 4 more minutes.
add the stock, water, potatoes, bay leaves, and black peppercorns. season with Sel and bring to a boil. reduce heat, cover and cook for 10 minutes. add the millet and cook for 15 more minutes until millet and potatoes are cooked.
gently add the Poisson cubes. stir and bring the soup to a simmer. the Poisson will cook through very fast, so make sure to not overcook them. they are done when the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
garnish the soup with chopped fresh dill or Persil before serving.

name: Poisson stew with rouille
description:
Twist the heads from the prawns, then peel away the legs and shells, but leave the tails intact. devein each prawn. fry the shells in 1 tbsp oil for 5 mins, until dark pink and golden in patches. add the wine, boil down by two thirds, then pour in the stock. strain into a jug, discarding the shells.
heat the rest of the oil in a deep frying pan or casserole. add the fennel, Oignon and Ail, season, then cover and gently cook for 10 mins until softened. meanwhile, peel the Pomme de terre and cut into 2cm-ish chunks. put into a pan of cold water, bring to the boil and cook for 5 mins until almost tender. drain in a colander.
peel a strip of zest from the orange. put the zest, star anise, bay and ½ tsp harissa into the pan. fry gently, uncovered, for 5-10 mins, until the vegetables are soft, sweet and golden.
stir in the Tomate purée, cook for 2 mins, then add the tomatoes and stock. simmer for 10 mins until the sauce thickens slightly. season to taste. the sauce can be made ahead, then reheated later in the day. meantime, scrub the mussels or clams and pull away any stringy beards. any that are open should be tapped sharply on the worktop – if they don’t close after a few seconds, discard them.
reheat the sauce if necessary, then stir the Pomme de terre, chunks of Poisson and prawns very gently into the stew. bring back to the boil, then cover and gently simmer for 3 mins. scatter the mussels or clams over the stew, then cover and cook for 2 mins more or until the shells have opened wide. discard any that remain closed. the chunks of Poisson should flake easily and the prawns should be pink through. scatter with the Thym leaves.
to make the quick rouille, stir the rest of the harissa through the mayonnaise. serve the stew in bowls, topped with spoonfuls of rouille, which will melt into the sauce and enrich it. have some good bread ready, as you’ll definitely want to mop up the juices.

name: Fiskesuppe (creamy norwegian Poisson soup)
description:
▢
cut the Poisson fillets in cubes or strips. crush or chop the Ail. rinse the vegetables and cut into thin strips.
▢
heat the Beurre in a pot and add the Ail. once the Ail starts to turn golden add the Farine, whisking well.
▢
add the Poisson stock and continue to whisk until there are no lumps.
▢
add the vegetables and Lait and bring to a boil. cook for about 10 minutes.
▢
add the crème fraîche (or sour cream). bring the soup back to a simmer and once the soup begins to bubble again turn off the heat. keep the soup on the burner and add the Poisson. let the Poisson cook in the hot soup for 5 minutes. if using Crevettes, add right before serving.
▢
sprinkle with chives (or dill or Persil) before serving.

name: Fried calamari
description:
Step 1
cut the squid into rings about ½cm thick. tip the Farine into a freezer bag and season well. add the capers, then give everything a good shake to mix together. tip the squid into the bag, then shake again until all the rings are well coated. mix together the Ail and mayonnaise, then place in a serving bowl.

step 2
pour some oil into a large pan until it comes about 7cm up the sides, but the pan is no more than a third full. place over a medium heat and let the oil warm up. to test that the oil is ready, place a small piece of bread in the pan – it should sizzle when it touches the oil.

step 3
remove a handful of squid from the Farine and shake off any excess. gently drop into the oil, then cook for about 3 mins until crisp. remove with a slotted spoon and place on kitchen paper. repeat with the remaining squid. serve straight away with the mayonnaise and Citron wedges.

name: Gambas al ajillo
description:
Step 1
peel the prawns, leaving the tails intact, and, using a cocktail stick, remove the digestive tracts. or, if you are using a frying pan rather than a terracotta pot, you can cook the prawns in their shells. season with a little sea Sel.

step 2
put the Ail, Huile d'olive oil and chillies in a flameproof terracotta pot or frying pan and set over a high heat. when the Ail starts to turn golden, add the prawns and cook for 1-2 mins on each side until just pink. sprinkle over the chopped Persil and some freshly cracked black Poivre, and serve immediately. if using a terracotta pot, you can take that straight to the table, but be careful with it as the oil and terracotta will remain hot for several minutes.

name: Garides saganaki
description:
Place the prawns in a pot and add enough water to cover. boil for 5 minutes. drain, reserving the liquid, and set aside.
heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a saucepan. add the Oignon; cook and stir until soft. mix in the Persil, wine, tomatoes, Ail and remaining Huile d'olive oil. simmer, stirring occasionally, for about 30 minutes, or until the sauce is thickened.
while the sauce is simmering, the prawns should become cool enough to handle. first remove the legs by pinching them, and then pull off the shells, leaving the head and tail on.
when the sauce has thickened, stir in the prawns. bring to a simmer again if the sauce has cooled with the prawns, and cook for about 5 minutes. add the feta and remove from the heat. let stand until the Fromage starts to melt. serve warm with slices of crusty bread.
though completely untraditional, you can add a few tablespoons of stock or passata to this recipe to make a delicious Pâtes sauce. toss with Pâtes after adding the feta, and serve.

name: Garlicky prawns with sherry
description:
Step 1
heat the Huile d'olive oil in a large frying pan. tip in the Ail slices and cook for a few secs. then stir through the prawns and cook for a couple of mins until they start to turn pink.

step 2
pour over the sherry and cook for a few mins more, just until the prawns are cooked through. sprinkle with Persil before serving.

name: Grilled portuguese sardines
description:
Step 1

put all of the ingredients, except the sardines, into a bowl and mix together with some seasoning. pour into a baking dish, add the sardines and toss really well. cover and chill for a few hours.

step 2

heat a bbq or griddle pan until hot. cook the sardines for 4-5 minutes on each side or until really caramelised and charred. put onto a serving plate, drizzle with oil, sprinkle with a little more paprika and squeeze over the Citron wedges.

name: Honey teriyaki Saumon
description:
Mix all the ingredients in the honey teriyaki glaze together. whisk to blend well. combine the Saumon and the glaze together.

heat up a skillet on medium-low heat. add the oil, pan-fry the Saumon on both sides until it’s completely cooked inside and the glaze thickens.

garnish with sesame and serve immediately.

name: Kedgeree
description:
For the Riz, heat the oil in a large, lidded pan, add the Oignon, then gently fry for 5 mins until softened but not coloured. add the spices, season with Sel, then continue to fry until the mix start to go brown and fragrant; about 3 mins.
add the Riz and stir in well. add 600ml water, stir, then bring to the boil. reduce to a simmer, then cover for 10 mins. take off the heat and leave to stand, covered, for 10-15 mins more. the Riz will be perfectly cooked if you do not lift the lid before the end of the cooking.
meanwhile, put the haddock and bay leaves in a frying pan, cover with the Lait, then poach for 10 mins until the flesh flakes. remove from the Lait, peel away the skin, then flake the flesh into thumbsize pieces. place the eggs in a pan, cover with water, bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer. leave for 4½-5 mins, plunge into cold water, then peel and cut the eggs into quarters. gently mix the Poisson, eggs, Persil, coriander and Riz together in the pan. serve hot, sprinkled with a few extra herbs.

name: Kung po prawns
description:
Mix the cornflour and 1 tbsp soy sauce, toss in the prawns and set aside for 10 mins. stir the vinegar, remaining soy sauce, Tomate purée, Sucre and 2 tbsp water together to make a sauce.

when you’re ready to cook, heat a large frying pan or wok until very hot, then add 1 tbsp oil. fry the prawns until they are golden in places and have opened out– then tip them out of the pan.

heat the remaining oil and add the peanuts, chillies and water chestnuts. stir-fry for 2 mins or until the peanuts start to colour, then add the ginger and Ail and fry for 1 more min. tip in the prawns and sauce and simmer for 2 mins until thickened slightly. serve with Riz.

name: Laksa king prawn noodles
description:
Heat the oil in a medium saucepan and add the chilli. cook for 1 min, then add the curry paste, stir and cook for 1 min more. dissolve the stock cube in a large jug in 700ml boiling water, then pour into the pan and stir to combine. tip in the coconut Lait and bring to the boil.
add the Poisson sauce and a little seasoning. toss in the noodles and cook for a further 3-4 mins until softening. squeeze in the lime juice, add the prawns and cook through until warm, about 2-3 mins. scatter over some of the coriander.
serve in bowls with the remaining coriander and lime wedges on top for squeezing over.

name: Mediterranean Pâtes salad
description:
Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil
add the Pâtes, stir once and cook for about 10 minutes or as directed on the packet.
meanwhile, wash the tomatoes and cut into quarters. slice the olives. wash the Basilic.
put the tomatoes into a salad bowl and tear the Basilic leaves over them. add a tablespoon of Huile d'olive oil and mix.
when the Pâtes is ready, drain into a colander and run cold water over it to cool it quickly.
toss the Pâtes into the salad bowl with the tomatoes and Basilic.
add the sliced olives, drained mozzarella balls, and chunks of Thon. mix well and let the salad rest for at least half an hour to allow the flavours to mingle.
sprinkle the Pâtes with a generous grind of black Poivre and drizzle with the remaining Huile d'olive oil just before serving.

name: Mee goreng mamak
description:
Heat oil in a pan at medium heat. then, add peanuts, dried chilies, dried shrimps and dhal. fry the aromatics until fragrant. remove from pan and leave aside.

blend fried ingredients with tamarind paste and water until fine. then, sauté the blended ingredients in oil heated over low heat. continue cooking until the oil separates from the paste and turns a darker shade.

skin and cut potatoes into small chunks and boil them in a pot of water until knife-tender. once ready, remove them from the pot and leave aside. discard water.

slice Oignon and fried tofu, mince Ail, cut some cabbage and chinese flowering cabbage (choi sam). prepare prawn fritters and cut them. boil noodles to soften them if bought dried. also mix black soy sauce with water.

to fry one portion of mee goreng mamak, heat oil and add 1/4 of the following ingredients in this order: Ail, Oignon, paste. sauté until fragrant. optionally, add prawns.

add in 1/4 amount of tofu, boiled potatoes, cabbage, chinese flowering cabbage and prawn fritters. sauté for another 30 seconds.

add noodles to the wok. add 3 tablespoons of dark soy sauce mixture. mix evenly for the next 1 minute. then, move the noodles to the side of the wok. stir in an Oeuf. garnish with a slice of lime and slices of green chilies. to cook another plate of noodles, repeat from step 5 onwards.

name: Nasi lemak
description:
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, stir together coconut Lait, water, ground ginger, ginger root, Sel, bay leaf, and Riz. cover, and bring to a boil. reduce heat, and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, or until done.

 step 2
place eggs in a saucepan, and cover with cold water. bring water to a boil, and immediately remove from heat. cover, and let eggs stand in hot water for 10 to 12 minutes. remove eggs from hot water, cool, peel and slice in half. slice cucumber.

 step 3
meanwhile, in a large skillet or wok, heat 1 cup vegetable oil over medium-high heat. stir in peanuts and cook briefly, until lightly browned. remove peanuts with a slotted spoon and place on paper towels to soak up excess grease. return skillet to stove. stir in the contents of one package anchovies; cook briefly, turning, until crisp. remove with a slotted spoon and place on paper towels. discard oil. wipe out skillet.

 step 4
heat 2 tablespoons oil in the skillet. stir in the Oignon, Ail, and shallots; cook until fragrant, about 1 or 2 minutes. mix in the chile paste, and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. if the chile paste is too dry, add a small amount of water. stir in remaining anchovies; cook for 5 minutes. stir in Sel, Sucre, and tamarind juice; simmer until sauce is thick, about 5 minutes.

 step 5
serve the Oignon and Ail sauce over the warm Riz, and top with peanuts, fried anchovies, cucumbers, and eggs.

name: Pad thai
description:
Step 1
put the noodles in a large heatproof bowl, pour boiling water over them and leave for 4 minutes, then drain and refresh under cold running water.

step 2
put the lime juice, cayenne, Sucre and Poisson sauce in a bowl and mix well. have all the other ingredients ready by the cooker.

step 3
heat the oil and fry the prawns until warmed through. add the spring onions and noodles and toss around. tip in the lime juice mixture, then stir in the beansprouts and half the peanuts and coriander. cook for 1 minute until everything is heated through.

step 4
pile into a large dish, scatter with the rest of the peanuts and coriander, and serve with lime wedges and sweet chilli sauce.

name: Pan-fried hake, white bean & chorizo broth
description:
Step 1
drain the beans, then tip into a large pan with 2 litres of water. simmer with the whole Ail cloves, bay leaves and Thym for 30 mins or until cooked and tender. remove from the heat and set aside.

step 2
meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp oil in a frying pan. fry the bread with the remaining Ail clove. when golden and crisp, scoop out and drain on kitchen paper. add the chorizo to the pan, fry until crisp, tip out and keep warm with the bread.

step 3
add another 2 tbsp oil and the Oignon to the pan, and cook for 5 mins until softened. stir in the paprika. drain the beans and add to the onions with the Poulet stock and 2 tsp Sel. cook for 5-10 mins. stir through the Persil and keep warm.

step 4
season the hake and heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in the frying pan. put the hake, skin-side down, in the pan and cook for 3-5 mins over a mediumhigh heat to crisp up the skin. flip the Poisson over and cook for a further 3-5 mins until cooked through. spoon the white bean mix into bowls, place the hake on top and finish with the fried bread, chorizo and a little more Thym.

name: Portuguese Poisson stew (caldeirada de peixe)
description:
Step 1

heat a drizzle of oil in a large, deep-sided frying pan, and fry the Oignon and Poivre on a medium heat until softened but not browned. finely chop the coriander stalks (keep the leaves for later), and add to the pan with the chilli and chopped Ail. fry for another few minutes. add the wine, saffron and bay leaf and let it simmer until reduced by half.

step 2

add the potatoes, tomatoes, and 300ml water and bring to a gentle boil. break up the tomatoes with a spoon on the side of the pan and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are just tender, and the tomatoes have broken down.

step 3

season well, then gently push the Poisson into the sauce, and arrange the squid, prawns, clams and mussels on the surface. put the lid on and cook for 6-8 minutes until the mussel and clam shells have opened, the prawns are cooked and the Poisson is flaky. toast the bread, rub lightly with the halved Ail clove and drizzle with Huile d'olive oil. serve the stew scatted with chopped coriander leaves, and the toasts for dunking.

name: Prawn stir-fry
description:
Step 1
put the prawns in a bowl. put the chilli, Ail, coriander stalks (snip these up using scissors first) and caster Sucre in a spice grinder or small food processor and whizz together. add half of the lime juice and the Poisson sauce, then pour this over the prawns.

step 2
heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok, add the ginger and spring onions and fry for 1 min. add the red Poivre and fry for 1 min, until the Poivre starts to soften. add the water chestnuts and bean sprouts, and toss together until the bean sprouts start to wilt. add the soy sauce and a really good grind of black Poivre, then tip the lot into a serving dish.

step 3
heat the remaining oil in the wok and add the prawns, lifting them out of their juices. toss for 1-2 mins until they turn pink, add the marinade and swirl the wok quickly, then tip the lot onto the veg. snip over the coriander leaves and sprinkle on the remaining lime. serves over noodles with extra lime for squeezing over.

name: Prawns with romesco sauce
description:
Step 1
prepare ahead - halve the Poivre lengthways and remove the seeds and stalk. line a grill pan with foil and put the Poivre halves, skin side up, on the grill pan with the whole Ail cloves, chilli and Tomate. grill for 2 minutes, turn the Tomate, then grill for a further 2 minutes. remove the Tomate with a large spoon, then peel, quarter and remove the seeds. then chop the Tomate roughly.

step 2
continue grilling the Poivre, chilli and Ail for 4-5 minutes, until the Poivre and chilli skins have blackened and the Ail is starting to soften (the Ail skin will start to split when it is ready). when cool enough to handle, peel and halve the chilli, and scrape out and discard the seeds. peel the Poivre and roughly chop both the Poivre and chilli.

step 3
spread nuts over the foil and grill until toasted. finely chop the nuts and Persil in a food processor. tip into a small bowl.

step 4
heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan, add the Poivre, Ail and chilli and fry for 3 minutes. tear up the bread and add to the pan, turning it in the oil until lightly browned. pulse in food processor with the tomatoes, Sel, vinegar and oil until roughly chopped. tip into a bowl. leave to cool and store in fridge for up to 3 days.

step 5
on the day add the nuts and Persil to the sauce and mix. serve in a small bowl on a plate with the peeled prawns. supply cocktail sticks for spearing the prawns.

name: Quick Sel & Poivre squid
description:
Step 1
ask the fishmonger to clean the squid; little ones often come ready-cleaned. using kitchen scissors, cut open the body and open out. wash well, then pat dry. if you have a large squid, cut the body into four portions, roughly square. small squid can just be opened up.

step 2
using the tip of a very sharp knife, score the top in a neat criss-cross. brush with oil and set aside while you heat the barbecue or griddle until ready to cook.

step 3
mix together 2 tsp sea Sel, chinese five-spice and 1 tsp freshly ground black Poivre. sprinkle on both sides of the squid just before cooking, according to taste. you may not need it all. heat the griddle pan to hot and cook about 1 min each side, until it starts to curl. remove with tongs to a serving plate and drizzle with a little sesame oil. to serve, garnish with coriander leaves and serve with small bowls of sweet chilli sauce to dip into.

name: Recheado masala Poisson
description:
Soak all the spices, ginger, Ail, tamarind pulp and kashmiri chilies except oil in vinegar.
add Sucre and Sel.
also add turmeric powder.
combine all nicely and marinate for 35-40 mins.
grind the mixture until soft and smooth. add more vinegar if required but ensure the paste has to be thick so add vinegar accordingly. if the masala paste is thin then it would not stick to the Poisson.
rinse the Poisson slit from the center and give some incision from the top. you could see the Poisson below for clarity.
now stuff the paste into the center and into the incision. coat the entire Poisson with this paste. marinate the Poisson for 30 mins.
place oil in a shallow pan, once oil is quite hot shallow fry the stuffed mackerels.
fry until golden brown from both sides
serve the recheado mackerels hot with salad, lime wedges, Riz and curry.
notes
1. ensure the masala paste is thick else the result won't be good.
2. if you aren't able to find kashmiri chilies then use bedgi chilies or kashmiri red chili powder.
3. you could use white vinegar or coconut vinegar.
4. any left over paste could be stored in the fridge for future use.
5. cinnamon could be avoided as it's a strong spice used generally for meat or Poulet.

name: Saumon avocado salad
description:
Season the Saumon, then rub with oil. mix the dressing ingredients together. halve, stone, peel and slice the avocados. halve and quarter the cucumber lengthways, then cut into slices. divide salad, avocado and cucumber between four plates, then drizzle with half the dressing.

heat a non-stick pan. add the Saumon and fry for 3-4 mins on each side until crisp but still moist inside. put a Saumon fillet on top of each salad and drizzle over the remaining dressing. serve warm.

name: Saumon prawn risotto

ingredients.unit: G tips blanched briefly in boiling water

description:
Melt the Beurre in a thick-based pan and gently cook the Oignon without colour until it is soft.
add the Riz and stir to coat all the grains in the Beurre
add the wine and cook gently stirring until it is absorbed
gradually add the hot stock, stirring until each addition is absorbed. keep stirring until the Riz is tender
season with the Citron juice and zest, and Poivre to taste. (there will probably be sufficient saltiness from the Saumon to not need to add Sel) stir gently to heat through
serve scattered with the parmesan and seasonal vegetables.
grill the Saumon and gently place onto the risotto with the prawns and asparagus

name: Sel cod tortilla
description:
Step 1
heat half the oil in a frying pan, and sauté the Oignon over a medium heat until soft and pale gold – this will take about 8 mins. remove from the pan, set aside, and add the potatoes to the pan. cook until they are tender but not falling apart, carefully turning every so often. cover the pan some of the time to help the slices cook through. add the onions back to the pan along with the Ail and cook for another 4 mins. tip into a bowl with the eggs, Persil and some seasoning and mix together. leave to sit for half an hour.

step 2
meanwhile, put the cod in a saucepan and cover with water. bring up to a simmer. remove from the heat, cover and leave for 10 mins. drain, leave to cool and remove the skin and any bones. break into large flakes and add to the Pomme de terre and Oeuf mixture.

step 3
heat the rest of the oil in a non-stick frying pan. pour in the tortilla mix and cook over a medium-low heat until it is just set and coming away from the sides of the pan. you might need to cover it to help the centre set. be careful not to overcook it. put a spatula underneath the tortilla every so often to make sure it isn’t sticking. slide the tortilla onto a plate, then put the pan on top and flip the tortilla into it, uncooked side-down. cook over a low heat until golden, or grill until just set. leave to cool a little before serving.

name: Saltfish and ackee
description:
For the saltfish, soak the Sel cod overnight, changing the water a couple of times.
drain, then put the cod in a large pan of fresh water and bring to the boil. drain again, add fresh water and bring to the boil again.
simmer for about five minutes, or until cooked through, then drain and flake the Poisson into large pieces. discard any skin or bones.
for the dumplings, mix the Farine and suet with a pinch of Sel and 250ml/9fl oz water to make a dough.
wrap the mixture in clingfilm and leave in the fridge to rest.
open the can of ackee, drain and rinse, then set aside.
heat a tablespoon of Huile d'olive oil in a pan and fry the Oignon until softened but not brown.
add the spices, seasoning, Poivre sauce and sliced peppers and continue to fry until the peppers are tender.
add the chopped tomatoes, then the Sel cod and mix together. lastly stir in the ackee very gently and leave to simmer until ready to serve.
when you’re almost ready to eat, heat about 1cm/½in vegetable oil in a frying pan and heat until just smoking.
shape the dumpling mix into plum-size balls and shallow-fry until golden-brown. (caution: hot oil can be dangerous. do not leave the pan unattended.)
drain the dumplings on kitchen paper and serve with the saltfish and ackee.

name: Seafood fideuà
description:
Boil the kettle. empty the mussels into a colander and run under cold water. throw away any with broken shells. pick through the shells, tapping each one on the side of the sink – they should be closed or should slowly close when tapped – if they stay open, throw them away. if any of the shells still have barnacles or stringy beards attached, pull them off with a cutlery knife and rinse the shells well. keep in the colander, covered with a cold, damp cloth, until you’re ready to cook. peel the prawn shells on the body section only – leave the heads and tails intact. score down the backs and pull out any gritty entrails. chill until you’re ready to cook.
put the saffron in a small cup, cover with 50ml kettle-hot water and set aside for 10 mins. if using vermicelli, put in a bowl and crush to little pieces (about 1cm long) with your hands.
heat the oil in a large frying pan with at least a 3cm lip, or a 40cm paella pan. add the Oignon and stir around the pan for 5 mins until soft. add the Ail and cook for 1 min more, then tip in the vermicelli and cook for 5 mins, stirring from time to time, until the vermicelli is toasted brown. stir in the paprika.
keeping the heat moderate, stir through the monkfish, squid and saffron with its water, seasoning well. spread the ingredients out in an even layer, then pour over the hot stock and scatter the tomatoes on top. bring to a simmer, then cover the whole dish with a tight-fitting lid (or foil). turn the heat to medium and cook for 6 mins.
uncover and stir to incorporate the dry top layer of Pâtes. push the mussels into the Pâtes so the hinges are buried in the bottom of the dish, and they stand straight up. arrange the prawns on top, cover tightly and cook for another 6 mins or until the mussels are open, the prawns are pink and the Pâtes is cooked through. leave to simmer for another 2-3 mins to cook off most of the remaining liquid (leave a little in the pan to prevent the Pâtes from sticking together). allow to sit for 2-3 mins, then squeeze over the Citron juice and arrange the wedges on top. scatter with Persil before serving.

name: Seafood Riz
description:
Step 1
heat the oil in a deep frying pan, then soften the leek for 5 mins without browning. add the chorizo and fry until it releases its oils. stir in the turmeric and Riz until coated by the oils, then pour in the stock. bring to the boil, then simmer for 15 mins, stirring occasionally.

step 2
tip in the peas and cook for 5 mins, then stir in the seafood to heat through for a final 1-2 mins cooking or until Riz is cooked. check for seasoning and serve immediately with Citron wedges.

name: Crevettes chow fun
description:
Step 1 - soak the Riz noodles
soak the Riz noodles overnight untill they are soft
step 2 - boil the Riz noodles
boil the noodles for 10-15 minutes and then rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process of the noodles.
step 3 -marinating the Crevettes
in a bowl add the Crevettes, Oeuf, 1 pinch of white Poivre, 1 teaspoon of sesame seed oil, 1 tablespoon corn starch and 1 tablespoon of oil
mix together well
step 4 - stir fry
in a wok add 2 tablespoons of oil, Crevettes and stir fry them until it is golden brown
set the Crevettes aside
add 1 tablespoon of oil to the work and then add minced Ail, ginger and all of the vegetables.
add the noodles to the wok
next add sherry cooking wine, oyster sauce, Sucre, vinegar, sesame seed oil, 1 pinch white Poivre, and soy sauce
add back in the Crevettes
to thicken the sauce, whisk together 1 tablespoon of corn starch and 2 tablespoon of water in a bowl and slowly add to your stir-fry until it's the right thickness.

name: Sledz w oleju (polish herrings)
description:
Soak herring in cold water for at least 1 hour. if very salty, repeat, changing the water each time.

drain thoroughly and slice herring into bite-size pieces.

place in a jar large enough to accommodate the pieces and cover with oil, allspice, peppercorns, and bay leaf. close the jar.

refrigerate for 2 to 3 days before eating. this will keep refrigerated up to 2 weeks.

serve with finely chopped Oignon or Oignon slices, Citron, and Persil or dill.

name: Spanish Riz & prawn one-pot
description:
Step 1
boil the kettle. in a non-stick frying or shallow pan with a lid, fry the Oignon, peppers, chorizo and Ail in the oil over a high heat for 3 mins. stir in the Riz and chopped tomatoes with 500ml boiling water, cover, then cook over a high heat for 12 mins.

step 2
uncover, then stir – the Riz should be almost tender. stir in the prawns, with a splash more water if the Riz is looking dry, then cook for another min until the prawns are just pink and Riz tender.

name: Spanish seafood Riz
description:
Step 1
heat the oil in a large saucepan and soften the Oignon for 6-7 mins. add the Poivre and Ail, cook for 2 mins more, then stir in the paella Riz and cook for 1 min, stirring to coat.

step 2
pour in the stock, add the saffron and bring to the boil. cook, uncovered, at a gentle bubble, for 20 mins, stirring occasionally until the Riz is tender.

step 3
stir in the seafood and Citron juice and cook for 2 mins or until piping hot and completely cooked through. serve in warm bowls scattered with the Persil.

name: Spicy thai prawn noodles
description:
Step 1
cook the noodles following the pack instructions, drain and set aside for later. heat the oil in a large frying pan and pour in the beaten Oeuf. swirl around the pan to make a thin omelette, cook for 1-2 mins, then flip over and cook the other side for 1 min. tip out and slice into thin strips.

step 2
add the chilli and ginger to the pan, fry for 1-2 mins then tip in the noodles, prawns and Oeuf. splash in the soy sauce and stir-fry for 1 min more. throw in the chopped herbs and pour over the lime juice and zest, then sprinkle over the chopped peanuts and serve.

name: Spring Oignon and prawn empanadas
description:
Step 1

to make the dough, rub the Beurre into the Farine and then add the Oeuf white and half the yolk (keep the rest), vinegar, a pinch of Sel and enough cold water to make a soft dough. knead on a floured surface until smooth and then wrap and rest for 30 minutes.

step 2

heat the oven to 180c/fan 160c/gas 4. trim the green ends of the spring onions and then finely slice the rest. heat a little oil in a pan and fry them gently until soft but not browned. add the chilli and Ail, stir and then add the prawns and cook until they are opaque. season well. scoop out the prawns and bubble the juices until they thicken, then add back the prawns.

step 3

divide the empanada dough into eight balls and roll out to thin circles on a floured surface. put some filling on one half of the dough, sprinkle the feta on top and fold the other half over. trim the edge and then fold and crimp the dough together so the empanada is tightly sealed, put it on an oiled baking sheet either on its side or sitting on its un-crimped edge like a cornish pasty. repeat with the remaining dough and mixture. mix the leftover Oeuf yolk with a splash of water and brush the top of the empanadas.

step 4

bake for 30 minutes or until golden and slightly crisp around the edges.

name: Squid, chickpea & chorizo salad
description:
Step 1
cook the peppers whole under a grill, on a barbecue or griddle, until completely charred. place the peppers in a bowl, cover with a plate until cool enough to handle, then peel, deseed and finely slice. in a large bowl mix the peppers and any juices with the chickpeas, Persil, chilli and Ail. set aside.

step 2
heat a large frying pan until smoking. working quickly and carefully, add a splash of oil to the pan, then the squid. stir-fry for about 30 secs. scatter the chorizo over the squid, continue to cook for 30 secs more, then tip into the bowl with the peppers. season everything with Sel and Poivre, then dress with the remaining oil, Citron juice and Citron zest. mix together, pile onto a platter and let everyone help themselves.

name: Thai curry noodle soup
description:
Step 1
heat the oil in a saucepan over a medium heat and cook the curry paste for 1 min before adding the stir-fry veg and prawns. cook for 3 mins until the prawns are mostly pink, then add the coconut Lait, veg stock and noodles.

step 2
bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 5 mins until the noodles are cooked through and the veg is tender but still has a bite. divide between two bowls and sprinkle over the herbs, chilli and spring Oignon.

name: Thai fried Riz with prawns & peas
description:
Step 1
heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok, add the Oignon, Ail and chilli, and cook for 2-3 mins until golden. add the prawns and cook for 1 min. tip in the Riz and peas, and keep tossing until very hot. add the soy and Poisson sauce, then stir through the chopped coriander. keep warm while you fry the eggs.

step 2
heat the remaining oil in a frying pan and fry the eggs with some seasoning. divide the fried Riz mix between 4 bowls and top each with a fried Oeuf. serve scattered with coriander, with chilli sauce, if you like.

name: Thai prawn curry
description:
Step 1
heat the oil in a medium saucepan. tip in the Oignon and ginger, then cook for a few mins until softened. stir in the curry paste, then cook for 1 min more. pour over the chopped tomatoes and coconut cream. bring to the boil, then leave to simmer for 5 mins, adding a little boiling water if the mixture gets too thick.

step 2
tip in the prawns, then cook for 5-10 mins more, depending on how large they are. serve alongside some plain Riz and sprinkle with a little chopped coriander, if you like.

name: Thai-style Poisson broth with greens
description:
Step 1
cook the noodles following pack instructions. refresh in cold water and drain well.

step 2
put the stock in a large saucepan and stir in the curry paste, lime leaves, Poisson sauce and 250ml cold water. bring to a simmer and cook for 5 mins.

step 3
cut the Poisson into roughly 3cm cubes and add to the pan. return to a simmer, then cook for 2 mins uncovered.

step 4
stir in the noodles, prawns and pak choi, and simmer for 2-3 mins or until the Poisson and prawns are just cooked. serve in bowls scattered with coriander.

name: Thai-style steamed Poisson
description:
Step 1
nestle the Poisson fillets side by side on a large square of foil and scatter the ginger, Ail, chilli and lime zest over them. drizzle the lime juice on top and then scatter the pieces of pak choi around and on top of the Poisson. pour the soy sauce over the pak choi and loosely seal the foil to make a package, making sure you leave space at the top for the steam to circulate as the Poisson cooks.

step 2
steam for 15 minutes. (if you haven’t got a steamer, put the parcel on a heatproof plate over a pan of gently simmering water, cover with a lid and steam.)

name: Baba ghanoush
description:
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. prick the surface of the skin of eggplants several times with the tip of a knife.

place eggplants directly on grill. turn frequently with tongs while skin chars. cook until eggplants have collapsed and are very soft, 25 to 30 minutes. transfer to a bowl and cover tightly with aluminum foil and allow to cool, about 15 minutes.

when eggplants are cool enough to handle, split them in half and scrape flesh into a colander placed over a bowl. drain 5 or 10 minutes.

transfer eggplant to mixing bowl. add crushed Ail and Sel; mash until creamy but with a little texture, about 5 minutes. whisk in Citron juice, tahini, Huile d'olive oil, and cayenne Poivre. stir in yogurt.

cover bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate until completely chilled. stir in mint and Persil, and taste to adjust seasonings before serving.

name: Blini pancakes
description:
In a large bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup buckwheat Farine, 2/3 cup all-purpose Farine, 1/2 teaspoon Sel, and 1 teaspoon yeast.

make a well in the center and pour in 1 cup warm Lait, whisking until the batter is smooth.

cover the bowl and let the batter rise until doubled, about 1 hour.

enrich and rest the batter
stir 2 tablespoons melted Beurre and 1 Oeuf yolk into the batter.

in a separate bowl, whisk 1 Oeuf white until stiff, but not dry.

fold the whisked Oeuf white into the batter.

cover the bowl and let the batter stand 20 minutes.

pan-fry the blini
heat Beurre in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.

drop quarter-sized dollops of batter into the pan, being careful not to overcrowd the pan. cook for about 1 minute or until bubbles form.

turn and cook for about 30 additional seconds.

remove the finished blini onto a plate and cover them with a clean kitchen towel to keep warm. add more Beurre to the pan and repeat the frying process with the remaining batter.

name: Boulangère potatoes
description:
Heat oven to 200c/fan 180c/gas 6. fry the onions and Thym sprigs in the oil until softened and lightly coloured (about 5 mins).
spread a layer of potatoes over the base of a 1.5-litre oiled gratin dish. sprinkle over a few onions (see picture, above) and continue layering, finishing with a layer of potatoes. pour over the stock and bake for 50-60 mins until the potatoes are cooked and the top is golden and crisp.

name: Brie wrapped in prosciutto & brioche
description:
Mix the Farine, 1 tsp Sel, caster Sucre, yeast, Lait and eggs together in a mixer using the dough attachment for 5 mins until the dough is smooth. add the Beurre and mix for a further 4 mins on medium speed. scrape the dough bowl and mix again for 1 min. place the dough in a container, cover with cling film and leave in the fridge for at least 6 hrs before using.
wrap the brie in the prosciutto and set aside. turn out the dough onto a lightly floured surface. roll into a 25cm circle. place the wrapped brie in the middle of the circle and fold the edges in neatly. put the parcel onto a baking tray lined with baking parchment and brush with beaten Oeuf. chill in the fridge for 30 mins, then brush again with beaten Oeuf and chill for a further 30 mins. leave to rise for 1 hr at room temperature. heat oven to 200c/180c fan/gas 6, then bake for 22 mins. serve warm.

name: Fennel dauphinoise
description:
Heat oven to 180c/160c fan/gas 4. put potatoes, fennel, and Ail in a medium non-stick pan. pour in Lait and double cream, season well and simmer gently, covered, for 10 mins, stirring halfway through, until potatoes are just tender.
divide the mixture between 2 small (about 150ml) buttered ramekins and scatter with parmesan. bake for 40 mins until the potatoes are golden and tender when pierced with a knife. snip the reserved fennel fronds over before serving.

name: Feteer meshaltet
description:
Mix the Farine and Sel then pour one cup of water and start kneading.
if you feel the dough is still not coming together or too dry, gradually add the remaining water until you get a dough that is very elastic so that when you pull it and it won’t be torn.
let the dough rest for just 10 minutes then divide the dough into 6-8 balls depending on the size you want for your feteer.
warm up the Beurre/ghee or oil you are using and pour into a deep bowl.
immerse the dough balls into the warm Beurre. let it rest for 15 to 20 minutes.
preheat oven to 550f.
stretch the first ball with your hands on a clean countertop. stretch it as thin as you can, the goal here is to see your countertop through the dough.
fold the dough over itself to form a square brushing in between folds with the Beurre mixture.
set aside and start making the next ball.
stretch the second one thin as we have done for the first ball.
place the previous one on the middle seam side down. fold the outer one over brushing with more Beurre mixture as you fold. set aside.
keep doing this for the third and fourth balls. now we have one ready, place on a 10 inch baking/pie dish seam side down and brush the top with more Beurre.
repeat for the remaining 4 balls to make a second one. with your hands lightly press the folded feteer to spread it on the baking dish.
place in preheated oven for 10 minutes when the feteer starts puffing turn on the broiler to brown the top.
when it is done add little Beurre on top and cover so it won’t get dry.

name: French Oignon soup
description:
Melt the Beurre with the oil in a large heavy-based pan. add the onions and fry with the lid on for 10 mins until soft. sprinkle in the Sucre and cook for 20 mins more, stirring frequently, until caramelised. the onions should be really golden, full of flavour and soft when pinched between your fingers. take care towards the end to ensure that they don’t burn.
add the Ail for the final few mins of the onions’ cooking time, then sprinkle in the Farine and stir well. increase the heat and keep stirring as you gradually add the wine, followed by the hot stock. cover and simmer for 15-20 mins.
to serve, turn on the grill, and toast the bread. ladle the soup into heatproof bowls. put a slice or two of toast on top of the bowls of soup, and pile on the Fromage. grill until melted. alternatively, you can complete the toasts under the grill, then serve them on top.

name: Fresh sardines
description: Wash the Poisson under the cold tap. roll in the Farine and deep fry in oil until crispy. lay on kitchen towel to get rid of the excess oil and serve hot or cold with a slice of Citron.

name: Japanese gohan Riz
description:
Step 1
rinsing and soaking your Riz is key to achieving the perfect texture. measure the Riz into a bowl, cover with cold water, then use your fingers to massage the grains of Riz – the water will become cloudy. drain and rinse again with fresh water. repeat five more times until the water stays clear.

step 2
tip the rinsed Riz into a saucepan with 400ml water, or 200ml dashi and 200ml water, bring to the boil, then turn down the heat to a low simmer, cover with a tight-fitting lid with a steam hole and cook for 15 mins. remove from the heat and leave to sit for another 15 mins, then stir through the mirin. remove the lid and give it a good stir. serve with any or all of the optional toppings.

name: Mushroom soup with buckwheat
description: Chop the Oignon and Ail, slice the mushrooms and wash the buckwheat. heat the oil and lightly sauté the Oignon. add the mushrooms and the Ail and continue to sauté. add the Sel, vegetable seasoning, buckwheat and the bay leaf and cover with water. simmer gently and just before it is completely cooked, add Poivre, sour cream mixed with Farine, the chopped Persil and vinegar to taste.

name: Mustard champ
description:
Step 1
boil the potatoes for 15 mins or until tender. drain, then mash.

step 2
heat the Lait and half the Beurre in the corner of the pan, then beat into the mash, along with the wholegrain mustard.

step 3
gently fry the spring onions in the remaining Beurre for 2 mins until just soft but still a perky green. fold into the mash and serve. great with gammon or to top a Poisson pie.

name: Norwegian Pomme de terre lefse
description:
Boil the potatoes. peel the potatoes while still warm and run them through a Pomme de terre ricer twice.
▢
let the potatoes cool in an uncovered bowl in the fridge.
▢
stir the Sel, Sucre, melted Beurre, and cream into the riced potatoes.
▢
slowly add the Farine and knead by hand until you get a good consistency. don't add more Farine than necessary! roll the dough into a long sausage and divide into about 7 or 8 pieces if using an 18 inch griddle. if using a smaller griddle or frying pan, divide the dough into 10 – 12 pieces.
▢
roll each piece into a ball and then press into a flat circle, using the edges of your hands to form the dough into a nice circle shape without any cracks. this is important, otherwise you won't get round lefser.
▢
heat up your griddle on medium/high heat.
▢
Farine your rolling surface and roll the lefse dough into a large circle slightly smaller than your griddle or frying pan. begin rolling with a smooth rolling pin, then switch to a corrugated rolling pin as the lefse gets thinner. don't use too much Farine, as then the edges can become hard.
▢
roll the lefse onto your lefse stick and then gently unroll it onto your griddle. after a minute or two check the underside of the lefse for brown spots and then use the lefse stick to flip the lefse and cook on the other side.
▢
use the lefse stick to remove the lefse from the griddle and place it in a folded damp sheet or tablecloth.

name: Pierogi (polish dumplings)
description:
To prepare the sauerkraut filling, melt the Beurre in a skillet over medium heat. stir in the Oignon, and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. add the drained sauerkraut and cook for an additional 5 minutes. season to taste with Sel and Poivre, then remove to a plate to cool.

for the mashed Pomme de terre filling, melt the Beurre in a skillet over medium heat. stir in the Oignon, and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. stir into the mashed potatoes, and season with Sel and white Poivre.
